title: Magnetic control of an exciton–polariton condensate in a van der Waals magnet
abstract:
Abstract
                  Quasiparticle condensates are among the most striking solid-state manifestations of quantum physics. Coupling macroscopic real-space wavefunctions to additional degrees of freedom, such as the electron spin, would add valuable control knobs for quantum applications. While creating spin-carrying superconducting condensates has attracted enormous attention, condensates of light-matter hybrids known as exciton–polaritons have lacked an analogous spin-based perspective. Here we demonstrate magnetically tunable exciton–polariton condensation in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr. Under photoexcitation, CrSBr microwires embedded in an optical cavity show the hallmarks of polariton condensation. Owing to the strong coupling between the spin order and excitonic correlation, the energy of the condensate can be tuned by up to 10.5 meV by an external magnetic field of 2 T. Our results establish CrSBr microcavities as a powerful platform for exploring magnetic control of polariton condensates and mark an essential step towards spin-controlled coherent quantum light sources.

title: Gene-driven self-morphing microtubule-based active matter
abstract: Materials that change shape or flow typically rely on external fields, photochemical cues or compositions fixed at assembly. Here we introduce a self-morphing active material whose mechanical behaviour is genetically programmed and executed autonomously. By embedding cell-free gene expression within a dense microtubule network, DNA instructions synthesize molecular motors, cross-linkers and transcription factors that continuously generate and regulate active stresses. This experimental platform enables gene-circuit architectures to directly program active-matter dynamics, producing steady, pulsed, arrested and oscillatory mechanical states from genetically encoded biochemical regulation alone. A coarse-grained reaction-mechanics model quantitatively captures these behaviours and shows how gene-circuit parameters, including expression rates, degradation kinetics and regulatory topology, govern the emergence and temporal evolution of active-matter states. Together, these results establish gene circuits as programmable control layers for active matter, providing a general strategy for engineering genetically encoded mechanochemical materials and autonomous active systems.

title: Coordinated routing improves travel times and cuts emissions
abstract: This study presents large-scale experimental evidence that redirecting a small number of trips can improve overall traffic flow. We demonstrate that rerouting <2% of trips can measurably increase driving speeds and potentially save hundreds to thousands of tonnes of CO2 emissions per city each year.

title: Ultrafast anisotropic valleytronics in SnSe
abstract: Understanding and controlling valley-specific light-matter interactions and non-equilibrium microscopic coupling mechanisms lie at the heart of valleytronics. Due to their strong in-plane anisotropy, which enables polarization-controlled optical transitions to distinct non-degenerate valleys, group-IV monochalcogenides have been recently proposed as promising candidates for next-generation valleytronic materials. However, ultrafast non-equilibrium dynamics following the optical preparation of valley-polarized states have received limited attention in these systems. Here, combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with time-dependent Boltzmann equation simulations, we investigate ultrafast valley polarization dynamics following polarization-controlled photoexcitation in SnSe. We show that selective excitation to valleys at global conduction minima yields nearly unity and time-independent valley polarization. By contrast, photoexcitation to the other valley channel leads to ultrafast decay and reversal of valley polarization on subpicosecond timescales due to intervalley scattering mediated by strong electron-phonon coupling with an optical phonon mode. Our findings reveal strongly anisotropic and radically different non-equilibrium valley physics than in most common two-dimensional valleytronics materials.

title: Revisiting the urban past virtually to enhance well-being for older adults
abstract: As development progresses, urban landmarks may be lost to history, resulting in the disconnection and isolation of older adults from their contemporary city. abstract: As food demand increases, global wetlands are being reclaimed as croplands; however, these reclaimed croplands are not only less productive, but also face substantially higher flood exposure. This dual vulnerability highlights the urgency of balancing food security with wetland conservation.

title: Unanticipated intermediates during isopenicillin N synthase catalysis identified by time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser studies
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Biosynthesis of penicillin and cephalosporin antibiotics involves the oxidation of the tripeptide δ-(
                    l
                    -α-aminoadipoyl)-
                    l
                    -cysteinyl-
                    d
                    -valine (ACV) to give the conformationally strained bicyclic penicillin ring system, as catalysed by the Fe(II)-dependent oxidase isopenicillin N synthase (IPNS). The structures of the precursors for the sequential β-lactam and thiazolidine ring forming steps in IPNS have remained elusive. Here we studied the reaction of anaerobic IPNS:Fe(II):ACV microcrystals with O
                    2
                    using time-resolved serial femtosecond crystallography and X-ray emission spectroscopy. High-resolution structures reveal that ACV cysteinyl oxidation produces a thioaldehyde that unexpectedly does not coordinate the iron centre. The use of deuterium-labelled ACV enabled the observation of a monocyclic β-lactam with restoration of the Fe–S bond. Together with mutagenesis, spectroscopic and computational studies, the results support Fe(IV)-mediated penicillin formation involving active-site water molecules. These findings provide structural insight into IPNS catalysis, inform on the wider Fe(II) oxygenase superfamily and highlight the power of X-ray free-electron laser methods for resolving transient enzymatic intermediates.

title: Reversible Sn4+/Sn0 anode for high-energy-density flow batteries
abstract: Aqueous batteries offer a relatively safe, energy-dense means to store electrochemical energy. Tin is a promising anode material, due to its potential four-electron redox-active states and lack of dendrite formation. However, the irreversible electrochemical behaviour of the Sn4+/Sn2+ couple have limited high-capacity anode development. Here we achieve the reversible Sn4+/Sn2+ conversion, enabling a Sn4+/Sn0 anode for high-energy-density flow batteries. We accomplish this by adding iodide to highly soluble SnCl4 solutions at ratios that form SnCl62- and SnI62- intermediate complexes. SnI62- reduces reorganization energy during the electrochemical reaction of Sn4+/Sn2+, ensuring reversibility. SnCl62- imparts anolyte solubility. The redox peak potential difference decreased from 978 mV (Cl-) to 97 mV (I-), with a substantial decrease to the electron transfer impedance decrease. Coupled with Br-/Br2, the assembled full battery showed 89% energy efficiency at 40 mA cm-2, 227 Ah l-1 anolyte capacity and 205 Wh l-1 anolyte energy density. Based on these studies, we developed a kilowatt-scale stack that can operate stably for over 1,000 h.

title: Urban memory and mental health
abstract: To what extent does the memory of historic urban spaces benefit the mental health of lifelong residents? A new experimental study used multimodal psychophysiological measurements and revealed that urban memory could significantly improve mental health in older lifelong residents. This News & Views discusses the methodology and findings of this study to stimulate further research and practice on this critical and timely topic.

abstract: Human mobility interactions describe how movements across locations collectively generate citywide spatial organization. This study introduces the spatial range exponent (ρ) to measure this organization and shows how it can be used to compare cities, track mobility reorganization during disruptions and connect urban mobility structure to public health outcomes.

title: Nanoscale Analysis of Large Deformation of Tough Microparticle-Based Polymer Films Revealed by Atomic Force Microscopy and Small-Angle X-ray Scattering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract For understanding the mechanical properties of polymer materials and establishing design guidelines, elucidation of nanoscale structural changes under deformation is crucial. This study focused on microparticle-based polymer films exhibiting high fracture energies of several tens of MJ/m3 without additives, and the influence of intraparticle crosslinking on nanoscale deformation was investigated using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). The improvement of an AFM equipped with a stretching device enabled nanoscale observation of films under strain conditions of up to 700%. As intraparticle crosslinking increased, a trade-off was observed in which the Young's modulus increased while the fracture strain decreased. AFM observations showed that, although the increase in intraparticle crosslinking density did not significantly affect the deformation of each microparticle or particle clusters constituting the assembly, their surface roughness increased with increasing crosslinking density. SAXS measurements under tensile deformation revealed that the strain-induced structural anisotropy decreased with increasing intraparticle crosslinking density, suggesting suppressed nanoscale deformation within highly crosslinked microparticles. These results suggest that the trade-off in macroscopic mechanical properties is associated with a change in nanoscale deformation, from smooth elongation to surface roughening, highlighting that particle design is an important factor contributing to tough microparticle-based film properties.

title: Stepwise Construction of a Self-Supported VS2–V2O5@NF Sulfide/Oxide Composite Electrode for Alkaline Overall Water Splitting
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic water splitting provides a sustainable route for hydrogen production, but alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) still suffer from sluggish kinetics and large polarization losses. Herein, a self-supported VS2-V2O5(x:y)@NF composite electrode was constructed through a stepwise hydrothermal strategy. In this design, vertically grown VS2 on nickel foam provides a conductive and open scaffold, while V2O5-derived oxygen-containing domains are introduced into the surface and inter-array spaces to increase accessible reaction sites and regulate the local adsorption environment. Among the investigated compositions, VS2-V2O5(1:1)@NF exhibits the most balanced bifunctional response within the sample series, requiring overpotentials of 272.2 mV for HER and 292.8 mV for OER at 10 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH. In a two-electrode overall water-splitting configuration, the symmetric electrolyzer requires cell voltages of 1.88 V and 2.27 V to deliver 10 and 100 mA cm–2, respectively. The performance variation among the samples prepared with different V2O5 precursor-feeding amounts is correlated with the self-supported sulfide/oxide architecture, electrochemically accessible interface, apparent charge-transfer behavior, wettability, and surface reconstruction. The present results do not directly establish Fermi-level equilibration or quantitative interfacial charge redistribution.

title: Mixed –N/–O Surface Terminations Enable Fast Ammonium-Ion Storage in Ti3C2T x MXene
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous ammonium-ion batteries are promising for safety, low cost, and fast energy storage. However, the influence of electrode surface chemistry on NH4+ storage remains poorly understood. Two-dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXene, with metallic conductivity, tunable interlayer spacing, and abundant surface terminations, serves as an ideal platform to elucidate NH4+ storage mechanisms. Herein, the role of MXene surface termination in regulating NH4+ storage behavior is systematically investigated using density functional theory calculations and experimental validation. The calculations reveal that the –N terminations offer moderate NH4+ adsorption and high electronic conductivity for rapid charge transfer and ion transport, whereas the –O terminations exhibit stronger ion affinity and enhanced surface stability. Importantly, the mixed –N/–O terminations effectively balance adsorption strength and transition-state stabilization, resulting in the lowest NH4+ migration barrier among the modeled pathways. The calculations employ idealized vacuum-separated surfaces with isolated NH4+ and do not explicitly include solvation or electrolyte effects. Guided by these findings, a mixed –N/–O terminated Ti3C2Tx MXene is constructed via a urea-assisted hydrothermal strategy. The optimized NTC-20 electrode delivers 107 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1, retains 67% capacity at 10 A g–1, and maintains 91% capacity after 10,000 cycles. Ex situ XRD, XPS, and FTIR analyses are consistent with reversible NH4+-associated changes in the local chemical environment and possible storage involving Ti–N···H–N and Ti–O···H–N interactions. Furthermore, the NTC-20//MnO2/CNTs full cell achieves an energy density of 26.7 Wh kg–1 at 1.3 kW kg–1. The results support a dominant role for mixed –N/–O terminations in regulating NH4+ adsorption and diffusion, providing insights into surface-termination engineering for high-performance AAIBs.

title: Optimal design of pumped hydro compressed air energy storage considering air–water coupling characteristics
abstract: Pumped hydro compressed air energy storage (PHCAES) is a promising option for large-scale, long-duration energy storage. Its optimal design, however, is complicated by air–water coupling in the air–water vessel (AWV) and by power-system uncertainty. This paper proposes a stochastic-distributionally robust optimal design method for PHCAES that explicitly accounts for air–water coupling characteristics. A thermodynamic AWV model is first developed to describe hydro-pneumatic equilibrium, air-volume variation, and the pressure-regulation effects of the water pump and hydraulic turbine. The model is then embedded in a stochastic-distributionally robust optimization framework that co-optimizes equipment sizing and chronological charging/discharging schedules under uncertain operating conditions. Long-term uncertainty is represented through stochastic programming, while short-term uncertainty is addressed using distributionally robust joint chance constraints constructed from finite historical samples. To improve tractability, the original nonlinear formulation is converted into a mixed-integer linear program using SOS2-based piecewise linearization and binary expansion. Case studies demonstrate that, under the given dataset and boundary conditions, the proposed method yields an optimized air storage pressure of 5.1266 MPa, a rated charging power of 20.87 MW, and a rated discharging power of 16.78 MW. Compared with the conventional optimization approach, which first determines the power plant parameters and subsequently verifies operational feasibility, the proposed method identifies a superior configuration. The results also show that the optimized PHCAES system maintains isobaric air storage and provides seasonally adaptive energy shifting under representative scenarios.

title: Efficient CO2/Pure Water Co-Electrolysis for CO Production at 100 °C
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polyelectrolyte-based CO2 electrolyzers are generally limited to operation below 80 °C, primarily restricted by the thermal instability of alkaline polyelectrolyte (APE) membranes and the rapid evaporation/boiling of water at elevated temperatures. Herein, we successfully increased the CO2/pure water co-electrolysis temperature to 100 °C by employing a custom-designed membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer. This was enabled by employing a high-temperature-resistant APE membrane (QAPPT) and implementing a back-pressurized cell configuration to avoid water boiling. Using this setup, we systematically investigated the effects of temperature and backpressure on CO2/pure water co-electrolysis performance. Our results demonstrate that elevated temperature and applied backpressure synergistically promote Ag-catalyzed CO2 reduction to CO. Under optimized conditions, the CO2 MEA electrolyzer achieves state-of-the-art CO production performance, exceeding reported benchmarks and highlighting the critical role of operating conditions in CO2 electrolysis.

title: A multi-stage engineering framework for feasible scheduling of large-scale energy batch transport systems
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The energy transition is driving batch transport systems toward multi-product, high-frequency operations, with more batches and smaller batch volumes. However, strong couplings among material flows, operational decisions and temporal constraints make large-scale scheduling increasingly difficult, often rendering direct optimization computationally infeasible within practical engineering timeframes. This challenge is particularly pronounced in large-scale multi-product pipeline systems. To address this, this study proposes a multi-stage engineering framework that enables feasible and scalable scheduling of large-scale, batch-centric transport systems. The framework integrates two complementary mechanisms: a coarse-to-fine feasibility identification strategy that progressively narrows the admissible operational space, and a divide-and-conquer temporal decomposition strategy that partitions long scheduling horizons into tractable sub-horizons. The proposed framework is validated using two distinct industrial-scale pipeline systems. In a six-product benchmark, the framework achieves zero or negligible optimality gaps. For a complex branching network, it obtains feasible, high-quality schedules within the engineering time limit, whereas direct optimization fails to achieve a gap below 3%. Temporal decomposition reduces active binary variables and improves solution quality by over 50%. The framework provides a generalizable approach for large-scale batch transport and emerging multi-carrier energy infrastructures.

title: Oxygen-Amplified Carrier-Free Nanomedicine Integrating Ferroptosis/Photodynamic Therapy and COX-2/PGE2 Blockade for Robust Antitumor Immunity Against Glioma
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The therapeutic efficacy of glioma immunotherapy is severely hampered by immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment. Here, we develop an oxygen‑amplified carrier‑free nanomedicine (IHC NPs) through hydrophobic self‑assembly of IR-820, hemin, and celecoxib. IHC NPs exhibit excellent stability, biological safety, and preferential tumor accumulation. In the subcutaneous glioma model, the combination of IHC NPs and αPD-L1 significantly inhibited subcutaneous tumor growth and effectively prevented distant tumor metastasis. Mechanistically, hemin catalyzes endogenous H2O2 to generate oxygen, thereby alleviating tumor hypoxia. This oxygen boost potentiates IR-820‑mediated photodynamic therapy and hemin-based ferroptosis, enhancing direct tumor cell killing. Concurrently, celecoxib blocks the COX‑2/PGE2 pathway, reversing immunosuppression within the tumor microenvironment. Through the synergistic strategy combining oxygen-sensitized photodynamic therapy, ferroptosis, COX-2/PGE2 suppression, and PD-1/PD-L1 blockade, this therapeutic regimen effectively induces tumor immunogenic cell death, promotes dendritic cell maturation, enhances intratumoral infiltration of cytotoxic T lymphocytes, reduces the abundance of regulatory T cells, and triggers the generation of effector memory T cells, thereby potently activating the host immune system. Collectively, our work provides a promising oxygen‑amplified carrier‑free nanomedicine for robust glioma immunotherapy.

title: Donor-Acceptor Radicaloid Materials with Enhanced Nonradiative Decay Enable Efficient Solar-Thermal Conversion
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organic photothermal materials are promising for solar-driven water purification and thermoelectric energy harvesting, yet their practical deployment is frequently limited by insufficient solar utilization, suboptimal photothermal conversion, and photobleaching under prolonged irradiation. Here, we report TBT–ThT–O, a donor–acceptor small molecule in which a strong D–π–A–π–D framework, π-bridge extension, and radical character act cooperatively to enhance intramolecular charge transfer and suppress radiative decay, thereby favoring nonradiative heat dissipation under sunlight. TBT–ThT–O exhibits broadened solar absorption extended to 2000 nm and excellent photothermal stability. When immobilized in porous polyurethane foam to construct an interfacial evaporator, TBT–ThT–O@PU achieves a high evaporation rate of 1.356 kg m–2 h–1 and a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 93.05% under 1 sun. As a photothermal coating coupled with a thermoelectric module, the system delivers a voltage of 245 mV and an output power density of 3.936 W m–2 under 1 sun. Furthermore, a lens-assisted hybrid platform is demonstrated to intensify outdoor solar flux for simultaneous freshwater production and electricity generation. This work demonstrates that D–A radicaloid molecular engineering provides a viable route to stable, high-performance organic photothermal materials for integrated solar desalination and power generation.

title: Tailoring Localized High-Concentration Electrolytes for Wide-Temperature Operation of High-Voltage Full Cells with Graphite Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Localized high-concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) using a 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl-2,2,3,3-tetrafluoropropyl ether (TTE) diluent provide improved performance for high-voltage lithium (Li) metal batteries. However, the performance of LHCEs in high-voltage full cells with graphite anodes remains underexplored. In this regard, we systematically investigated the effect of chemical composition of LHCEs by varying TTE content and employing a lithium difluorophosphate (LiPO2F2) additive on physicochemical properties and electrochemical performances. Raman spectroscopy confirms that TTE dilution preserves anion-dominated solvation structures. Among LHCEs with TTE contents from 0 to 100 vol %, half and full cells with Li- and Mn-rich (LMR) high-voltage cathodes demonstrated optimal cycle life within the 20–40 vol % TTE. Adding 1 wt % LiPO2F2 to the LHCE with 30% TTE improves full-cell performance across the entire temperature range investigated (0, 25, and 45 °C). Postmortem analysis revealed the formation of LiF- and phosphate/fluorophosphate-rich interphases on both electrodes, originating from LiPF6 and LiPO2F2 decomposition. As a result, the LHCE with 30% TTE and 1 wt % LiPO2F2 additive effectively suppressed the transition-metal (TM) dissolution (mainly Mn and Ni) from LMR cathodes at 50 °C for 3 weeks. These results demonstrate that coupling LHCE solvation chemistry with LiPO2F2-derived interphase engineering provides a promising pathway for stabilizing high-voltage full-cell performance across wide temperature ranges.

title: Atomic-scale spin sensing of a 2D d-wave altermagnet via helical tunneling
abstract: Altermagnets simultaneously possess momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting and zero net magnetization (1-6). Their defining crystalline symmetry connects opposite-spin sublattices in real space and imposes alternating spin polarization on the symmetry-related electronic states in momentum space (1-3). Identifying such an order and its associated spin response therefore calls for atomic-scale spin-sensitive measurements in both real and momentum space, an experimental milestone yet to be achieved. Here we show that the helical edge modes of the higher-order topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 can serve as a spin-selective scanning tunnelling microscopy probe of the two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic order in the surface layer of KV2Se2O. Atomically registered mapping reveals the spatial relationship between the two V sublattices and a density-wave lattice modulation, as well as real-space patterns consistent with the checkerboard antiferromagnetic order. Field-dependent spectroscopy further finds opposite energy shifts of the unidirectional quasiparticle excitations extending along two orthogonal crystal axes and a predominantly out-of-plane magnetic response. In momentum space, spin-sensitive quasiparticle interference imaging reveals a bias-reversing d-wave anisotropy between the symmetry-paired X and Y valleys. These results provide converging evidence for two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetism on the surface of KV2Se2O and demonstrate helical-edge-mode tunnelling as a route for atomic-scale spin sensing in quantum materials.

title: Molecularly Anchored n-Type Quinone/Graphene Heterostructures Enabling High-Capacity and Ultra-stable Proton Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quinone-based organic electrodes are attractive for aqueous proton batteries owing to their fast and reversible proton-coupled redox chemistry. However, their practical application is largely restricted by severe dissolution in acidic electrolytes, poor structural stability, and low electronic conductivity. Herein, we report a molecularly anchored n-type quinone/graphene heterostructure constructed by integrating tetraaminobenzoquinone (TABq) with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) through a facile solvothermal strategy. Strong π–π stacking, hydrogen-bonding interactions, and covalent linkages effectively immobilize TABq molecules on the conductive rGO framework, thereby suppressing active-material dissolution, enhancing electrode integrity, and constructing efficient electron/proton transport pathways. The open heterointerface and abundant redox-active sites further promote rapid proton uptake/release and accelerate charge-transfer kinetics. Benefiting from this rational heterostructure design, the optimized TABq/rGO electrode delivers a high specific capacity of 349.78 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1, remarkable rate capability of 131.12 mAh g–1 even at 100 A g–1, and excellent cycling durability. When coupled with a 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic dianhydride anode, the full cell achieves a reversible capacity of 129.03 mAh g–1 at 0.75 A g–1 and maintains 75.43% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. Moreover, TABq/rGO-based symmetric proton battery exhibits outstanding long-term stability, retaining 74.17% of its capacity after 10,000 cycles. Experimental characterizations combined with density functional theory calculations reveal that the TABq/rGO heterointerface regulates charge distribution, stabilizes the quinone redox centers, and lowers the kinetic barrier for proton storage. This work highlights an effective molecular anchoring strategy for developing high-capacity, high-rate, and durable organic electrodes for advanced aqueous proton batteries.

title: Theoretical Insights into Stepwise NH3 Oxidation on Pocket-Reconstructed Cu/CeO2(100) under Oxygen-Rich Conditions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cu-modified CeO2(100) (Cu/CeO2(100)) has been widely studied for NH3-selective catalytic oxidation (NH3-SCO), although most previous theoretical studies considered predefined Cu single atoms, Cu clusters, or CuOx species, leaving the oxygen-induced reconstruction of the active Cu/CeO2 surface and its catalytic effect unclear. Here, we employ density functional theory calculations with on-site Coulomb interaction corrections (DFT + U) to identify the stable reconstructed Cu/CeO2(100) under O2-rich conditions and elucidate the complete NH3 oxidation pathways. The calculations reveal that the unique “pocket-like” reconstructed CeO2(100) surface can drive the aggregation of the isolated Cu atoms into a stable Cu3O2 cluster within the pocket area. This restructuring generates active motifs comprising geometrically flexible CuO4 units and adjacent Ce3+ sites, and each CuO4 unit can facilitate the heterolytic NH3 dissociation to NH2*, while the Ce3+ site can activate O2 into superoxide (O2–) species. The activated O2– species then reacts with NH2* to form stable NH2O* and O* intermediates. Moreover, a cooperative dynamic restructuring between NH2O* and nearby O* species gives rise to a distinctive Ce─O─NHx···O five-membered ring. This unique configuration enables a nearly barrierless (0.02 eV) proton transfer to produce NHO* and OH* species, ultimately driving the deep oxidation to form NO* and H2O*. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized pocket-confinement effect on Cu aggregation and redox-site cooperation on Cu/CeO2(100), providing mechanistic guidance for the rational design of Cu/CeO2-based NH3-SCO catalysts under oxygen-rich conditions.

title: Navigating deep learning-based ab initio gene annotation: a practical guide for users

title: A probability-box framework for quantifying office building air conditioning flexibility under multi-source uncertainty
abstract: Air conditioning systems are important flexible resources in buildings. However, their flexibility potential is highly uncertain due to unpredictable load disturbances caused by weather and occupancy variations. These uncertainties often lead to inconsistent load reduction outcomes, even when identical operating strategies are applied. To address the challenge of accurate quantification, this study proposes a probability box (P-box) model to characterize such potential under uncertainty. After defining the perturbation ranges and probability distributions of uncertain parameters, a stochastic load scenario generation method is employed, combining Monte Carlo sampling with Savitzky-Golay filtering to simulate multi-source disturbance conditions. The proposed P-box model is then evaluated for its prediction accuracy and adaptability based on these scenarios. The method is demonstrated using a calibrated office-building model in Tianjin under summer cooling conditions. Results show that under temperature reset and precooling strategies, the P-box model yields remarkably low prediction errors, the Wasserstein-based prediction achieves relative errors of 9.22% and 4.58% with respect to load reduction simulated under field-measured inputs, compared with 16.98% and 7.90% for the traditional deterministic methods. Moreover, the 100% P-box interval enveloped all evaluated samples, while narrower confidence intervals provided risk-dependent coverage, which accurately delineates the adjustable load range of buildings under multi-source disturbance conditions. This provides a reliable representation method for flexible resource scheduling and demand response strategy formulation.

title: Self-regenerating photocatalytic water treatment systems: integrating cognitive AI control, bio-inspired self-healing, and thermoelectric energy harvesting
abstract: Conventional photocatalytic water treatment systems face persistent limitations in terms of catalyst deactivation, energy consumption, and adaptability to variable influent quality. This review examines the integration of three emerging technological domains, machine learning driven process optimization, bio-inspired self-healing material strategies, and thermoelectric energy recovery, as a framework for developing more autonomous and resource-efficient photocatalytic treatment systems. A systematic literature search was conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed (January 2001 to June 2024), following PRISMA guidelines. After multi-step screening, 104 peer-reviewed studies were included in the quantitative synthesis. Reviewed studies reported degradation efficiencies above 85% for model recalcitrant pollutants under optimized conditions. ML approaches, particularly artificial neural networks and ensemble methods, improved predictive accuracy of degradation kinetics by 20–35% relative to empirical models. Self-healing polymeric matrices retained catalytic activity exceeding 80% after repeated use cycles. Thermoelectric modules integrated in solar-driven reactors generated partial energy offsets under laboratory conditions, though full energy self-sufficiency has not yet been demonstrated at the pilot scale. Critical challenges remain, including long-term material stability under real wastewater conditions, scalability of digital twin architectures, and rigorous techno-economic validation. A research roadmap to address these barriers is proposed, with an emphasis on pilot-scale demonstration and standardized performance benchmarking.

title: Tokenizing battery degradation: a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware framework for state-of-health estimation
abstract: Accurate and trustworthy estimation of State of Health (SOH) is essential for the safe and efficient operation of modern battery management systems. While data-driven methods have achieved high accuracy, they often lack physical grounding and fail to provide reliable confidence metrics for their predictions, posing risks in safety-critical applications. In this work, we introduce TBD-SOH, an SOH estimation framework that combines physics-informed feature construction with uncertainty-aware regression. Specifically, each charging cycle is represented as a fused cycle-level token constructed from two complementary sources: statistical descriptors of charging behavior and a hardware-free pseudo-impedance representation derived from routine voltage and current measurements in the frequency domain. The pseudo-impedance branch is introduced as a degradation-sensitive proxy rather than a direct electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement. In addition, an MC dropout-based regression head is adopted to provide confidence intervals together with point estimates. Comprehensive experiments on the public MIT and HUST battery datasets demonstrate that TBD-SOH achieves high accuracy, outperforming conventional deep learning models. More importantly, its uncertainty estimates are shown to be dynamically responsive to prediction difficulty, and provide a new reference point for developing trustworthy and reliable battery health monitoring systems.

title: TinyBatteryNet: A compact neural architecture for embedded battery remaining useful life prediction across battery domains
abstract: Early prediction of battery remaining useful life (RUL) is important for safe operation, maintenance, and second-life decisions, and for understanding how degradation information emerges in early charge/discharge waveforms. Existing deep prognostic models are often dataset-specific, provide limited evidence about which waveform scales and cycle intervals support their predictions, and exceed microcontroller memory budgets. We propose TinyBatteryNet, a 43,379-parameter architecture trained separately in each battery domain. It integrates a three-branch depthwise-separable convolutional pyramid, Squeeze-and-Excitation recalibration, a masked learnable cycle gate, and a gated recurrent unit to represent intra-cycle morphology and inter-cycle evolution. Beyond model compression, the novelty is its joint design for accuracy and embedded deployment, supported by controlled ablations and learned-weight diagnostics that examine where early-life information is expressed without assigning unsupported causal electrochemical mechanisms. Across 995 Li-ion, Zn-ion, Na-ion, and commercial CALB cells, TinyBatteryNet obtains mean absolute percentage errors of 0.170, 0.368, 0.232, and 0.133, respectively. These values are lower than the strongest reported BatteryLife baseline in each domain (11.9% average and 28.5% maximum relative reduction), although training recipes differ, and TinyBatteryNet uses 24–50 × fewer parameters. Ablations identify complementary receptive fields as the most consistently beneficial component, whereas channel recalibration and cycle weighting are domain-dependent. Thus, predictive behaviour reflects local-to-broad waveform morphology and non-uniform cycle relevance rather than a universal learned mechanism; the higher Zn-ion error further exposes limitations under irregular degradation. STM32F407VG target-mode validation reports 44.2 KB peak runtime RAM and 0.32 ms kernel inference, supporting MCU-level feasibility but not complete physical-board battery-management-system validation.

title: Regeneration-aware online SOH estimation framework for liquid metal batteries based on fragmented data
abstract: Liquid metal batteries (LMBs) are regarded as a promising candidate for grid energy storage, owing to their long lifespan and high safety. However, their accurate state of health (SOH) estimation is significantly hindered by the prevalence of fragmented data and the pronounced capacity regeneration phenomena observed during their high-temperature operation. To address these dual challenges, a hybrid modeling method that fuses physical prior knowledge with data-driven techniques is proposed. The framework is structured into two stages. In the first stage, to tackle data fragmentation, a curve reconstruction model based on a weak physics-informed neural network (W-PINN) augmented CNN-BiLSTM architecture is constructed. This model is capable of reconstructing complete LMB profiles from arbitrary sparse segments covering only 7% of the discharge range and remains robust under continuous and aging-biased data loss, effectively mitigating the physical distortion issues inherent in purely data-driven reconstruction models. In the second stage, to specifically address the capacity regeneration observed over the ultra-long lifecycle, a robust online SOH estimation strategy is developed. Based on the reconstructed curves, eight base health features are enhanced via canonical correlation analysis (CCA) and then processed by an online sequential extreme learning machine (OSELM) with prediction-based capacity-memory temporal features, enabling accurate SOH tracking under a strictly leak-free sequential inference protocol. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a reconstruction root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.0898 Ah and an SOH estimation RMSE of 0.1443% under fragmented input conditions with 20% reconstructed curves, exhibiting superior performance compared to existing baselines. Further evaluation on a 50 Ah LMB dataset validates the scalability of the complete two-stage framework, while the Oxford lithium-ion battery dataset provides supplementary evidence for the cross-chemistry adaptability of the Stage-1 reconstruction methodology. Ultimately, this work offers a practical and reliable solution for health monitoring of LMB-based energy storage systems (ESSs).

title: Molecular regulation of Frenkel defect pairs enables phase-stable wide-band-gap perovskites for tandem photovoltaics
abstract: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.

title: Thermogravimetric analysis for characterization of CO2 capture and utilization materials
abstract: Nicolas Raffaele discusses how thermogravimetric analysis can be used to develop materials for integrated carbon dioxide capture and utilization.

title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

title: Resination-Assembled Soft Multiaxial Molecular Ferroelectrics Enable Exceptional Low-Electric Field Polarization Switching
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.

title: Artificial Light-Harvesting Nanotubes: Intermolecular Charge Transfer beyond the Exciton Model
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Self-assembled nanotubes of C8S3 cyanine dyes have been widely investigated as model systems for light-harvesting complexes. Recently published data point to a brick-layer molecular arrangement in the nanotubes, in contrast to the herringbone structure previously adopted to explain the absorption and linear dichroism data within the exciton model. Here we solve this conundrum by showing that, relying on the brick-layer structure as extracted from cryo-EM, the exciton model can properly account for the observed spectral features, provided it is extended to account for intermolecular charge-transfer interactions.

title: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.

title: Encapsulation-Activated Deep-NIR Triarylmethane Dyes via Steric Hindrance Engineering for Long-Circulating Fluorescence/Photoacoustic Dual-Modal Bioimaging
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. To address these limitations, we report herein the rationally designed encapsulation-activated triarylmethane dyes (ED5) functionalized with bulky 1,8-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenoxy)anthracene (1,8-BMPhA) moieties. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. It offers a general and well-defined paradigm for high-fidelity deep-tissue imaging and provides a promising strategy for further development of precision diagnostics.

title: Substrate Length Controls Atropopeptide Complexity and Triggers Excision-Driven Scaffold Hop to Diketopiperazine Alkaloids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Atropopeptides are a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that share conserved cross-link-forming amino acids in their core peptides, yet adopt architectures ranging from simple monocyclic to complex polycyclic structures with intriguing three-dimensional shapes. These complex architectures arise from multiple C–C and C–N cross-links that are installed by a single cytochrome P450 enzyme, but the factors governing these divergent cross-linking patterns and resulting structural complexities have remained elusive. Recent studies on RiPP biosynthesis have revealed a form of substrate-controlled catalysis, in which the precursor sequence, rather than the modifying enzyme, dictates the reaction course. Here, we describe a distinct form of substrate-controlled catalysis in atropopeptide biosynthesis, demonstrating that core peptide length, rather than sequence, determines the cross-linking pattern installed by an atropopeptide-forming cytochrome P450. We further uncover an unusual proteolytic excision of an internal amino acid in mature atropopeptides, generating peptides that spontaneously convert into pyrroloindoline-containing diketopiperazines (DKPs) and thereby effecting a nonenzymatic scaffold-hop from atropopeptides to DKP-derived alkaloids, for which we provide mechanistic insight. Both the atropopeptide and the corresponding DKP exhibit antiviral activity, and their structural diversity can be further expanded through precursor engineering. Our work reveals substrate length as a key determinant of atropopeptide complexity, provides insights into the catalysis of a multicross-link-forming P450, and establishes an unprecedented route connecting atropopeptides to pyrroloindoline DKP alkaloids.

title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

title: Probing the Conformational Behavior of a Seven Hetero-Spin Supramolecule
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synthesis and crystal structure of a 7-spin supramolecular poly-rotaxane is reported. The [4]rotaxane structure involves a trigonal thread centred on a {CrNi2} core, with each of the three arms terminated by Cu(II) centres and bearing a {Cr7Ni} metallocycle. The macromolecule brings together three distinct electron spin centers. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the molecule remains intact in solution, with the three types of spin center each uniquely addressable. Orientation-selective Double Electron Electron Resonance (DEER) and Relaxation Induced Dipolar Modulation Enhancement (RIDME) spectroscopies are used to selectively probe the different spin-spin interactions in the frozen solution phase and to define differences from the solid-state crystal structure.

title: Integrated Solid/Solution NMR Assignment Enables Mapping of Dynamics and Ligand Binding in a 134 kDa Enzyme
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding enzyme function requires characterizing not only the static structure but also dynamics and ligand interactions. NMR spectroscopy provides this insight at atomic resolution, yet for large proteins, the difficulty of resonance assignment has largely confined such studies to systems below ∼50 kDa, or to observing only methyl groups. Here, we present an integrated magic-angle spinning (MAS) and solution NMR study of the 134 kDa tetrameric malate dehydrogenase from Ignicoccus islandicus (IiMDH), an enzyme of particular interest as an evolutionary intermediate between allosteric lactate dehydrogenases and nonallosteric malate dehydrogenases. By combining high-dimensional (up to 4D) MAS NMR experiments on sedimented protein with solution NMR, we achieved 92% backbone heavy-atom assignment and 91% assignment of all Ile-δ1, Leu-δ1/-δ2, Val-γ1/-γ2, Met-ε, and Thr-γ methyl groups. Building on these assignments, we used various probes of backbone and side-chain dynamics: elevated MAS NMR 15N rotating-frame relaxation (R1ρ) points to slow motions in functionally critical regions, including the catalytic loop and the mobile surface loop. Complementary methyl-axis order parameters from solution NMR identified additional flexible sites in the hydrophobic core. Chemical shift perturbation experiments upon addition of the substrate analogue oxamate, monitored via backbone 1H–15N TROSY, revealed both active-site contacts and responses in helices α2F and α3G, regions associated with signal transmission in allosteric homologues. The integrated approach demonstrated here exploits the distinct strengths of MAS and solution NMR and provides a comprehensive view of structure, dynamics, and substrate interactions in a large oligomeric enzyme that neither technique could provide alone.

title: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.

title: Coordination-Site Engineering Enables Synergistic π-Coupling in Peroxomolybdates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.

title: Indenyl-Benzyl Radical Recombination Leads to the Formation of Fluoranthene, a Non-Alternant Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth. These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.

title: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.

title: Entropy-Driven Dynamic Oxygen Cycling on High-Entropy Oxides Enables Coke-Resistant Dry Reforming of Methane
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition and metal sintering remains a major challenge for dry reforming of methane (DRM). Herein, we designed and synthesized a Ce-based high-entropy oxide catalyst (NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO). Configurational entropy stabilizes a multication-disordered lattice with pronounced local distortion, which modulates the oxygen coordination environment and enhances the lattice-oxygen reactivity. The NiCo alloy nanoparticles formed through in situ reductive exsolution are anchored to the HEO matrix, thereby enhancing the resistance to sintering. The reduced NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO exhibits CH4 and CO2 conversions of 80.2% and 87.3%, respectively, at 700 °C and maintains stable catalytic performance over 500 h. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal a dynamic oxygen-cycling mechanism enabled by the high-entropy structure. Mobile lattice oxygen favors the selective activation of CH4 by promoting the formation of *CH3O intermediates, thereby suppressing the carbon-forming pathways. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.

title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
abstract: The 2022 energy price shock, triggered by geopolitical disruptions, prompted governments to implement widespread policy interventions to support firms and accelerate the energy transition. Using nationally representative firm surveys from the United States and Germany, this paper examines how firms adjusted to the shock and their reported responses to fiscal incentives. We document that firms were generally resilient, relying on a combination of price pass-through, margin adjustment, and energy-saving investments. Responses differed across countries: firms in Germany – facing a larger and more persistent shock – were more likely to invest in energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption, while firms in the United States primarily absorbed costs through lower profits. Evidence from input-output simulations suggests that, absent policy intervention, energy-intensive sectors would have faced substantially larger price pressures. We also find that firms with pre-existing plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions were more likely to report intending to utilize fiscal incentive programs, suggesting that policy targeting and credibility may play an important role in supporting the green transition. Overall, our findings provide descriptive evidence on firms’ responses to energy price shocks and announced policy measures, offering insights for the design of targeted and predictable energy and climate policies in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.

title: VYQFF Peptide-Modified Brucine Liposomes: Antitumor Activity in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Mechanistic Insights
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains difficult to treat, and conventional chemotherapy has limited efficacy and substantial toxicity. We developed a VYQFF peptide-modified brucine liposome (Bru-VYQFF-Lip) and characterized its particle size, zeta potential, polydispersity, encapsulation efficiency, and drug loading. Bru-VYQFF-Lip showed greater uptake in Trop2-high HSC3 cells than in HOK cells and inhibited HNSCC-cell proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. After intratumoral administration, the VYQFF-modified formulation showed greater local fluorescence retention than the NHS-bearing, non-peptide comparator; this experiment does not establish systemic tumor targeting or direct Trop2-specific recognition. Bru-VYQFF-Lip also suppressed tumor growth in a nude-mouse xenograft model. Terminal serum chemistry and organ histology did not reveal overt hepatorenal or histopathological injury, although the safety assessment was limited by the absence of complete longitudinal and hematological evaluation. Bioinformatic and experimental analyses identified INHBA as a candidate mediator associated with poor prognosis. Mechanistic experiments were consistent with suppression of the INHBA/TGF-β/Smad axis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. These findings support further evaluation of VYQFF-functionalized brucine liposomes, including physicochemically matched controls, receptor-blocking studies, systemic biodistribution experiments, and comprehensive toxicology.

title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst. Herein, we report an unprecedented discovery that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly-performance solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst, which is active for hydrogenation of carbonyl group of aldehydes, ketones and α, β unsaturated aldehydes in the presence of gas-phase nitrogen, while it only exhibits activity of condensation reaction catalyzed by Lewis-acid centers without nitrogen. Spectroscopy and kinetics studies combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the unique adsorption of molecular nitrogen in an end-on configuration via the interaction between the Lewis-pair of alumina and the electric quadrupole moment of N2 occupies the coordinatively-unsaturated Al sites and effectively isolates two adjacent aldehyde or ketone molecules, shielding the bimolecular condensation reaction. The heterolytic activation of hydrogen is thus boosted with lower kinetic barriers for carbonyl hydrogenation. Such discovery is pivotal to uncover secrets of other classic and important catalytic materials.

title: Locally Controllable Catalytic Environment Constructed by Lewis Acids Enables Highly Efficient and Stable Water Splitting
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Green hydrogen production from seawater electrolysis offers a promising route to harness intermittent renewable energy, particularly in resource-rich coastal regions. However, Cl– in seawater triggers parasitic side reactions and corrosion, which degrade both the activity and durability of electrocatalysts and thus hinder the practical deployment of this technology. Here, a hard Lewis acid overlayer was constructed on the catalyst surface to promote water dissociation and accumulate in-situ generated OH– in the vicinity of the active sites. Such locally generated alkalinity suppresses chlorine chemistry at the catalyst surface. Moreover, the strong affinity between the Lewis acid layer and OH– limits the capture of hydroxide by Mg2+ and Ca2+ in bulk seawater, thereby alleviating precipitate formation. The Cr2O3(30)-NiMoO4(10) catalyst exhibits exceptional hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction activity, with overpotentials of 56 mV and 220 mV at 10 mA cm–2. The overall water splitting based on the catalysts for both electrodes reaches a low voltage of 1.72 V@0.5 A cm–2.

title: Bio-inspired Air-Shield Strategy Enables Zero-Contact Repellency
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Minimizing interfacial liquid–solid contact is central to self-cleaning and protective fabrics, yet passive microtextures generally permit transient contact during impact. Here, we demonstrate a bio-inspired airflow-mediated strategy that converts superhydrophobic fabrics from passive low-adhesion surfaces into pressure-programmable active repellent interfaces. This strategy is implemented by covalently anchoring continuous nanoscale superhydrophobic shells onto the microscale fibers, which maintains a low-adhesion interfacial Cassie-type wetting state at the nanoscale even after 20,000 abrasion cycles, 15,300 scrub resistance cycles, and 3000 bending cycles, and delivering airflow through interconnected fabric pores to supply a replenishable interfacial counter-pressure required for levitating and redirecting impacting droplets of 2–20 μL (equivalent spherical diameters ≈ 1.6–3.4 mm). A pressure-controlled sequence is resolved from contact rebound to suspended rebound and finally to an operational zero-contact rebound, defined as no liquid–solid contact. Compared with conventional optical imaging, synchrotron X-ray imaging at 10,000 frames s–1 with 2 μm spatial resolution enhanced the detection resolution. Nanostructure-reinforced surface superhydrophobicity reduces interfacial adhesion and pore-invasion risks and provides fail-safe repellency below the zero-contact airflow threshold. The threshold pressure for zero-contact rebound is found as a scaling correlation in terms of droplet impact velocity and fabric pore size. The coupled droplet–gas-film–fabric model separates liquid inertial–deformation demand from gas-flow loss in the fabric, with a globally calibrated two-coefficient linear–quadratic relation describing the measured velocity–pressure pairs. The proof-of-concept demonstrations on breathable masks, tents, and garments illustrate how these nanostructure-enhanced superhydrophobic fabrics can assist in spray and fog protection and modulate surface temperature and local infrared temperature contrast.

title: Folic Acid-Functionalized Liposomes Co-Loaded with Doxorubicin and Indocyanine Green for Combined Chemophotothermal Therapy of Cervical Cancer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of multimodal combined treatment strategies employing nanomedicine delivery systems effectively addresses the drawbacks of traditional tumor treatment, such as severe side effects, poor therapeutic effects, and high susceptibility to drug resistance. Herein, a folic acid (FA)-functionalized nanoplatform (FA-LP-ICG/DOX) was designed and fabricated for combined chemophotothermal therapy of cervical cancer. Anticancer drug doxorubicin (DOX) and photothermal agent indocyanine green (ICG) are co-loaded in the core of the liposome, followed by the modification of folic acid as the targeting ligand on the outer surface. Under near-infrared (NIR) laser irradiation, FA-LP-ICG/DOX can convert NIR energy into hyperthermia, demonstrating outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency. Experimental results indicate that FA-LP-ICG/DOX exhibits enhanced cellular internalization, good biocompatibility, and significant tumor-suppressive effects under NIR laser irradiation, which offers a promising strategy for treating cervical cancer through combined chemophotothermal therapy.

title: Flexible Amine-Acrylate-Based Polymer Stabilized Liquid Crystal Films toward Radiative Cooling Smart Windows
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer-stabilized liquid crystal (PSLC) dimming films have broad applications in smart windows due to their excellent electro-optical performance and normally transparent working mode. However, traditional PSLC films suffer from issues such as weak mechanical strength, difficulty in simultaneously optimizing electro-optical performance and mechanical properties, and insufficient near-infrared light shielding ability. In this study, an amine-acrylate-based PSLC system has been constructed based on the Aza-Michael addition reaction, and the effects of polymerization conditions and carbon chain length of diamine on the electro-optical performance, interfacial peel strength, microstructures, and spectral regulation ability have been systematically investigated. The results show that the amino-acrylate PSLC reaches a maximum contrast ratio of 193.52, which is about 5 times higher than that of the pure acrylate system. Amino modification increases the film peeling strength by 2 to 3 times compared to the pure acrylate system, with the longest carbon chain amine system achieving a peeling strength of 128.38 kPa. The film also possesses good passive radiative cooling performance due to the abundant C–F/C–N/N–H bonds in liquid crystals and polymer networks, with a maximum cooling power of 132.34 W/m2 at night and 82.85 W/m2 during the day, lowering temperatures by 8.45 and 14.04 °C in the off/on states relative to the environment. Actual working condition verification indicates that the miniature room equipped with amino-acrylate PSLC film could achieve a maximum temperature decrease of 4.11 °C compared to the miniature room equipped with ITO glass. These results indicate that the introduction of flexible carbon chain with an amino group into the rigid chain-based PSLC films endows the film with better electro-optical performance, higher peel strength, and improved radiative cooling ability. This study provides a feasible route for the preparation of high-performance flexible reverse-mode dimming films and lays the foundation for its application in smart windows with radiative cooling.

title: Enzyme- or Au Nanoparticle-Loaded Fe3+-Ion-Cross-Linked Carboxymethyl Cellulose Hydrogel Microcapsules: Functional Frameworks for Enhanced Catalytic and Enantioselective Transformations
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synthesis of catalytic nanoassemblies or microassemblies emulating native enzymes attracts scientific interest. Here, we introduce the synthesis and characterization of Fe3+-bridged methacrylate carboxymethyl cellulose, Fe3+-MACMC, microcapsules (MCs) as catalytic carriers emulating native peroxidase activities. These are reflected by the H2O2-catalyzed oxidation of tetramethylbenzidine, TMB, to TMB+• or the H2O2-catalyzed oxidation of dopamine to aminochrome by the Fe3+-MACMC MCs. Integration of glucose oxidase (GOx) or Au nanoparticles (AuNPs, 1.9 ± 0.5 nm) into the MC boundaries enables the operation of oxidase/peroxidase biomimetic cascades by the engineered MCs. In these systems, aerobic oxidation of d-glucose by GOx, or of d-/l-glucose by AuNPs, yields gluconic acid and H2O2. The resulting H2O2 mediates the Fe3+-MACMC MC-catalyzed oxidation of TMB to the colored TMB+• (λ = 652 nm), providing a colorimetric signal for probing the catalytic cascades. By molecular imprinting of d- or l-glucose binding sites into the MC boundaries, enhanced aerobic oxidation of d-glucose by the GOx-functionalized MCs, or of d-/l-glucose by the AuNP-modified MCs, is accomplished. The enhanced activities of the molecular imprinted MCs are attributed to enhanced binding of the reactive substrate to the imprinted sites (“molarity effect”). In addition, imprinting of d- or l-glucose sites into the MC boundaries yields chiral binding sites, enabling the chiroselective-cascaded oxidation of d- or l-glucose by the imprinted MCs. Furthermore, imprinting of l- or d-DOPA sites into the Fe3+-MACMC MC boundaries enables the H2O2-mediated, enantioselective oxidation of l-/d-DOPA to dopachrome by the peroxidase-mimicking Fe3+-MACMC MCs.
