title: Crystallographic Parity and Inverse Area Scaling in Two-Dimensional Perovskite Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for next-generation high-density non-volatile memory; however, conventional polycrystalline oxide FTJs face issues with defect-induced leakage and degraded ferroelectricity at nanometer scales. Here, we demonstrate atomically defined nanocrossbar FTJs based on single-crystalline two-dimensional (2D) Dion–Jacobson perovskite nanosheets designed to address these scaling challenges. Electrical transport measurements reveal crystallographic-parity-dependent switching behavior: odd-layered (m = 3, 5) homologs exhibit hysteretic switching consistent with ferroelectric tunnel barriers, whereas even-layered (m = 4, 6) homologs show non-switching behavior consistent with paraelectric controls. Simmons-model analysis supports direct tunneling as the dominant transport mechanism through the atomically uniform nanosheet barriers, even at the smallest junction area of 520 nm2. Notably, the tunneling electroresistance (TER) ratio increases as the junction area decreases, reaching approximately 35, consistent with the suppression of defect-induced OFF-state current inhomogeneity under nanoconfinement. These FTJs show strong non-volatile retention (extrapolated to 10 years) and reliable switching endurance (100 cycles) at room temperature. These results highlight that crystallographic layer parity and nanoconfinement-enabled defect avoidance serve as key design principles for scalable 2D ferroelectric tunnel devices and facilitate pathways toward ultra-dense post-Moore memory and neuromorphic computing architectures. This favorable scaling behavior aligns lateral miniaturization with improved memory contrast and, together with the metal-electrode nanocrossbar architecture, provides a promising basis for high-density integration if wafer-scale nanosheet assembly and reproducible interface control can be established.

title: Ultrastable Cycling of Sodium Metal Battery at Rates Exceeding 20 C Achieved with a NaB3H8-SiO2 Composite Solid Electrolyte
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solid-state sodium metal batteries are promising candidates for grid-scale energy storage due to their inherent safety and low cost. However, the development of solid electrolytes that support high-rate (>20 C) cycling for fast-charging applications remains a major challenge. Herein, we explore how adding SiO2 affects the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression of NaB3H8, to develop superior solid electrolytes for high-rate batteries. The composites featuring an amorphous passivating layer with B–O bonds were fabricated via ball milling. Among them, NaB3H8-40%SiO2 exhibits the best conductivity, reaching 0.62 mS cm–1 at 25 °C, 2 orders of magnitude higher than that of pristine NaB3H8. Crucially, by reducing electronic conductivity and enhancing mechanical strength, it possesses a high critical current density of up to 6.5 mA cm–2, significantly higher than that of other reported hydridoborates. The Na/NaB3H8-40%SiO2/TiS2 batteries exhibit superior rate capability (216.4 mAh g–1 at 1 C and 143.1 mAh g–1 at 20 C) and long-term cycling stability (nearly 100.0% capacity retention after 2000 cycles at 20 C) at 30 °C. This work offers a promising approach for the development of innovative solid electrolytes in fast-charging or high-power-density sodium metal batteries.

title: One-Step Preparation of a Self-Standing LiFePO4 Cathode with an In Situ SiO2 Coating via Modified Coaxial Electrospinning for Advanced Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract LiFePO4 cathodes have gained much attention for Li-ion batteries due to their superior electrochemical and economic features. However, their practical applications are limited by poor electronic conductivity, sluggish lithium-ion diffusion, and unstable cathode/electrolyte interfaces. Conventional approaches require separate electrode fabrication and surface coating steps, increasing process complexity. Herein, a modified coaxial electrospinning method was developed to prepare a free-standing LiFePO4 cathode with a simultaneous in situ SiO2 coating. The core solution consists of LiFePO4 and polyacrylonitrile, while the shell solution consists of ethanol and tetraethyl orthosilicate. The modified coaxial electrode (CE-LFP@SiO2) exhibits a more uniform and smaller average fiber diameter (200 nm) compared to the single electrospinning electrode (E-LFP). Results confirm the formation of a thin SiO2 surface coating. The discharge capacity at 0.1 C reaches 166.3 mAh g–1, compared with 160.0 mAh g–1 for E-LFP and 150.0 mAh g–1 for a conventional LiFePO4 electrode (LFP). CE-LFP@SiO2 provides a capacity retention of 89% after 300 cycles, compared with 78 and 74% for E-LFP and LFP, respectively. The lithium-ion diffusion coefficient increases to 4.70 × 10–13 cm2 s–1, compared with 5.43 × 10–14 cm2 s–1 for LFP. This work demonstrates a simple one-step strategy for simultaneously fabricating and coating free-standing LiFePO4 cathodes.

title: Next-Generation Autocatalysis-Integrated Antibody-Bioorthogonal Catalyst Conjugates for Amplified Cell-Surface Antigen Imaging and Targeted In Situ Prodrug Activation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Immunoassays and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) rely on specific antigen–antibody recognition for biomarker detection and targeted cancer therapy; however, their practical performance is often hampered by low antigen abundance, which yields weak readout signals or insufficient local drug concentrations. Autocatalytic bioorthogonal reactions offer an attractive route to achieve exponential signal amplification, but existing CuAAC-based autocatalytic systems suffer from slow multistep ligand assembly and fluorophore self-quenching that degrade signal-to-background ratios. Herein, we report a next-generation autocatalysis-integrated bioorthogonal catalyst-linked immunosorbent assay (BCLISA) employing bis(triazolylmethyl)aminopropyne (DTTA) as a key autocatalytic precursor. Unlike the prior tripropargylamine (TPA) system that demands three successive CuAAC events for ligand formation, DTTA assembles active tris(triazolylmethyl)amine ligands via only one single CuAAC reaction with 7-azidocoumarin (7AC), incorporating merely one coumarin moiety per ligand to mitigate fluorescence self-quenching. Benefiting from accelerated kinetics and suppressed self-quenching, DTTA-mediated autocatalysis enables sensitive in vitro detection of recombinant HER2 and BK polyomavirus VP1 antigens, outperforming commercial ELISA kits. Functionalized with n-octyl lipid tails, DTTA-C8 anchors autocatalytic cascades onto living cell membranes, allowing confocal imaging and quantitative measurement of low-abundance cell-surface antigens free from endogenous enzyme interference. Furthermore, autocatalytically generated copper catalytic centers drive local CuAAC-mediated prodrug cyclization to produce cytotoxic agents. Distinct from conventional ADC approaches that pursue high drug-to-antibody ratios, our strategy achieves targeted in situ drug activation without heavy antibody modification, retaining native antibody-binding capacity and eliciting antigen-selective cancer-cell death. This work illustrates the utility of rationally optimized autocatalytic bioorthogonal cascades to couple antibody-based molecular recognition with exponential chemical amplification for both diagnostic and therapeutic applications.

title: Nickel Nanoparticles Anchored by Nano-ZrO2 on SiO2 for CO2 Methanation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract ZrO2 is an effective support for CO2 methanation, but its low surface area limits the dispersion and thus activity and stability of the Ni/ZrO2 catalyst. Herein, a ZrO2/SiO2 support was constructed by dispersing nano-ZrO2 on high-surface-area SiO2 to improve the activity and anti-sintering capability of the Ni catalysts. The results showed that SiO2 stabilized the nano-ZrO2, which further provided favorable sites for dispersing and stabilizing Ni species. Ni/0.4ZS exhibited decent performance among the Ni/xZS catalysts (x was the mass ratio of ZrO2 to SiO2) due to the increased dispersion of Ni. Moderate CeO2 promoter addition further improved the activity and resistance to deactivation due to the increased dispersion of Ni NPs and the enhanced adsorption of CO2. XPS and DFT results indicated that the composite support strengthened the electronic interaction between Ni species and the support. Furthermore, based on the experimental and DFT results, it is proposed that additional geometric stabilization of Ni species may be provided by the spatially constrained sites between adjacent nano-ZrO2 particles. These findings demonstrated that constructing nano-ZrO2 on SiO2 was an effective strategy for developing active and stable Ni-based catalysts for CO2 methanation.

title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recycling end-of-life (EoL) NdFeB magnets is critical for securing supply of rare-earth element neodymium in the low-carbon transition. We develop a molten salt electrolysis recycling approach using EoL NdFeB magnet anodes and a consumable solid magnesium cathode, operating at 548–650 °C and 0.75–3 A·cm−2 cathodic current density. Selective neodymium dissolution and in situ formation of a liquid Mg– (12.0–15.1 mol%) Nd alloy with average current efficiency of 98.4% are achieved. With high recycling efficiency and continuous operation, this approach overcomes neodymium collection and scalability barriers of conventional chloride electrolysis. Life-cycle assessment shows that the proposed process lowers climate change impacts to 17.36–18.18 kg CO2 eq. kg⁻¹ Nd, approximately 15% of that of primary production. Techno-economic analysis shows that neodymium metal production costs fall to 90.0 USD kg⁻¹ Nd at the 3000 A scale scenario, which is approximately one-third lower than the sales price of Nd metal. Such approach demonstrates significant potential for industrial-scale application and facilitates the integration of neodymium recycling into circular economy strategies.

title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production.1 However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications.2 Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties.3–5 Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid–liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid–liquid interface adheres to polar surfaces up to 90-fold more strongly than does pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than does PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C–H bond functionalization at the solid–liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.

title: Precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine covalent organic frameworks for atmospheric water harvesting
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Interlayer stacking modes dictated by noncovalent interactions play a pivotal role in influencing pore structures and emergent properties of 2D covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), yet precise control over stacking modes remains challenging. Herein, we report a supramolecular strategy based on dipole-dipole interactions originated from 4,7-bis(phenylethynyl)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (BT) units, enabling precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine-linked COFs. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that BT incorporation directs antiparallel stacking through cooperative hydrogen bonding and multiple π–π interactions between adjacent layers. The resulting COF-BB-R (R = H, 2Me and 4Me) exhibits higher crystallinity and stability than the corresponding eclipsed-stacked COF-PB-R. Notably, COF-BB-H achieves a total water uptake of 0.70 g g−1 at 298 K, 2.2-fold higher than COF-PB-H (0.32 g g−1) and surpassing that of most imine-based COF adsorbents. This work provides an effective approach for precisely fabricating antiparallel-stacked 2D COFs for next-generation functional porous materials.

title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between care systems and family demographic structures in shaping end-of-life care access, and underscore the need for tailored policy approaches that strengthen both formal and informal care systems while addressing sociodemographic disparities in care access.

title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr−1. Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

title: Enhancing fairness in climate action through policy packages
abstract:
Abstract
                  Achieving a fair transition to climate neutrality requires a careful balancing of policy options. Here we quantitatively evaluate the equity implications of different European Union climate policy packages, considering pricing, regulation via standards, subsidies and transfers. Leveraging an integrated modelling framework, we show that standards limit impact variability within income groups, whereas carbon pricing with transfer-based revenue recycling offsets regressive impacts between income groups. Restricting climate policy implementation to either option, therefore, gives rise to a trade-off between horizontal and vertical equity. We then demonstrate numerically how a multi-instrument budget-neutral policy package can resolve this trade-off. Adopting a broader equity perspective that encompasses both horizontal and vertical equity shifts the preferred policy mix towards a combination of standards, pricing, subsidies and transfers. These results provide an explicit, quantified, equity-based rationale for the adoption and acceptability of comprehensive climate policy packages, offering a more nuanced view on policy design.

title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

title: Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Soft robots operate safely in delicate, confined environments and require materials that combine softness and large deformation in complex architectures. Digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing enables such structures, but rapid curing fixes networks with short strands, limiting extensibility of printed hydrogels. Here we report a controlled post-print decrosslinking strategy that decouples shape fixation from network maturation to yield highly stretchable, strong DLP-printed hydrogels. In this design, photo-triggered, base-cleavable coupling between o-nitrobenzyl acetal and (meth)acrylate groups establishes a dense network for printing and shape fixation. Subsequent alkaline cleavage restores chain mobility and lengthens network strands, while hydrophobic side-group modification induces phase-separated domains that enhance strength. The resulting hydrogels reach 1100% strain at break and 3.7 MPa tensile strength, combining high stretchability with high strength. This performance enables pneumatic actuators with 8-fold volumetric expansion and payload transport in confined fluidic environments. Our strategy provides a soft material platform for 3D-printed soft robotic systems requiring large, reversible deformation.

title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO2 and rutile SnO2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO2. The tensile-strained PtO2/SnO2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO2, delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO2/TiO2 and 469 °C for PtOx/Al2O3) and

title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. Existing methods have difficulty characterizing single-emitter spectra and optical heterogeneity with accuracy and ease-of-use. Here, we introduce SPICEE (SPectrally Imbalanced Correlations from Ensemble Emission), a photon-correlation technique that automatically samples an ensemble to recover statistical trends in the single-particle spectra. Analytical derivations, numerical modeling, and experiments on a solution ensemble of emitters validate the technique. We apply SPICEE to blue-emitting ZnSeTe semiconductor nanocrystals relevant to display applications and find that the ensemble’s low color purity is primarily caused by a small subpopulation of nanocrystals with a distinct emission mechanism. This work demonstrates SPICEE to be an efficient and powerful tool for analyzing nanoscale systems.

title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Materials combining colossal birefringence with a wide bandgap are of considerable interest for miniaturized photonics, yet remain rare because strong optical transitions that enhance birefringence usually introduce optical loss. Here we show that CuAlO2 exhibits colossal ultraviolet–visible birefringence alongside a wide bandgap. Spectroscopic ellipsometry on millimeter-sized single crystals reveals a sharp, intense lowest-energy transition near 3.78 eV exclusively in the ab-plane, yielding a maximum birefringence ∣Δn∣max = 3.67, and ∣Δn∣ > 0.5 throughout the visible range, with a direct band gap of 3.71 eV. The same transition generates a Type-II hyperbolic window between two ultraviolet epsilon-near-zero points. First-principles calculations and optical selection rules attribute this anisotropy to Cu-dominated band-edge states and a dipole-allowed Cu dz2-to-px/y transition enabled by the linear O–Cu–O dumbbell structure. These results establish CuAlO2 as a natural oxide platform that bridges broadband low-loss birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolic photonics.

title: Wireless, optoelectronic, multimodal skin sensor for simultaneous monitoring of mechanical stress and vascular responses
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Prolonged mechanical loading and subsequent vascular ischemia drive the development of severe pressure injuries. Effective prevention of irreversible tissue damage requires monitoring both multiaxial mechanical forces and physiological erythema. However, conventional diagnostic tools remain limited by rigid architectures, single parameter detection, and subjective visual assessments. Here, a wireless, battery free optoelectronic multimodal sensor platform provides an integrated framework for tracking posture dependent mechanical loading and localized erythema. The soft, skin conformable device uses geometric light modulation within an isolated optical cavity to quantify normal pressure and biaxial shear stresses. To resolve complex mechanical environments, a deep neural network regression model decouples simultaneous tri-axial forces, Fx, Fy, and Fz, at the skin interface. Concurrently, a dual wavelength optical reflectance mechanism quantifies skin erythema by capturing subtle variations in hemoglobin absorption. Opaque elastomeric encapsulation shields the internal optics, supporting stable optical measurements under varying ambient illumination and skin conditions. System level integration via near field communication enables untethered operation across a multiplexed sensor network. On-body evaluations in a simulated clinical bed setting demonstrate the ability of the platform to dynamically map posture-dependent biomechanical loading and localized vascular responses, providing a technological basis for future studies on data-driven monitoring of the mechanical and vascular factors associated with pressure-injury risk.

title: Metabolically reprogrammed blastoids from totipotent-like stem cells exhibit enhanced tissue-specific organ-like development and placental formation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: While blastoids derived from pluripotent stem cells recapitulate pre- and early post-implantation embryogenesis, their long-term post-implantation development remains constrained. We define Snαnv, a chemical cocktail that promotes oxidative-phosphorylation-driven metabolic reprogramming, to efficiently generate ESC-blastoids with proper trophectoderm (TE)/inner cell mass (ICM) from conventional mouse ESCs at an efficiency of approximately 70%. These blastoids closely resemble blastocysts in morphology and cell-lineage allocation, with high Cdx2 expression in TE-like cells and notably display similar metabolic profiles. Furthermore, enhancing ESC totipotency via pladienolide B (PlaB) and crotonic acid (CA) augments the developmental potential of resulting PC-blastoids, which yield gonad-like tissues at E10.5, beating heart-like structures, and blood vessels under specific in vitro induction. These metabolically reprogrammed PC-blastoids are transcriptionally analogous to blastocysts by scRNA-seq. Moreover, they generate E7.0/E7.5-like embryos and placental structures comparable to E8.5 counterparts in vivo. Together, mimicking blastocyst metabolism and enhancing ESCs' totipotency yield blastoids with notably improved developmental competence.

title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Predicting cognitive processes from brain activation maps remains a key challenge in neuroscience. Meta-analytic functional decoding provides an estimation of behavioral profiles associated with specific brain regions; however, existing methods fail to capture the full semantic content of the neuroimaging literature. To address this, we present NiCLIP, a contrastive language-image model trained on over 23,000 articles to predict cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. NiCLIP achieves optimal performance when using full-text articles and a curated cognitive ontology with precise task-concept-domain mappings. Our results show that NiCLIP accurately predicts cognitive tasks from Human Connectome Project group-level maps across multiple domains (e.g., emotion, language, motor) and precisely characterizes the functional roles of specific brain regions, including the amygdala, hippocampus, and temporoparietal junction. However, NiCLIP showed limitations with noisy subject-level activation maps. NiCLIP represents a significant advancement in functional decoding, offering a powerful tool for hypothesis generation and scientific discovery.

title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) replenishment sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. However, chemotherapy-induced NAD+ metabolic reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotherapy induces a macrophage-dependent IL-1β inflammatory response and NAD+ metabolic reprogramming, thereby conferring chemoresistance via CD44. Mechanistically, IL-1β-induced NAD+ salvage cooperates with the clearance of nicotinamide (NAM), the physiological inhibitor of the NAD+-consuming enzymes sirtuins, to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance by boosting the NAD+/NAM ratio for sirtuin activation. NAM phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT)-mediated NAD+ salvage recycles NAD+ from NAM and further triggers serine biosynthesis, ultimately supporting NAM N-methyltransferase (NNMT)-mediated NAM clearance. Importantly, NAMPT inhibition disrupts the NAD+/NAM ratio and mitigates CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction, ultimately enhancing the efficacy of chemoimmunotherapy when combined with IL-2 across multiple preclinical models of solid tumors. Thus, our findings underscore the NAD+/NAM ratio as a metabolic therapeutic target for enhancing chemotherapy and NK cell-based chemoimmunotherapy efficacy.

title: High average and linear scaling of Ecological Footprint in cities
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cities are often assumed to be environmentally efficient in high-income countries, but their indirect impacts through consumption make this efficiency uncertain. Studies of agglomeration effects and urban scaling have reported contradictory results, with most analyses relying on consumption-based carbon footprints and rarely examining non-carbon impacts. Here we present spatially and sectorally detailed Ecological Footprint estimates covering all 83,603 populated US census tracts and disaggregating consumption into 52 categories in 2021. We found that per-capita Ecological Footprint was highest in cities, followed by suburbs and rural areas, with only small differences in effect size. Total urban Ecological Footprint scaled approximately linearly with population and remained robust across city delineations. These results indicate that cities do not exhibit clear footprint efficiency and that policies targeting settlement type or individual sectors alone are unlikely to deliver meaningful reductions. We suggest treating Ecological Footprint reduction as a wicked problem and reframing it toward actionability.

title: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.

title: Ultrafast water transport through densely fluorinated foldamer channels
abstract: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.

title: Life cycle environment and direct operating cost assessment of coal to polyolefin integrated with coke oven gas, membrane separation and CO2 utilization
abstract: Coal to polyolefin (CTP) is an important route for polyolefin in China, but its manufacturing process is associated with serious environmental issues. In this study, life cycle assessment (LCA) coupled with direct operating cost analysis methods were employed to compare the CTP route with petroleum, biomass, and waste plastic polyolefin production routes. On the basis, Dual gas feed (coal gas with coke oven gas, CTP-DGF), heat exchanger network optimization (CTP-HEN), externally and internally coupled membrane distillation (CTP-EMEM, CTP-MEM) and CO 2 utilization (CTP-CCU) technologies were respectively proposed and evaluated to improve the performance of traditional CTP route. Finally, the optimal integrated route (CTP-INT) was established from CTP-DGF, CTP-MEM and CTP-CCU. The results indicated that, CTP showed the highest environmental impacts, in which coal gasification and methanol to polyolefin units were the main contributors. Among the five optimization technologies, CTP-DGF exhibits the optimal environmental performance. Compared with CTP, CTP-INT reduced the global warming potential and direct operating cost by 49.7% and 19.0%. In the future, the environmental impact of CTP-INT route could be reduced by 50.0% considering the low-carbon power grid. This study aims to provide practical insights into improving the cradle-to-gate environmental and direct operating-cost performance of the CTP route.

title: From DNA to full-length proteins through nanopore sequencing
abstract: Nanopore protein sequencing has advanced from a theoretical ambition to a practical technology, overcoming major challenges in protein unfolding, transport and signal detection to achieve single-amino-acid and post-translational modification sensitivity. With both full-length and peptide-based approaches progressing towards commercialization, the field is now focused on scaling throughput and refining analysis tools to unlock a new generation of single-molecule proteomics.

title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6-circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

title: Self-Healing Armor Enables Electrode Integrity and Interfacial Stability for Durable Silicon Anodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer coatings are widely used to stabilize silicon anodes, yet repeated volume changes can fracture the coating and accelerate continuous SEI reconstruction. Here, we construct a self-healing fluorinated acrylate/methacrylate copolymer coating in situ on silicon-based anodes through the UV-induced copolymerization of HFBA and MPS. The resulting copolymer combines strong adhesion with dynamic self-recovery through reversible dipole-dipole interactions, enabling microcrack repair within 1 min. Meanwhile, the HFBA-derived segments act as a fluorine reservoir, promoting the formation of a thin SEI with a polymer-rich outer layer and a LiF-rich inner layer. Consequently, SiOx-P(HFBA+MPS)||Li cells deliver 73.5% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 800 mA g–1. A practical 1.5 Ah NCM811||Si/C/Gr-P(HFBA+MPS) pouch cell achieves 71.9% capacity retention after 300 cycles and shows improved thermal safety. This work provides a scalable strategy for durable and safe silicon-based batteries by integrating autonomous self-healing of the polymer coating with sustained fluorine-assisted interphase stabilization.

title: Is this idea from AI or humans? A detector claims it can tell
abstract: A tool called IdeaLens helps to judge whether concepts — rather than just writing — in scientific papers are AI-generated.

title: Coordinated planning and operation of SST-based DC data centers with tiered workload flexibility
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads is making modern data centers increasingly energy-intensive and reliability-critical. This trend not only raises electricity expenditure but also amplifies the economic impact of power interruptions, motivating coordinated planning of power infrastructure and computing resources. Against this background, solid-state transformer (SST)-based DC supply architectures are emerging as a promising direction for next-generation data centers because they provide a controllable interface for integrating diverse energy and computing resources. Under this architectural setting, this paper proposes a coordinated planning and operation framework for SST-based DC data centers with tiered workload flexibility. The framework incorporates nonlinear SST losses into long-term capacity planning, treats tiered workload flexibility as a planning resource, and coordinates energy storage and diesel generators for backup supply during utility outages. An annual bi-level model is formulated to jointly determine the capacities of SST conversion stages, renewable generation, energy storage, diesel generators, and heterogeneous computing servers, together with their scenario-dependent operating decisions. Piecewise linear approximation is used to reformulate the SST loss model, and an enhanced Benders decomposition algorithm is developed to solve the resulting multi-scenario mixed-integer problem. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces total annual cost while satisfying workload service constraints. Further analysis shows that nonlinear SST losses influence capacity configuration, whereas tiered workload flexibility reshapes server deployment and backup resource requirements.

title: Marine Carbonate System Observing and mCDR: New Processes, Needs, and Systems
abstract: Abstract Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.

title: Ground-based spectral irradiance for intra-hour photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Electricity markets worldwide are shortening their settlement intervals, with Australia adopting 5-minute settlement in 2021 and the European Union now mandating a 15-minute imbalance settlement period across Member States. Shorter intervals sharpen the value of accurate intra-hour photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting at the timescale of cloud-induced ramp events, which broadband irradiance cannot fully resolve. In this study, ground-based high-resolution spectroradiometer measurements (213 channels, 350–1052 nm) are exploited as an input to short-horizon PV forecasting for the first time, and the gain is quantified across two climates and multiple years using data from the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS). A SpectralEncoder is introduced, a lightweight 1-D convolutional network applied along the wavelength axis, combined with a physically motivated spectral-ratio representation that decouples spectral shape from broadband magnitude. Performance is evaluated under a dual-dimension framework crossing ramp/non-ramp conditions with clear/intermediate/overcast regimes defined by the clear-sky index. At the primary German site (temperate oceanic; trained 2018–2021, tested 2023), overall RMSE is reduced by 4.4% with spectral inputs, with the largest gain (+9.4%) under overcast ramp conditions, the regime most damaging to grid balancing. At the Australian site (hot desert; trained 2018–2020, tested 2022) the gain is 2.7%, of the same sign as at the German site. A noise-replacement control confirms the gain is driven by genuine spectral structure rather than dimensionality. The contribution is positively signed across forecast horizons from 15 to 90 min, holds across three model families (TCN, LSTM, LightGBM), and is statistically significant under day-block bootstrap ( p < 0.001 ). Post-hoc wavelength-importance analysis localises the signal to visible and near-infrared channels coinciding with known atmospheric absorption features, with cross-site Pearson correlation r = 0.69 . As market clearing intervals shrink and PV penetration rises, ground-based spectral irradiance, already collected at BSRN and collaborative PV testing networks worldwide, is a low-cost, deployable input feature for intra-hour forecasts.

title: Variational Bayes-based multiple neural network method for battery SOC estimation
abstract: Accurate estimation of battery state of charge (SOC) under complex and varying operating conditions remains challenging. This paper proposes a variational Bayes-based multiple neural network (VBMNN) method for battery SOC estimation. Within the proposed algorithm, a hierarchical probabilistic model based on Dirichlet and categorical distributions is constructed to characterize the model indicator vector and model probability vector. Variational Bayesian inference is employed to obtain approximate posterior distributions of the state, model indicator, and model probability vector. The posterior expectation of the model indicator serves as the fusion weight to combine the information provided by different models, thereby forming a single state posterior distribution. Through a pseudo-measurement formulation, neural networks trained under different operating conditions are incorporated into recursive state estimation as measurement models. In addition, a Student’s t noise model with a latent Gamma variable is introduced to mitigate the effects of outliers and non-Gaussian measurement noise. Experimental results obtained from the tested battery show that VBMNN achieves root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 0.40%, 0.49%, and 0.49% under three driving cycles not used for training. After artificial non-Gaussian noise is introduced, the corresponding RMSEs remain below 0.60%, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed algorithm. Additional tests at different temperatures and cross-cell validation further demonstrate its adaptability to operating conditions not encountered during training and to cell-to-cell variations.

title: How display technology adopted quantum dots
abstract: Quantum dots — semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical and electronic properties can be tuned by controlling their size, composition and surface chemistry — have found commercial success for display technologies. Their transition from nanophotonics research into an applied modern nanotechnology exemplifies the bottlenecks that many emerging technologies must overcome on the path to commercialization.

title: How spin-transfer-torque magnetoresistive random access memory bridged spintronics research and the microelectronics industry
abstract: Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory has emerged as a leading non-volatile memory technology replacing embedded Flash in diverse fields including aerospace, automotive and healthcare applications.

title: From a single atom to manufacturable quantum processors in silicon
abstract: Two decades on from the first atomic-scale devices, atom-based silicon quantum computers have progressed from proof of concept to scalable quantum processors that are rapidly gaining commercial traction. What remains is largely a matter of industrial-scale engineering and 3D integration.

title: From nano to technology
abstract: As the journal turns 20, we reflect on the journey nanoscale science has undertaken over the past two decades and how nanoscience-enabled technologies have had a real-world impact.

title: Impact of sub-hourly wind dynamics on green hydrogen yield and electrolyser lifetime
abstract: Direct wind-to-hydrogen systems, in which a wind farm supplies power to an electrolyser without a firm grid connection, must accommodate the full variability of the wind resource, yet many existing techno-economic and design studies rely on input data with temporal resolutions of several minutes to one hour. This coarse averaging can mask short-term power fluctuations that drive electrolyser performance, cycling and degradation. This paper presents a novel wind-to-electrolyser model that synthesises effective wind speed suitable for a power curve wind model at 1 Hz, combining low-frequency trend variation, mesoscale wind speed changes and Kaimal turbulence, validated against aeroelastic simulations. The resulting power output is supplied to a PEM electrolyser model incorporating bank-level thermal dynamics and steady-state, cyclic and on/off degradation, enabling the effect of wind-power variability on long-term electrolyser performance to be quantified. Using 10-year simulations of a wind farm at a site in Orkney, Scotland, two scenarios are investigated: the effect of wind farm size (1–10 turbines) and input temporal resolution (1 s, 1 min, 10 min) on power variability, degradation and hydrogen production; and the effect of turbine configuration for a fixed installed capacity (three 5 MW turbines versus one 15 MW turbine). Results show that coarser temporal resolution substantially overestimates hydrogen production, particularly for small wind farms, where 10-minute-averaged data increase predicted output by up to 428% relative to 1 s data, primarily due to underestimated on/off and cyclic degradation. Aggregating turbines and, to a lesser extent, using larger rotors both smooth the power input and reduce this sensitivity, though the effect remains significant even for 10-turbine farms. These findings demonstrate that high-frequency wind power variability must be explicitly considered in the design and performance assessment of wind-to-hydrogen systems.

title: How single-atom catalysis transformed from a nanoscience curiosity into a new paradigm for heterogeneous catalysis
abstract: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.

title: How lipid nanoparticles evolved from models of biological membranes to systems that enable RNA therapeutics
abstract: Curiosity-driven studies of lipid organization and lipid asymmetry in biological membranes led to scalable methods for making liposomes, efficient loading of drugs and ionizable cationic lipids. In turn, these advances led to lipid nanoparticles enabling the RNA medicine Onpattro and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, and they are now facilitating gene therapies that can potentially treat most human diseases.

title: Unlocking the green power of the North Sea: Identifying key energy infrastructure synergies for 2030 and 2040
abstract: The North Sea will play a key role in providing clean and secure energy for Europe. This not only requires the development of new offshore wind farms, but also their successful integration into the onshore system. In this work we analyze and compare three key integration options and their preferred siting (onshore vs. offshore): grid expansions, electricity storage, and the production, storage and transport of low-carbon hydrogen. We focus on their potential to reduce emissions and energy system costs – individually and in combination with each other. Additionally, we study the consequences of constraints on their implementation. We analyze the years 2030 and 2040, starting from the projections of installed energy infrastructure and demand from the Ten Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) 2022 of the European Network of Transmission System Operators (ENTSO-E). Results show that cross-border electricity grid expansions across the North Sea are a no-regret measure, resulting in significant reductions in system costs and emissions compared to national grid expansions. By comparison, the production, storage and transport of hydrogen have a lower cost and emission reduction potential. In both the short and long term (2030 and 2040), electricity storage can help to reduce emissions, but it is not cost competitive unless emission reduction targets are enforced. Combining the three integration measures at optimal capacities provides additional benefits. Overall, the highest emission reductions can be achieved by combining electricity storage with an expansion of the grid, while the highest economic benefits can be achieved with a combination of grid expansions and hydrogen production for direct use in industry.

title: Where is my graphene battery?
abstract: After years of hype and research, there is still no graphene battery electrode in mass production, but researchers say the material shows promise for energy storage.

title: CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1high Hmgb2+ precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200+ fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1+ G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

title: Facet-Dependent Plating/Stripping Behavior and Crystallographic Evolution during Cycling on Zn Metal Anodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. Here, Zn single-crystal electrodes exposing well-defined (002), (100), and (101) crystalline facets were used to isolate the role of crystallography in Zn metal cycling. Zn deposition is strongly facet-dependent, forming hexagonal, rectangular/prismatic, and corner-defined morphologies on (002), (100), and (101) facets, respectively. Time-dependent SEM further reveals that Zn growth proceeds via discrete edge- or corner-initiated crystallographic units rather than uniform terrace coverage. During stripping, Zn metal is removed via facet-preserved mesoscopic dissolution domains, leaving geometry-defined pits rather than random corrosion-like features. However, these pits are not preferentially refilled during subsequent plating. Repeated cycling redirects Zn growth to protrusions and roughened regions, causing mossy/dendritic accumulation, mixed-texture evolution, and loss of epitaxial reversibility. These findings highlight the need to control both oriented deposition and poststripping surface reconstruction.

title: Overcoming the Trade-off Between the Activity, Stability, and Cost of OER Catalysts for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis in a Self-Driving Laboratory
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, yet its practical deployment is limited by trade-offs among activity, stability, and precursor cost of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. Here, we present a self-driving laboratory (SDL) integrating automated batch synthesis, electrochemical half-cell testing, and AI-guided decision-making to simultaneously optimize these properties. A composition-constrained design space, clustering-based batch selection, and relaxed-percentile Pareto filtering enable efficient exploration of ternary Ir–Ru–X (X = Ni, Co, Fe) systems. Using this framework, the platform conducted 24 experiments per ternary system and identified Ir10Ru65Ni25/C as a Pareto-balanced composition exhibiting an overpotential of 211.8 mV at 10 mA cm–2, limited degradation after accelerated durability testing, and reduced Ir content. In PEMWE, Ir10Ru65Ni25 delivered 3.90 A cm–2 at 1.8 V and stable operation for 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2, demonstrating SDL-driven discovery of multimetallic OER catalysts.

title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-cell genomics enables cell-resolved insights into in-situ microbial communities, yet single amplified genomes (SAGs) are often fragmented, taxonomically ambiguous, and prone to contamination, limiting their biological interpretation. Here, we present Scellmate, a scalable, semi-supervised framework that integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring and SAG–mobilome linkage analysis for large-scale SAG datasets. Following benchmarking of its SAG curation and SAG–eMGE linkage modules using in silico and four-strain mock SAG datasets, respectively, Scellmate was applied to 11,976 sewage-derived SAGs. This approach yielded 4,198 SAGs passing Scellmate’s whole-SAG curation, which captured pronounced heterogeneity masked by bulk methods. At the species level, we resolved extensive hidden diversity within abundant taxa such as Aliarcobacter that was unresolved by matched metagenome-assembled genomes; at the strain level, we pinpointed a distinct Agathobacter rectalis cluster carrying specialized carbon-utilization pathways, suggesting niche differentiation. Leveraging these curated SAGs, we identified 6,474 host–mobilome linkages across 2,378 SAGs; these linkages not only showed high concordance with host-association data within the Integrated Microbial Genomes (IMG) system but also significantly expanded species-level host assignments. Furthermore, we detected frequent inter-species sharing patterns of diverse cryptic plasmids within the order Bacteroidales. Together, this work demonstrates that high-throughput single-cell genomics, empowered by the robust framework, resolves fine-scale heterogeneity and host–mobilome dynamics, advancing culture-independent microbiome research.

title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H 2 O 2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O 2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O 2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp 2 ‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H 2 O 2 selectivity, and improved 2e − ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H 2 O 2 production rate of 27.8 mol g −1 h −1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O 2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.

title: Bioorthogonal Vitamin C Probes Enable Cellular Profiling and Investigation of Lysine Vitcylation
abstract: ABSTRACT Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.

title: Near Infrared Photoswitching by Direct Excitation—A Next Frontier
abstract: ABSTRACT The field of molecular photoswitches has grown tremendously over the past decades and pervaded every applied field from chemistry, biology, physics, to materials science and beyond. A main driver for continuous progress is tailoring absorption properties as a fundamental tool for controlling the light response. So far, the shift of absorption from UV light addressability into lower‐energy visible and red spectral regions has unlocked numerous unique opportunities, both in capability increase as well as in applicability of photoswitches. A next frontier has been opened more recently by extreme redshifting of absorption, allowing to enter the near‐infrared (NIR) spectral realm via direct excitation. This minireview highlights these important developments, delineates design principles to achieve NIR responsiveness in molecular photoswitches, and showcases the specific benefits that come with such low‐energy light control over molecular states. The outlook glimpses into the future and points out the particular opportunities and challenges ahead.

title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β ‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu 2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional bex ‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni 2+ and Co 2+ , affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO 2 /CO electroreduction to CH 4 . This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

title: Double‐Volcano Catalytic Response in Furfural Reductive Amination Over Inverse Ni─Al Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT Reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones to primary amines is an important route for biomass valorization, yet achieving efficient synergy between substrate and hydrogen activation in cascade reactions remains challenging. Herein, we construct a compositionally tunable Ni─Al catalyst system whose architecture evolves from conventional Ni/Al 2 O 3 to inverse Al 2 O 3 /Ni. This structural evolution gives rise to an unusual double‐volcano catalytic behavior in furfural reductive amination. Two activity maxima are identified over 30Ni/Al 2 O 3 and inverse Al 2 O 3 /90Ni, respectively, with the optimal Al 2 O 3 /90Ni catalyst delivering 98.5% furfurylamine yield and a space‐time yield of 65 mmol g cat −1 h −1 under mild conditions. Adsorption studies, initial‐rate kinetic isotope effect and reaction‐order measurements, apparent activation‐energy analysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy indicate that the double‐volcano behavior reflects the coupled evolution of catalyst composition and architecture and a composition‐dependent balance between Lewis‐acid‐assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen‐dependent intermediate conversion. Hydrogen‐dependent steps exert a stronger kinetic influence over 30Ni/Al 2 O 3 than over Al 2 O 3 /90Ni, while the inverse catalyst exhibits enhanced H 2 adsorption and activation and more rapid Schiff base conversion. These results indicate a shift in the dominant kinetic limitation between the two catalysts and provide a framework for designing efficient non‐noble‐metal catalysts for multifunctional cascade reactions involving coupled substrate and hydrogen activation.

title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O 2 ‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO 2+ ) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO 2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O 2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O 2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

title: A Z‐Scheme CuWO 4 /Poly(heptazine imide) Interface Coupled With Asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + Sites Enables Efficient Photocatalytic CO 2 ‐to‐Ethanol Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective photocatalytic reduction of CO 2 into multicarbon products remains challenging because constructing uniform C─C coupling centers while maintaining their stability under reaction conditions is difficult. Here, we report a Z‐scheme CuWO 4 /poly(heptazine imide) heterojunction featuring asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites for CO 2 ‐to‐ethanol conversion. Site‐selective oxygen vacancies in CuWO 4 trigger generation of structurally identical, charge‐asymmetric neighboring Cu sites, which enhance CO 2 activation and stabilize adjacent *CO intermediates, thereby facilitating C─C bond formation. Meanwhile, an atomically bonded O─W─N heterointerface enables directional Z‐scheme charge transfer, supplying photogenerated electrons to the CuWO 4 surface and stabilizing the asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites throughout photocatalysis. Consequently, the optimized photocatalyst achieves an ethanol production rate of 244.5 µmol g −1 h −1 in pure water without sacrificial reagents. Advanced synchrotron spectroscopies identify the asymmetric Cu 2+ /Cu + dual sites and the chemically bonded heterointerface, while operando spectroscopies record the dynamic evolution of active sites and the * CO─ * CO coupling pathways upon illumination. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the synergy between asymmetric catalytic centers and the atomically bonded heterointerface promotes the C─C coupling process. This work establishes a strategy for constructing and stabilizing asymmetric catalytic centers through atomic engineering of crystal structure and heterointerface, providing a photocatalyst design paradigm for selective multicarbon solar fuel synthesis.

title: Sterically Shielded Heavy‐Atom Strategy for Constructing Narrowband Pure‐Green MR‐TADF Emitters With Concentration‐Quenching Resistance and Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing
abstract: ABSTRACT Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates ( k RISC ) of these materials lead to pronounced aggregation‐caused quenching and significant efficiency roll‐off. Here, we propose a sterically shielded heavy‐atom strategy that simultaneously suppresses detrimental π–π stacking, accelerates k RISC , and reinforces the rigidity of the conjugated framework to retain narrowband emission. The proof‐of‐concept emitters BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN‐FLSSe achieves rapid k RISC of 4.2 × 10 6 s −1 , maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non‐sensitized OLEDs based on BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show pure‐green electroluminescence with CIE y coordinates exceeding 0.70, high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max s) of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs, maintaining EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m −2 , respectively. Impressively, even at high doping concentration of 30 wt%, these devices retain high EQE max s of 30.7%–33.1% with virtually unchanged emission spectra.

title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na 0.44 MnO 2 , where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na 0.44 MnO 2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

title: Mixed‐Valence Dimeric Olympicenyl Radical Cation With Improved Electrical Conductivity
abstract: ABSTRACT p‐Type doping is an effective strategy for modulating molecular packing arrangement of organic compounds, thus improving their electrical conductivity. In this work, the first example of a mixed‐valence radical cation dimer based on an odd alternant hydrocarbon, [OR5] 2 +• [FeCl 4 ] − (OR5‐MV), was successfully prepared by the oxidation of olympicenyl radical (OR) derivative OR5 using FeCl 3 . X‐ray crystallographic analysis revealed that cation‐radical dimer [OR5] 2 +• , acting as a fundamental building block, forms [OR5] 4 2+ tetramer via a multi‐center–two‐electron bond, which further aggregates into a one‐dimensional chain in the solid state. SQUID measurement reveals that the magnetic susceptibility is dominated by the FeCl 4 – anions with no detectable OR5 moiety contribution. Theoretical calculations disclosed an open‐shell singlet ground state for [OR5] 4 2+ tetramer and demonstrated that the pancake‐bond formation between OR5 cation‐radical dimers confers significant energetic stabilization. Compared to the neutral compound, more uniform molecular packing and reduced intermolecular distance in the one‐dimensional columnar architecture of OR5‐MV facilitate effective intermolecular orbital overlap, leading to broader band dispersion along the molecular stacking direction. A substantially improved electrical conductivity of up to 10 − 3 S cm − 1 is achieved compared to neutral radical (10 − 9 S cm − 1 ), representing the highest value reported for monomeric odd alternant hydrocarbons.

title: Self‐Calibrated Luminescence Sensing Under Pressure in a Hybrid Manganese Halide
abstract: ABSTRACT Hybrid organic‐inorganic manganese halides have emerged as a promising class of emitters, owing to their excellent optical properties, low toxicity, and rich structural diversity. However, achieving site‐specific control over their high‐pressure optical response remains a great challenge. In this study, we report a zero‐dimensional manganese chloride, (HIm) 6 [MnCl 4 ∙MnCl 6 ] (HIm = imidazolium), which concurrently incorporates both tetrahedral and octahedral Mn 2 + centers within a single lattice. Under pressure, the red emission of [MnCl 6 ] 4− exhibits a pronounced and linear redshift and intensity attenuation. However, the green emission of [MnCl 4 ] 2− remains stable in both peak position and intensity, serving as a rigid energetic anchor. By leveraging the invariant green emission as an internal reference and the pressure‐sensitive red emission as a probe, a self‐calibrated pressure sensing system is achieved. Synchrotron high‐pressure x‐ray diffraction, in situ optical spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that this decoupled response originates from the large structural compressibility of the [MnCl 6 ] 4− octahedra and high rigidity of the [MnCl 4 ] 2− tetrahedra. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid organic‐inorganic crystals represent a promising class of self‐calibrated optical sensing materials for next‐generation metrology.

title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O 2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well‐defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular‐level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage‐angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o ‐TPDA‐COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments.
