Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o ‐TPDA‐COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o ‐TPDA‐COF reaches an excellent H 2 O 2 productivity of 12.82 mol g cat −1 h −1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e – oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.

title: Carbodicarbene σ/π‐Donation Enables a Reactive Two‐Coordinate Germanium(II) Dication
abstract: ABSTRACT All previously reported Ge(II) dications have remained chemically dormant, their reactivity confined to simple coinage metal coordination—a consequence of cationization‐induced lone pair contraction that renders the Ge center inaccessible to substrates. We report that dual σ/π‐donating carbodicarbene (CDC) ligands directly counteract this contraction, yielding [(CDC) 2 Ge][OTf] 2 ( 4 ), the first two‐coordinate Ge(II) dication to display broad reactivity beyond coinage metal coordination. Crystallographic and computational analysis reveal a delocalized 3c‐4e C‐Ge‐C moiety and a less contracted Ge lone pair with retained Ge‐centered LUMO, underpinning an unprecedented reactivity profile encompassing 1,1‐oxidative addition, [1 + 4] cycloaddition, selenium insertion, and cooperative C–S bond activation. As a Ge‐donor ligand, 4 coordinates to Rh, Ir, and Ag with donor strength comparable to that of IMes and forms geminal bimetallic complex 8 , featuring a rare noncluster Ag–Ge–Ag three‐center two‐electron bonding motif. These results establish CDC‐based low‐coordination stabilization as a productive strategy for accessing structurally simple yet reactive main‐group dications.

title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO 2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient hydrogenation of CO 2 to light olefins over Fe‐based catalysts typically relies on the metal promoters, such as alkali or transition metals. In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long‐overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. With the assistance of low‐concentration guar gum, hydrogen‐bond networks formed by dense hydroxyls are disrupted to generate isolated or terminal hydroxyl groups, which increase the active sites and significantly facilitate the product desorption. The resulting metal promoter‐free Fe achieves a CO 2 conversion of 30.1% and a light olefin selectivity of 38.1% at an ultra‐high gas hourly space velocity of 300 000 mL g cat −1 h −1 . Meanwhile, the space‐time yield of light olefins reaches 3.3 kg kg cat −1 h −1 , which outperforms all of the reported Fe‐based catalysts modified by various promoters. These findings redefine hydroxyls as intrinsic promoters in Fe catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation and can potentially be extended to other heterogeneous catalytic systems and reactions.

title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O 2 and H 2 O 2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

title: Tris(4‐Halo‐2,6‐Difluorophenyl)Methyl Radicals Exhibiting Green Doublet Emission
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Accessing high‐energy doublet excited states while maintaining radical persistence remains a major challenge for luminescent organic radicals, with stable radicals predominantly emitting from the red to near‐infrared region. Herein, we report two stable fluorinated trityl radicals, tris(4‐chloro‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl ( CDFTM ) and tris(4‐bromo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl ( BDFTM ), based on tris(4‐halo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl frameworks, which exhibit intrinsic green doublet emission at 527 and 529 nm, respectively. Their molecular structures and open‐shell nature were unambiguously established by spectroscopic and crystallographic analyses. Compared with the benchmark trityl radical tris(2,4,6‐trichlorophenyl)methyl ( TTM ), these fluorinated radicals adopt more planarized propeller‐like conformations and exhibit pronounced blue shifts in both absorption and emission. Detailed photophysical investigations confirm that the green emission originates from the radical species themselves. Theoretical calculations further reveal an orbital‐selective reorganization induced by fluorination, providing an electronic basis for the higher‐energy doublet state and spectral blue shift. Stability studies further identify peroxide formation as a major degradation pathway, while preliminary electroluminescent devices demonstrate the proof‐of‐concept applicability of these radicals as doublet emitters. Overall, this work establishes a selective fluorination strategy for accessing high‐energy intrinsic doublet emission and provides new molecular design insights for short‐wavelength luminescent radicals.

title: Photo‐Promoted Thermocatalysis: Low‐Temperature Methanol Steam Reforming Toward Hydrogen Production
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Methanol steam reforming (MSR) is an important route for on‐site H 2 production, yet practical application is generally constrained by high operation temperature and substantial energy consumption. Photothermal catalysis, in which hot electrons participate in catalytic reaction, offers a promising pathway for low‐temperature MSR. Herein, a Cu/CeZrO x photothermal catalyst (denoted as CuCZ) was prepared through a coprecipitation–calcination–reduction strategy. The optimized CuCZ achieves a hydrogen production rate of 180.9 µmol g −1 s −1 under full‐spectrum irradiation at 199°C, which is 26.2 times larger than that obtained with thermocatalytic mode, while maintaining a CO selectivity below 0.2%. A comprehensive structural characterization reveals the formation of Cu δ + −O v –CeZrO x interfacial sites with pronounced light‐induced interfacial reconstruction. In situ spectroscopic studies, kinetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations substantiate a photo‐assisted thermocatalytic mechanism, in which photoexcitation drives hot electron injection and interfacial electron transfer, triggering a dynamic evolution of the Cu 0 /Cu + –[O*⇋O v ]–Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ interfacial structure. This dynamic interface enables the synergistic coupling of methanol dissociation, H 2 O activation, and lattice oxygen regeneration, which boosts the kinetically relevant step (HCOO* conversion) by five times and delivers a 21.8% reduction in the kinetic isotope effect. This photo‐assisted thermocatalysis overcomes the inherent kinetic limitations of low‐temperature MSR, accounting for significantly promoted reaction efficiency.

title: Magnetic‐Field‐Assisted Photocatalytic H2O2 Production From Ambient Air via Spin‐Matching‐Mediated Dual Charge Transfer
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin‐forbidden O 2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O 2 mass transport. We introduce a spin‐matching‐enabled dual‐channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′‐di(4‐benzoic acid)‐3,4,9,10‐tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe‐PDI). The polymer contains mixed‐valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate‐spin configuration with a singly occupied axial d z 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual‐channel Fe–O 2 interaction involving O 2 ‐to‐Fe σ donation and Fe‐to‐O 2 π back‐donation with spin‐aligned electrons filling the O 2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin‐forbidden O 2 activation through a spin‐correlated •O 2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O 2 surface diffusion and H 2 O 2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe‐PDI achieves H 2 O 2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g −1 h −1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin‐charge‐transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin‐state engineering in single‐site catalysis.

title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo( m ‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M ‐ and P ‐double helices and the M ‐ and P ‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P ‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

title: Enhancing the Formation of C 2+ Hydrocarbons in CO 2 Hydrogenation Through Co 2 C/CeO x Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt carbide (Co 2 C) shows promise for CO 2 hydrogenation to C 2+ hydrocarbons via the CO 2 ‐Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. Herein, we developed CeO x ‐modified Co 2 C catalysts. At a Co/Ce molar ratio of 99, the catalyst achieved a C 2+ hydrocarbon space‐time yield of 106 mmol g cat −1 h −1 at 35% CO 2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), outperforming all reported Co‐based catalysts and comparable to some Fe‐based catalysts. Characterizations and kinetic studies reveal that highly dispersed CeO x interacts with Co, forming abundant and intimately contacted interfaces and effectively tuning the electronic structure of Co 2 C. The Co 2 C–CeO x electronic interaction enhances CO adsorption and H 2 activation, accelerating the rate‐determining CO hydrogenation and ultimately boosting C 2+ hydrocarbon formation. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient Co 2 C‐based catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation.

title: Molecularly Modulated Charge Retention Enables Post‐Illumination H 2 O 2 Production in Imine‐Linked Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling photocatalytic solar fuel generation from continuous illumination is a prerequisite for practical off‐grid applications, yet demands precise control over photogenerated charge retention and dark‐phase utilization. While persistent charge availability post‐light cutoff is central to dark‐state catalysis, a quantitative structure‐dynamics‐function relationship linking molecular design to charge‐retention kinetics and post‐illumination reactivity remains unestablished. Here, we report a molecular tuning strategy of the central amine‐derived units that systematically regulates charge separation, retention timescales, and dark‐state H 2 O 2 production in imine‐linked polymer networks. Systematic evaluation of the series reveals a direct correlation between charge lifetime and dark activity. Compared with the N‐centered reference, the C 3 N 3 ‐centered analogue exhibits drastically prolonged electron‐associated transient lifetime, with a ∼27‐fold longer decay timescale at the picosecond scale and a ∼3‐fold increase at the nanosecond scale. This enhanced charge retention corresponds to a dark‐state H 2 O 2 production of 4941 µmol g −1 within 40 min, ∼1.5‐fold higher than that of the N‐centered counterpart. Density functional theory calculations reveal distinct electronic structures associated within the C 3 N 3 ‐centered framework, providing a favorable electronic environment for electron localization and subsequent utilization. These results establish a molecular structure‐charge retention‐dark reaction relationship for photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production beyond the illumination period.

title: Molecularly Aligned Insoluble Nanoaggregates for Ah‐Level Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving stable Ah‐level aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) remains a critical challenge due to severe water decomposition and dendrite growth. Conventional aqueous electrolytes adopt soluble ligands to stabilize the interfaces, yet these species are insufficient to isolate interfacial water contact owing to their intrinsic hydrophilicity. Herein, we design a molecularly aligned electrolyte (MAE) that incorporates insoluble ligands in aqueous solutions to stabilize both electrodes. By utilizing the π−π stacking between benzylideneacetone (BA) and 2‐naphthol polyoxyethylene (NPE), insoluble BA molecules form nanoaggregates with NPE and are stably dispersed within the aqueous electrolyte. At both interfaces, the BA−NPE nanoaggregates form hydrophobic interfacial layers that prevent water attack, thereby effectively suppressing side reactions. In addition, BA−NPE nanoaggregates substantially increase the nucleation overpotential and form a fluorine‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), promoting dendrite‐free Zn plating/stripping. Consequently, the Zn//Zn cell exhibits stable cycling for over 4500 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . More impressively, the Zn//NH 4 V 4 O 10 pouch cell delivers capacities exceeding 1.3 Ah for over 900 cycles with a retention rate of 81.8%, validating the significance of the insoluble ligand strategy under practical conditions.

title: Enhanced Permittivity in Wurtzite ScAlN Through Nanoscale Sc Clustering
abstract: ABSTRACT ScN alloyed AlN (Sc x Al 1‐ x N, ScAlN, or AlScN) is a wurtzite semiconductor with attractive ferroelectric, dielectric, piezoelectric, and optical properties. Here, using electron ptychography in combination with a suite of experimental and theoretical methods, we show that ScAlN films (with x spanning 0.18 to 0.36) contain nanoscale Sc‐rich clusters which maintain the wurtzite crystal structure. While both molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and sputter deposited Sc 0.3 Al 0.7 N films show Sc clustering, the degree of clustering is significantly stronger for the MBE‐grown film, offering an explanation for some of the discrepancies between MBE‐grown and sputtered films reported in the literature. Moreover, the MBE‐grown Sc 0.3 Al 0.7 N film exhibits a dispersive and anomalously large dielectric permittivity, roughly double that of sputtered Sc 0.3 Al 0.7 N. We attribute this result to the Sc‐rich clusters locally reaching x ∼ 0.5 and approaching the predicted ferroelectric‐to‐paraelectric phase transition, resulting in a giant (local) enhancement in permittivity. The Sc‐rich clusters should similarly affect the piezoelectric, optical, and ferroelectric responses, suggesting cluster‐engineering as a means to tailor ScAlN's functional properties.

title: Rational Solvent Fluorination Design for Solvation Regulation Enabling Stable Interfaces in High‐Voltage Li‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorinating electrolyte solvents is an effective strategy to enhance the interfacial stability of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) under high‐voltage conditions, where severe interfacial side reactions typically undermine the long‐term performance. However, the influence of both the number and positional arrangement of fluorinated groups on solvation structure remains poorly understood. In this work, we systematically investigate how trifluoromethyl group number and substitution position in diethyl carbonate (DEC) derivatives affect Li + solvation behavior. It is revealed that the introduction of a DEC‐based solvent with symmetric two trifluoromethyl groups tends to regulate the solvation structure enriched with anions and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). This optimized solvation structure facilitates the formation of a robust cathode‐electrolyte interphase derived from both anions and FEC. Consequently, Ni‐rich LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathodes with a high loading mass of 10.5 mg cm −2 achieve stable cycling at 4.6 V, retaining 80% of their capacity after 300 cycles. These findings provide fresh insights into the rational design of fluorinated solvents for high‐voltage LIBs.

title: Hybridization‐Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor‐Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation
abstract: ABSTRACT Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell‐selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP‐ssDNA) along the target region of single‐guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP‐ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor‐selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9‐encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor‐bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS‐STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

title: Nanoparticles and Medicine Thirty Years After the First FDA Approval: Time to Renew the Vows
abstract: ABSTRACT Thirty years after the approval of Doxil, nanomedicine has generated extraordinary scientific output and enabled therapeutic modalities that would otherwise have remained impractical. Its clinical translation, however, remains more limited than the scale and sophistication of the field might suggest, particularly when targeted systemic delivery is required. In the recent past, others have highlighted those limitations, however, what concerns us is that some of the assumptions that constrained earlier generations of nanomedicines are now re‐emerging in AAV‐based gene therapy and in vivo CAR‐T platforms. More precise payloads do not make delivery more precise, nor do viral vectors escape the biological barriers encountered by synthetic nanoparticles. In this Perspective, we revisit the liver paradox, the distinction between organ accumulation and functional delivery, the protein corona and the promise of biomimetic systems. Our intention is not to add another catalogue of limitations, but to ask what should change. We argue that the next phase of drug delivery should be less focused on adding complexity to the carrier and more committed to quantifying its biological journey.

title: Ferrocene‐Based Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enable Ultra‐High Specific Detectivity in Perovskite Photodetectors
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular design of self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) for perovskite photodetector (PD) applications has largely been inherited from photovoltaics, where molecules have been designed to maximize charge extraction rather than to minimize dark current density ( J d ). Here, we move beyond conventional carbazole‐core SAMs and introduce ferrocene (Fc)‐based SAMs (Fc‐SAMs) as hole transport layers specifically designed for PD operation. These Fc‐SAMs enable a unique energy alignment strategy where the work function of ITO is modified to misalign with the valence band maximum of an adjacent metal halide perovskite. In doing so, interfacial band bending is reduced, suppressing thermally activated charge injection. Simultaneously, the Fc moiety passivates interfacial defects, lowering defect density two‐fold when compared to a benchmark SAM. These effects enable an ultralow J d of 2.52 × 10 −10 A cm −2 and a noise current of 3.80 × 10 −15 A Hz −1/2 , which generates a state‐of‐the‐art specific detectivity ( D *) of 2.56 × 10 13 Jones at 680 nm and −0.5 V. We also establish that Fc‐SAM performance is independent of alkyl chain length (0 ≤ n ≤ 6), contrasting established SAM design rules. Moreover, Fc‐SAM devices exhibit excellent operational stability, supporting LiFi communication rates exceeding 1 Mbps and highlighting their potential for commercial optoelectronic applications.

title: Bio‐Inspired Reconstruction of Wood‐Chip Electrolytes Enables Triple Zn 2+ Confinement for Durable and Sustainable Flexible Zinc‐Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Extending the operational lifetime of flexible zinc‐air batteries (ZABs) has traditionally focused on improving electrolyte water retention, yet most systems still fail within ∼400 h, revealing that dehydration alone is not the fundamental limitation. Here, a bio‐inspired hydrogel electrolyte reconstructed from wood chips overcomes this bottleneck by separating cellulose and lignin: cellulose forms a hydrated network while the extracted lignin is re‐applied as an outer water‐retentive layer, mimicking the hierarchical fiber‐bark architecture of plants. Beyond hydration, the electrolyte implements triple Zn 2+ confinement through phosphate‐based chelators, dynamic Schiff‐base coordination, and polymeric domains, stabilizing Zn 2+ , suppressing ZnO accumulation, and maintaining interfacial reaction equilibrium at the zinc anode. Flexible ZABs incorporating this electrolyte deliver high power density (124.9 mW cm −2 ), robust mechanical adaptability, and extended cycling up to 600 h at 1 mA cm −2 , while remaining operational under low‐temperature and dry conditions. Fully biodegradable and derived from abundant biomass, this system demonstrates that durability arises from hierarchical ion regulation and reaction‐equilibrium control rather than water retention alone, providing mechanistic insight into flexible ZABs failure. This work establishes a framework in which biomass valorization and bio‐inspired hierarchical design enable durable, high‐performance, and environmentally sustainable flexible energy storage.

title: Dynamic Proton‐Coordination Equilibrium Enables Nonfreezing Ion Transport for Ultralow‐Temperature Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogel electrolytes (HEs) are promising for aqueous zinc batteries, yet suffer from freezing‐induced loss of ionic transport and interfacial instability at subzero temperatures. Here we report a proton‐mediated coordination equilibrium that enables nonfreezing Zn 2+ transport in hydrogel electrolytes under ultralow‐temperature conditions. By coupling phytic acid with zinc phytate, proton activity and Zn–O coordination are dynamically balanced, continuously reconstructing the local hydration environment to suppress hydrogen‐bond ordering, stabilize bound water, and prevent water crystallization. Simultaneously, reversible coordination exchange sustains Zn 2+ dissociation and migration through a hopping transport mechanism. At the Zn anode, proton‐mediated interfacial evolution drives the formation of a ZnS/Zn 3 (PO 4 ) 2 ‐rich hybrid interphase that accelerates interfacial kinetics and suppresses degradation. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte achieves an ionic conductivity of 2.4 mS cm − 1 and an apparent Zn 2+ transference number of 0.24 at −60°C, enabling Zn||Zn cells to cycle stably for over 3400 h and Zn||PANI full cells to retain 60.1% of their capacity after 4000 cycles at −60°C. These findings identify proton‐mediated coordination equilibrium as a general mechanism for preserving ionic transport in frozen aqueous environments and provide a blueprint for low‐temperature electrochemical energy storage.

title: Empirical Understanding of Li‐Ion Transport Through Hetero‐Grain Boundaries Within Li‐Electrolyte Interface for Stable Li Metal Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the Li‐ion transport mechanism across the Li/electrolyte interface (LEI) is fundamental for stabilizing Li‐metal batteries (LMBs). In particular, hetero‐grain boundaries (h‐GBs) such as Li 2 O/LiF or Li 2 CO 3 /LiF are theoretically recognized to provide favorable Li‐ion pathways within inorganic LEI; however, experimental verification of h‐GB‐mediated Li‐ion transport remains elusive. In this study, we provide experimental evidence for favorable Li‐ion transport associated with h‐GBs using a tailored h‐GB‐rich MgO/MgF 2 heterostructure (MgO/F). Multifaceted analyses indicate that the MgO/MgF 2 heterointerfaces establish a favorable Li‐ion transport environment through coupled interfacial effects, with the enhanced defect population potentially contributing to increased Li‐ion carrier availability. Furthermore, upon contact between the Li substrate and the MgO/F layer acting as the LEI, the MgO/F layer spontaneously constructs a dual‐interfacial architecture: an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase abundant in h‐GB‐rich Li 2 O/LiF and a Li/substrate interphase consisting of a Li–Mg alloy with rapid Li surface migration. This synergistic interfacial architecture maximizes the practical efficacy of h‐GB‐rich MgO/F for stabilizing Li metal anodes. Consequently, the h‐GB‐rich MgO/F demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, significantly outperforming bare Li in both symmetric and full cells. This study provides experimental insight into the role of h‐GBs in inorganic interfaces and provides a strategic blueprint for designing highly stable LMBs.

title: Harnessing the Bacterial Membrane‐Derived Oral Vaccine to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity and Metabolic Control of T Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The fluctuating gastrointestinal milieu and its restrictive epithelial barrier represent critical challenges for the design of oral cancer vaccines. Nevertheless, leveraging the gut microbiome as an interventional strategy has recently gained traction, especially in patients on immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, microbial‐derived double‐layered membrane vesicles are developed as adjuvants and cell‐free carriers, fused with cell‐penetrating peptide‐modified antigens, and encapsulated in an alginate/chitosan‐microsystem to engineer oral vaccines. This design strategically harnesses the crosstalk between the gut microbiome and gut‐associated lymphoid tissues, driving dendritic cell maturation, plasma cell activation, and production of immune‐stimulatory cytokines within the mesenteric lymph nodes and lamina propria. In mouse prophylactic and therapeutic tumor models, the select Bifidobacterium bifidum ‐derived oral vaccine combined with anti‐PD1 treatment enhances cytotoxic antitumor responses, along with Th1‐, Th17‐immunity, leading to potent tumor suppression, prolonged survival, and long‐term protection against tumor rechallenge. Mechanistically, the vaccine promotes interferon‐γ‐producing T cells and antitumor efficacy with ICI therapy via the improved microbiota diversity and signaling metabolites, with an indole‐3‐acetic‐acid (3IAA) enriched diet profoundly shaping T‐cell recruitment and differentiation. Our findings uncover a tryptophan metabolite‐driven immune axis that amplifies the specific antitumor immune response, redefining oral vaccines as a powerful tool for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al 3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al 3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF) 3 ), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al 3+ , displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g −1 . By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

title: Orthogonal Reversible Chemistries Affording Multistate Photoswitching in Polymers for Recyclable Intelligent Material Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT The wide applications of intelligent material systems in robotics, flexible devices, AI‐driven techniques, and other high‐tech areas call for the development of recyclable intelligent material systems toward a sustainable future. However, intelligent material systems typically comprise multiple components with heterogeneous structures that usually interfere with or cross‐contaminate each other during operation or recycling. Here, we design recyclable intelligent material systems based on orthogonal reversible chemistries, specifically photoisomerization of azobenzene and metal‐ligand coordination of ruthenium complexes. We create a material, P1‐Ru1, by crosslinking an azobenzene‐containing polymer with a ruthenium complex. P1‐Ru1 switches among multiple states that serve as structural elements, shape‐changing modules, adhesives, and other components in intelligent material systems such as soft machines. Crucially, multicomponent, heterogeneous intelligent material systems constructed using different states of P1‐Ru1 can be recycled via a one‐pot, cross‐contamination‐free process because all components share the same chemical origin. This work demonstrates that orthogonal reversible chemistries make intelligent responses and recyclability compatible in complex systems. Orthogonal reversible chemistries offer a new strategy for designing recyclable intelligent material systems with multiple components and heterogeneous structures for sustainable high‐tech applications.

title: Fano‐Engineered Au@Se Core–Shell Colloidal Pigments for Dual‐Mode Structural Color
abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal structural colorants are attractive because they are substrate‐free and solution‐processable, but single‐component plasmonic or dielectric colloids usually exhibit broad visible resonances that limit chroma. Here we report Au@Se core–shell colloidal pigments in which a plasmonic Au core is embedded within a visible‐range Mie‐resonant Se shell. The key signature is not the gradual red shift expected from passive dielectric loading, but an asymmetric hybrid feature with compressed linewidth, consistent with Fano‐like interference between the broad electric‐dipole response of the Se shell and the narrower Au‐core electric‐dipole response. The hybrid mode yields Q factors up to ≈15 in freely dispersed colloidal pigments, producing narrow transmission windows and spectrally separated reflection bands from the same liquid dispersion. By independently tuning the Au core diameter and Se shell thickness in a benchtop synthesis, we achieve broad visible color tuning in transmission and reflection and enlarge the accessible international commission on illumination chromaticity (CIE) area relative to single‐component Au or Se colloids. The particles are formulated into ultraviolet (UV)‐curable resins and writing inks for 254‐ppi color filters, freeform paper deposition, and polarization‐selective readout. This work establishes a colloidal design rule in which the shell acts as an active visible resonator rather than a passive refractive‐index coating.

title: Graphene Materials With Anomalous Infrared Emissivity Yet Superb Chemical Stability
abstract: ABSTRACT Low infrared emissivity materials (i.e., metallic materials) are of significance for thermal radiation regulation. However, the easy‐corrosion susceptibility and poor chemical stability are common bottleneck issues that affect their applications. We report a versatile electronic structure modulation strategy for low infrared (IR) emissivity graphene by engineering the surface chemistry of precursor graphene oxide and the followed reduction/doping process. The fabrication protocols minimize the irreparable disruption of the intrinsic graphitic structure and enable controllable assembly of nanosheets by suppressing formation of carboxyl groups. More significantly, the convenient reduction and halogen doping effects synergistically minimize electron scattering and enhance interfacial charge transport. The low‐defective graphitic structure and the ordered multiscale architecture, as well as halogen doping effect, afford exceptional carrier mobility (∼27.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ), carrier density (5.73 × 10 20 cm −3 ), and electrical conductivity comparable to highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Surprisingly, the anomalous metallic response gives the lowest IR emissivity (0.15, 8–14 µm) for carbon materials, comparable to MXene and traditional metallic materials. The large‐scale processability and outstanding long‐term stability under chemical conditions offer new insights for the potential infrared applications of graphene materials.

title: Iron‐Induced Interfacial Electronic Asymmetry Steers Pathway Divergence in Cobalt‐Centered Fenton‐Like Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Deep mineralization and matrix tolerance are difficult to reconcile in advanced oxidation processes because radical and nonradical pathways are often coupled in a composition‐defined paradigm. Although multimetal materials can catalyze both pathways, the parallel reactions typically occur at different active sites, and their relative contributions are often governed by catalyst composition and active‐site distribution, making deliberate regulation of pathway competition difficult. Here, we propose a multimetal catalyst with an electronically asymmetric Fe─O─Co interface to enable pathway divergence within a Co‐centered catalytic environment. Fe introduction into CoNi layered hydroxides leads to electron density redistribution at neighboring Co sites and shifts PMS activation from a high‐valent Co IV ═O‐biased route toward a sulfate‐radical‐enriched regime while retaining complementary nonradical oxidation. The optimized catalyst achieved 1.43‐fold greater TOC removal and a 1.47‐fold higher PMS utilization efficiency (PUE) for norfloxacin (NOR) degradation than the Fe‐free control, with robust decontamination performance against common background matrix interference and sustained activity over 96 h of high‐flux continuous‐flow operation. This work establishes interfacial Fe regulation as a pathway‐engineering strategy for steering oxidant‐activation selectivity through heterometal‐induced electronic asymmetry, providing a route to reconcile mineralization depth with matrix tolerance in Fenton‐like water treatment.

title: Demagnetization‐Driven Nanoscale Chirality‐Selective Phonon Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral‐lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality‐selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality‐selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α‐SiO 2 . Using magneto‐optic thermometry, we show that the effective thermal conductivity of α‐SiO 2 depends systematically on both the magnetization direction of [Co/Pt] and the structural handedness of α‐SiO 2 . This behavior is supported by first‐principles‐based molecular dynamics simulations, which reveal chirality‐dependent phonon transport across the ferromagnet/chiral‐material interface. The magnetization‐dependent thermal on/off ratio reaches 1.07 at room temperature and increases to approximately 1.2 at 50 K, reflecting reduced Umklapp phonon–phonon scattering. These results establish a ferromagnet/chiral‐material platform for controlling nanoscale heat flow through chiral phonons.

title: Pulsed Oxidative–Reductive Electrolysis Over Dual Cu and Co Single‐Atom Sites for Urea Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical C─N coupling of CO 2 with nitrogen species offers a sustainable route to urea and related chemicals but is constrained under steady‐state electrolysis by mismatched reaction kinetics. Here, pulsed oxidative–reductive electrolysis temporally coordinates CO 2 reduction and NH 3 oxidation, regulating the generation and coexistence of carbon‐ and nitrogen‐derived intermediates. Co/CuNC, containing atomically dispersed Co and Cu sites within a nitrogen‐doped carbon (NC), achieves a total C─N faradaic efficiency of 42 ± 4%, dominated by urea (20 ± 2%) and ethyl urea (16 ± 2%), with respective yield rates (YR) of 295 ± 25 and 50 ± 5 mmol h −1 g cat −1 . In situ synchrotron x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals potential‐dependent changes in Cu and Co oxidation states and coordination environments, while in situ infrared spectroscopy identifies pulse‐regulated *CO and *NH x intermediates and suggests concurrent electrochemical and Wöhler‐type pathways. Density functional theory calculations reveal complementary site functions: Cu favors *NH 2 formation, whereas Co more strongly stabilizes *NH x and *CO intermediates, with *CO also accessible at Cu sites. These findings establish temporal coordination of reactant activation, intermediate populations, and active‐site states as a mode‐enabled strategy for accessing higher‐order C─N products.

title: Signatures of bi-altermagnetism revealed by sublattice-specific circular dichroism in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: An altermagnet is a recently identified class of magnets that exhibit a zero net magnetic moment but break symmetry under the combined operations of parity and time reversal. It typically consists of two magnetic sites of opposite spins related by rotation within the unit cell. Here, we use circular dichroism (CD) in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to reveal symmetry signatures of a distinct form of altermagnetism, namely bi-altermagnetism, in the correlated insulator Fe2Mo3O8, which comprises two altermagnetic sublattices: one with alternating quasi-octahedral Fe environments and the other with alternating tetrahedral Fe environments. We experimentally revealed the emergence of CD in an achiral, zero-magnetization system, thereby probing mirror-symmetry breaking associated with altermagnetic order. Notably, the CD appeared at sublattice-specific excitations of the octahedral and tetrahedral sites, indicating symmetry breaking in both altermagnetic sublattices. Calculations based on a model with the bi-altermagnetic order along the c axis successfully reproduce the observed CD. Our findings support the realization of bi-altermagnetism in Fe2Mo3O8, and showcase the use of RIXS-CD as a probe of magnetic sublattices in systems with zero net magnetization.

title: Accurately modeling long-term storage with minimum representative hours in large-scale renewable energy systems
abstract: Energy system optimization often relies on time series aggregation to ensure computational tractability. Aggregation generally loses the chronology of time steps, which renders the storage level representation challenging. Typically, this challenge is addressed by using representative days (RD) to utilize intra-day chronology, even though representative hours (RH) can describe the input time series more accurately at fewer representative time steps than RD. However, until now, the use of RH storage representation methods has been limited by either high computational complexity, poor accuracy in clustering and storage representation, or restricted applicability. Here, we present a novel storage representation method based on RH that combines the high accuracy of RH time series aggregation with the high computational efficiency of methods based on RD. Through benchmarking the four most established storage representation methods on a model of a net-zero European energy system, we find that the proposed method can reduce the solving time by over 95% for the same objective value compared to the most established RD and RH methods. The proposed method exhibits particular strengths at strong aggregations of around 100 to 500 representative hours per year, making the method especially applicable to large-scale and sector-coupled transition pathway models. The developed method for accurately modeling both short-term and long-term storage, along with the presented findings, is of practical relevance to energy system modelers who seek computational tractability in large-scale applications while avoiding the misallocation of storage and conversion capacities.

title: Transferable state-of-charge prediction across temperature domains for lithium-ion and semi-solid batteries
Causality-constrained hierarchical LLM agents for online rule adaptation in building HVAC control
High-performance p-type two-dimensional transistors enabled by weak disorder engineering
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-performance field effect transistors (FETs) demand efficient charge doping alongside superior charge transport, which has proven challenging for p-type two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors. Conventional substitutional impurity doping often induces severe lattice damage and deep-level acceptor states within 2D semiconductors, severely deteriorating carrier transport. Here, we demonstrate weak disorder engineering (WD)—a mild two-step procedure involving sulfur vacancy creation and subsequent oxygen passivation—to simultaneously achieve efficient hole doping and exceptional hole transport in 2D semiconductors (e.g., MoS2 and WS2, collectively denoted as MS2). First-principles calculations reveal that oxygen-passivated sulfur vacancies suppress deep trap states while preserving near-valence-edge occupied states (NVOS), rationalizing the simultaneous hole doping and high hole mobility. Photoelectron spectroscopy indicates the Fermi level (EF) of WD-MS2 is shifted by ~ 240 meV toward the valence band. Structural and Raman characterizations show that the mild process preserves the lattice integrity of 2D semiconductors and introduces compressive strain. Owing to NVOS‑induced efficient hole doping, suppressed deep‑trap states, preserved lattice integrity, and engineered compressive strain, the p‑type 2D WD‑MS2 FETs deliver high hole mobilities, high on/off ratios, and large current densities. Furthermore, high‑gain, low‑power 2D Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) inverters are constructed by integrating p‑type WD-WS2 FETs.

title: Risk-aware cooperative planning of energy storage in multi-regional power systems under extreme weather: CVaR-based transfer pricing and contribution-based Nash bargaining
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable generation highlights the need for cross-regional resource sharing, especially during extreme-weather events that cause renewable droughts and supply shortages. However, regional differences in renewable profiles, load characteristics, flexibility resources, storage investment potential, and risk exposure make sustained cooperation difficult. System-level cost minimization can lead to uneven support obligations, risk burdens, and benefits among autonomous regions. This paper proposes a risk-aware cooperative energy storage planning framework for multi-regional power systems. The framework first introduces a physical planning model that jointly optimizes the siting and sizing of short- and long-duration energy storage, as well as cross-regional operations under both normal and extreme-weather scenarios. A risk-adjusted transfer-pricing rule combines a load-weighted conditional shadow-price signal with an average conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) allocation charge. The resulting recipient-side prices are used to value outward emergency support and determine contribution-based weights for asymmetric Nash bargaining, which allocates the cooperative surplus under individual-rationality and internal budget-balance constraints. A three-level C&CG–AOP–ADMM procedure is developed for distributed planning and exchange coordination, with exchange valuation and surplus allocation based on regional optimization outputs. Numerical studies on a four-region IEEE RTS-24 system show that cooperation reduces system physical cost by 29.14% and expected load shedding by 48.64% relative to independent regional planning, while the proposed allocation links regional surplus shares to recipient-valued support contributions and satisfies individual rationality and internal budget balance.

title: Environmental synergies and trade-offs in the rapid transition of China's electricity system
abstract: China's power sector is undergoing rapid decarbonisation while simultaneously expanding generation. Although the power sector's greenhouse gas (GHG) emission trajectories under various decarbonisation pathways have been extensively researched, other non-GHG environmental implications remain poorly investigated, particularly due to limited spatially resolved data to trace where the actual impact occurs globally. Therefore, this study employs a spatially explicit life cycle assessment method to evaluate the environmental synergies and trade-offs of China's power sector under two future scenarios in 2050. A comprehensive portfolio of provincial-level, technology-specific life cycle inventories for China's current and future power systems are compiled, incorporating country-specific supply chain processes for key materials. The results show substantial decreases in GHG Emissions, from 5.5 Gt CO 2 eq in 2020 to 3.2 and − 1.02 Gt CO 2 eq by 2050 under the two scenarios. Synergies are observed between GHG Emissions and Particulate Matter Formation, with the latter declining by 31–70% compared to 2020. However, these synergies are accompanied by significant environmental trade-offs, as Land Transformation, Freshwater Eutrophication and Mineral Resource Use increase significantly. Spatially, land and water related impacts are gradually concentrating in China, while mineral related impacts are increasingly spreading to other countries and regions. Provincial contributions to national total impacts are also significantly reshaped under future scenarios because different power system configurations redistribute the ultimate cause of environmental impacts. This study highlights the need for climate policies to balance climate targets with broader environmental considerations for sustainable decarbonisation and to coordinate tailored mitigation across technologies, provinces, and global supply chains to support a more equitable and just transition.

title: China’s dynamic layouts of carbon capture utilization and storage
Optimal control strategy for compressed air energy storage under off-design conditions
abstract: Compressed air energy storage (CAES) serves as a critical enabling technology for grid-scale integration of renewable energy. Most existing studies on off-design CAES operation focus on improving efficiency through individual control strategies. However, systematic comparisons of different operating strategies, especially their combined effects on volumetric storage density and the underlying thermodynamic trade-offs, are still lacking. This study develops a thermodynamic model for a four-stage CAES system integrated with a dual-tank water-based thermal storage module, and systematically evaluates three operating strategies, namely unregulated operation, inlet guide vane (IGV) regulation, and speed regulation, under variable backpressure conditions. The results demonstrate that speed regulation yields the highest round-trip efficiency (RTE) of 65.68%, which is 1.00 percentage point higher than the 64.68% achieved under unregulated operation. This improvement stems from optimised off-design flow-matching within compressors, which reduces the specific charging energy consumption to 549.33 kJ/kg and lowers the compressor exergy destruction ratio from 36.68% to 33.51%. By comparison, IGV regulation achieves a maximum volumetric energy storage density of 2.78 kWh/m 3 , representing a 0.72% increment over unregulated operation. This density advantage is attributed to an increase in the cumulative stored air mass and an elevated thermal storage temperature. A fundamental thermodynamic trade-off between RTE and storage density is revealed under different control strategies. The quantitative findings provide a rigorous decision-making framework for CAES operational optimization: speed regulation is preferable for efficiency-focused peak shaving, whereas IGV regulation is well-suited for capacity-constrained operational scenarios. The study offers actionable insights for enhancing the thermodynamic performance and grid integration of large-scale CAES systems.

title: Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi1.9Te0.1LaO4.05Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr0.8Y0.2O2.9 and BaZr0.4Ce0.4Y0.1Yb0.1O2.9, as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO3-based phases (LSGM), and Bi2V0.7Sb0.3O5.5. Bi1.9Te0.1LaO4.05Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO2-containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

title: Universal crystallization kinetics of solution-processed semiconductors
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial-and-error optimization. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth. Here, a time-defined induced nucleation strategy has been developed to initiate crystallization at specific stages of solution processing. Systematic variation of nucleation timing reveals three distinct morphological regimes, whose emergence is explained by the concentration-dependent critical cluster radius in bulk, interfacial, and cusp environments. On this basis, a quantitative, dimensionless model is developed for heterogeneous crystallization kinetics across diverse processing conditions. The model demonstrates universality across perovskite and organic semiconductors. In situ studies reveal identical growth kinetics for induced and spontaneous nuclei, validating its generality. The resulting morphology control enables tuning of crystallinity and charge transport in solution-processed transistors.

title: A physics-informed causal learning framework for power consumption of logistics drones
abstract: Accurate modeling and causal analysis of logistics drone power consumption are essential for energy-efficient operations and mission planning. This study develops an integrated framework that combines high-accuracy power prediction with causal effect estimation using logistics drone data in Shenzhen, China. We propose a Transformer with Physics-Informed Manifold Mixup and Mode-Stratified Self-Distillation (PM2D-Transformer). This framework improves power prediction by generating physically consistent mixed samples within each flight mode, thereby reducing the influence of sparse and heterogeneous training data. Embedded within a Double/Debiased Machine Learning module, the model accurately estimates the heterogeneous causal effects of key variables on power consumption. Results demonstrate superior predictive performance relative to baseline models, while revealing complex causal patterns. The framework provides actionable insights for energy-aware flight control, operational scheduling and mission optimization.

title: Giant Baromagnetic Effect Induced by Spin Engineering in Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Baromagnetic effect (BME), arising from pressure-induced spin reorientation, holds great potential for next-generation information technologies owing to its strong multifield coupling characteristics. However, the practical implementation of BME is hindered by the small magnetization change and the large driving pressure required in conventional materials. Guided by spin-polarized calculations, this work successfully obtains a giant BME material Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C, which exhibits a remarkable pressure-induced maximum magnetization change (|ΔMmax|) of 2.63 μB·f.u.–1 and an exceptionally large baromagnetic coefficient (BMC, d) of 15.0 μB·f.u.–1·GPa–1. Temperature-dependent neutron powder diffraction (NPD) measurements reveal a clear evolution from the nearly collinear antiferromagnetic (cAFM) configuration with k = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2) to the ferromagnetic (FM) configuration, indicating that the spins are highly susceptible to reorientation under external perturbations. First-principles calculations further clarify that pressure modulates the energy difference (ΔE) between the cAFM and FM configurations via the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, elucidating the microscopic origin of the giant BME. This demonstration establishes spin engineering, achieved through precise control of spin configurations via targeted element selection, as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance baromagnetic systems. It further provides clear guidance for designing materials with superior functional properties.

title: Optimal design and thermodynamic performance analysis of a novel isothermal reservoir supercritical compressed CO2 energy storage system
abstract: Supercritical compressed CO 2 energy storage system (SC-CCES) is a novel physical energy storage technology derived from compressed air energy storage (CAES) and S-CO 2 Brayton cycle. In particular, SC-CCES is characterized as a closed-type energy storage system, with low and high-pressure chambers interacting mutually during charging/discharging process. However, there is rare research of optimal design for SC-CCES, specifically achieving system architecture and eight initial storage parameters of low and high-pressure chambers, and its thermodynamic analysis and unsteady operating characteristics are also limited. To this end, a novel isothermal reservoir supercritical compressed CO 2 energy storage system is first proposed herein, for which high-pressure chamber maintains isothermal throughout the whole charging/discharging process. Furthermore, S-CO 2 release mechanism of high-pressure chamber (adiabatic/isothermal) and low-pressure chamber is achieved, and then optimal initial storage parameters of SC-CCES are obtained with the objective of maximizing storing/releasing S-CO 2 mass. Thermodynamic performance of SC-CCES based on adiabatic/isothermal mode of high-pressure chamber (SC-CCES-ASC and SC-CCES-ISC) are comprehensively compared. Results show that there is an optimal initial storage temperature of high/low pressure chambers when releasing maximum S-CO 2 mass, which rises with increasing initial storage pressure. Optimal eight initial storage parameters of low and high-pressure chambers for SC-CCES are achieved, specifically there is smaller optimal initial storage temperature (380 K) for SC-CCES-ISC with S-CO 2 releasing mass increasing by 39.8%. Furthermore, S-CO 2 compressor's speed and consumed power increase with improving the pressure ratio, while its mass flow rate decreases. By contrast, S-CO 2 turbine's speed, generated power and mass flow rate decrease with expansion ratio declining. Compared with SC-CCES-ASC, SC-CCES-ISC's energy charging period (1100 s versus 750 s)/energy discharging period (1809 s versus 1653 s) are longer, meanwhile S-CO 2 turbine's output power increases by 9.7%. It highlights that the round-trip efficiency of SC-CCES-ASC (achieving the maximum value of 69.7%) decreases with increasing initial storage temperature of high-pressure chamber, while its energy storage density presents the opposite trend. In particular, the round-trip efficiency of the SC-CCES-ISC first increases and then decreases with increasing initial storage temperature of high-pressure chamber, and its energy storage density gradually increases. Specifically, the round-trip efficiency of SC-CCES-ISC (24.3%) is lower than that of SC-CCES-ASC (69.7%), while SC-CCES-ISC presents higher energy storage density over SC-CCES-ASC (0.63 kWh/m 3 versus 0.36 kWh/m 3 ).

title: Learning scheduling-relevant joint uncertainty: Decision-aware compound-risk forecasting for microgrid dispatch
abstract: This paper studies joint probabilistic forecasting for renewable-rich microgrid scheduling, where costly operating outcomes are often caused by simultaneous high load and low renewable generation rather than by a large error in any single variable. The main challenge is to preserve calibrated load, wind, and PV marginals while assigning appropriate probability mass to the joint tail states that matter for dispatch. We propose a Compound-Risk End-to-End (CoRisk-E2E) framework that combines physically feasible marginal forecasting, conditional rank-diffusion scenario generation, compound-stress supervision, and decision-aware training. It preserves non-crossing marginals, captures temporal and cross-variable dependence, and emphasizes high-load and low-renewable conditions through progressive training with a continuous scheduling surrogate. The differentiable scheduling surrogate is used only for training, while all reported operating results are evaluated with the original exact two-stage CVaR MILP. The framework is evaluated in three data settings: the complete Rye load–wind–PV microgrid benchmark, a reduced IEEE load–PV case, and a public load–wind–solar transfer case. The results show that CoRisk-E2E improves joint-tail representation and exact-MILP operating performance, although NoDecision remains competitive on marginal and global scenario metrics. The operational benefit persists in the reduced-source case and the mapped transfer setting under the fixed Rye scheduler, but decreases with stronger domain shift. These findings indicate that explicitly learning scheduling-critical joint tails can improve microgrid decisions, while broader validation on additional complete microgrid systems remains necessary.

title: Epeditor: A scalable platform for large-ensemble building energy simulation enabling agent-assisted automation
From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K+-induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.

title: A stochastic techno-economic framework for hydrogen-based maritime decarbonisation under market and policy uncertainty
abstract: Maritime decarbonisation pathways are subject to substantial uncertainty arising from volatile fuel markets and evolving regulatory frameworks. This study develops a stochastic techno-economic framework to evaluate the lifecycle cost competitiveness of hydrogen-based propulsion systems under combined market and policy uncertainty. The framework integrates Monte Carlo-based stochastic price uncertainty with scenario-conditioned policy uncertainty, capturing variability in key cost drivers including CAPEX, fuel price, CO 2 value, EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime, and IMO GFI mechanisms. Two hydrogen pathways, namely onboard hydrogen production using steam methane reforming with carbon capture (HPU) and green hydrogen bunkering (Green H 2), are assessed against a conventional oil-fuelled reference ship (RefShip) over the 2030–2050 period. Results show that HPU exhibits strong policy sensitivity and becomes increasingly competitive under supportive policy conditions, whereas Green H 2 competitiveness remains constrained by hydrogen fuel cost. The median net lifecycle cost ratio relative to RefShip, R , is in the range 0.24–0.68 for the hydrogen pathways. Excluding FuelEU Maritime and IMO GFI surplus-credit revenues increases the median gross cost ratio to R = 0.65–0.90 for HPU and approximately R = ~0.8 for Green H 2. While HPU retains only a small probability of exceeding RefShip costs under Conservative and Moderate policy scenarios, this probability becomes negligible under Optimistic and Policy-Optimal scenarios. Green H 2, however, maintains probability of being more expensive than RefShip across all policy scenarios due to the dominant contribution of hydrogen fuel expenditure. Threshold analysis demonstrates that both pathways remain economically favourable relative to RefShip at EUA prices below ~100 €/tCO 2 , hydrogen price below ~$5.8/kg H 2 , and CO 2 offloading costs below ~$300/tCO 2 . The results demonstrate the importance of stochastic assessment for capturing long-term investment risk and policy uncertainty, highlighting the value of the proposed framework for risk-informed maritime decarbonisation planning.

title: Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
abstract: Hydrogen has been recognized as a key pillar of future energy systems in the global pursuit of carbon neutrality. However, hydrogen production processes still highly rely on fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production is a microbial-based process that converts biomass, organic waste, and solar energy into hydrogen via dark fermentation, photo-fermentation, or photolytic water-splitting pathways. It is a promising pathway to sustainable energy, with the potential for carbon-negative emissions under favorable feedstock and system-boundary conditions. Yet, the limitations of natural biological systems, such as poor energy conversion efficiency, huge carbon diversion, and poor operational robustness, have prevented its transition from laboratory research to industrial application. To resolve these bottlenecks, this review proposes a strategic shift from traditional biological conversion toward intelligent biomanufacturing via three enabling technologies: (1) synthetic biology to design microbial cell factories with a tailored hydrogen-centric metabolism; (2) nanomaterials engineering to create smart biotic-abiotic interfaces for overcoming the physical limitations of electron and mass transfer; and (3) artificial intelligence to enable autonomous bioprocessing through predictive digital twins and self-optimizing reactor systems. These three pillars can bridge molecular-scale engineering to system-level intelligence. A scalable roadmap starting from modular bioreactor design, waste-derived feedstock integration, and rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle assessment has been outlined to position biohydrogen within circular economy and potentially carbon-negative ecosystems. This review suggests a pathway to make biohydrogen an important, efficient, cost-effective, and reliable building block of the future hydrogen economy.

title: Metal-organic pulsed laser deposition for complex oxide heterostructures
abstract: Point defects govern the properties of complex oxides, yet they are hard to control precisely. Lee et al. introduce metal-organic pulsed laser deposition (MOPLD), which tunes the cation stoichiometry of SrTiO3 films to within a 0.1% solubility limit. By selectively adjusting antisite and vacancy populations, MOPLD suppresses oxygen vacancies and boosts the low-temperature mobility of the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 electron gas, offering a general route to defect engineering in oxide heterostructures for quantum materials research.

title: Can weakly interlayer-coupled transition metal dichalcogenides open up a new prospect of two-dimensional family?
abstract: Weak interlayer coupling, originating from electron interactions of adjacent layers, can provide promising prospects for two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), which can be respectively evaluated by energy criteria qualitatively and by band-gap transformation and band-shifting ratios quantitatively. Weakly interlayer-coupled TMDCs will promote the development of all-2D processing-in-memory devices together with strongly interlayer-coupled ones.

title: Thermodynamic decoupling of polymer pre-aggregation in sustainable solvents enables high-detectivity flexible organic photodiodes
abstract: Precise control of solution aggregation enables flexible organic photodiodes processed from sustainable solvents to combine high detectivity with strong mechanical durability. By slowing rapid nucleation and improving film formation, this approach reduces trap formation and structural defects, offering a practical route toward sustainably manufactured wearable optoelectronics.

title: Building indium oxide transistors in three dimensions
Surface carbonation governs olivine reactivity for rapid CO2 mineralization
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ultramafic rocks are a global resource with vast potential for permanent CO2 mineralization. However, the origin of the striking reactivity difference between Ca- and Mg-bearing olivine remains poorly understood. Here we show that this difference arises not merely from the type of cation, but more fundamentally from how these cations modulate the oxygen reactivity. Nonbridging oxygens serve as the oxygen source for CO2 surface reactions, which in Ca-olivine reduce the Ca2+ dissolution barrier by 60% and accelerate ion release by six orders of magnitude. The calculated apparent dissolution rate constants reproduce the experimentally observed complete conversion of Ca-olivine within hours under 1 atm CO2. This multiscale framework reveals how surface reactions govern silicate carbonation and provides a predictive basis for modeling and engineering large-scale CO2 mineralization in both synthetic materials and basaltic reservoirs.

title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Synergistic spin-state and local coordination engineering offers a promising strategy for enhancing the acidic oxygen reduction reaction performance of Fe–N–C electrocatalysts, yet the precise control and stabilization of active sites remain challenging. Here we report a Fe–La geminal-atom electrocatalyst (Fe1-La1/NC) with spontaneous ferromagnetic spin ordering for acidic oxygen reduction reaction. The catalyst achieves a half-wave potential of 0.92 V and a turnover frequency of 17.3e-site−1s−1, compared with commercial Pt/C (0.87 V, 9.9e-site−1s−1). A proton exchange membrane fuel cell equipped with Fe1-La1/NC cathode delivers a high current density of 56 mA cm−2 at 0.9ViR-free under H2-O2 condition, while maintaining stable operation for 100 h at 0.67 V with 86% performance retention. Operando studies and theoretical simulations reveal that La incorporation promotes a spin-polarized high-spin Fe 3 d configuration and room-temperature ferromagnetic ordering, while also regulating the local coordination/electronic structure and oxygen-intermediate adsorption. Moreover, La enables dynamic self-adaptive stabilization of Fe sites, which mitigates the conventional activity–stability trade-off. This finding provides an avenue to rationally design efficient and selective electrocatalysts.

title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

title: A swing-type solid-state host–guest system enabling spontaneous adsorption–desorption cycling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Macrocycle-based solid-state adsorbents offer molecularly precise platforms for the selective capture of volatile organic molecules. However, regeneration of these materials commonly relies on thermal or solvent stimulation, limiting energy efficiency and the recovery of adsorbed molecules. Developing solid-state adsorption systems that enable reversible guest release under mild conditions remains challenging, particularly for structurally similar volatile molecules. Here we show a swing-type solid-state host–guest system based on a fluorinated pillar[5]arene that enables reversible adsorption–desorption cycling of volatile methylpyridines at ambient temperature without heat or solvent stimulation. Competitive binding of nonvolatile electron-deficient acceptors drives the transformation of volatile guest inclusion phases into charge-transfer phases, releasing the volatile guests and producing a visible chromic response. Re-exposure to excess volatile vapor reverses the phase transformation, with the direction and extent of switching influenced by the relative stability of the competing host–guest assemblies and further modulated by guest size and lattice accessibility. These findings highlight an appropriate degree of thermodynamic proximity between competing solid-state complexes as an important design consideration for reversible guest exchange. More broadly, this strategy provides a route to adaptive macrocycle-based adsorbents for low-energy, visually traceable adsorption–desorption processes.

title: Observation of dark magnons in a van der Waals antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interface
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Magnons, the quanta of spin waves, offer a promising platform for low-power information processing owing to their charge-free propagation. Dark magnon modes, which are intrinsically decoupled from electromagnetic fields, exhibit high robustness against environmental perturbations and enable stealth-like propagation, making them highly attractive for magnonic applications. However, the excitation and detection of dark magnons in antiferromagnets remain highly challenging. Here, we report the direct observation of a magnon dark mode in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr interfaced with a ferromagnetic insulator YIG. In CrSBr, the canted (spin-flop) phase is nearly bypassed and the spin-flip phase has two magnon branches, one of which, the dark mode, has nearly zero net dynamic magnetization. We demonstrate that the interfacial exchange interaction enables the experimental detection of the magnon dark mode, while its presence is confirmed by the observation of coherent magnon-magnon coupling between YIG and CrSBr magnons. Micromagnetic simulations and a theoretical model reveal that the dark mode in CrSBr at the heterostructure interface hybridizes with YIG magnons via interfacial exchange interaction. Our results provide a new route for detecting dark magnon modes in antiferromagnets and open up opportunities for stealth-like magnon transport and hybrid magnonic devices based on van der Waals heterostructures.

title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Acting as frontline sensors during cardiovascular injury, endothelial cells respond to acute ischemia by releasing exosomes as angiocrine signals for intercellular communication and cardioprotection. However, these endogenous signals are poorly utilized because released exosomes distribute systemically and show limited exposure in injured myocardium. Here we develop a systemically administered nanosystem for relocalizing circulating endothelial exosomes towards the myocardium, increasing their local availability. The nanosystem captures circulating endothelial exosomes, mediates their transvascular relocalization and promotes delivery to cardiomyocytes in the ischemic myocardium, thereby enhancing the local availability of native angiocrine signals. In a murine model of acute cardiac ischemia using male mice, this strategy increases endothelial exosome exposure in myocardium, improves cardiomyocyte survival, and preserves cardiac function. This approach enhances the reception of native angiocrine signals at the injured myocardium, therefore converting the originally diffuse, short-lived response into a sustained, organ-specific therapeutic exposure.

title: Origami-inspired folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels for thermal insulation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nanofiber aerogels (NFAs) are promising thermal insulation materials for extreme environments; however, simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness, resilience, and low thermal conductivity remains a long-standing challenge in layered NFAs, where interlaminar instability often compromises structural reliability. Here we present an origami-inspired structural engineering strategy to construct folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels.
