A folded-interlocked origami skeleton, integrated with a tailored interlaminar structure, introduces geometric confinement and fiber-mediated interlaminar toughening. As a result, the aerogels exhibit high compressive strength (548.02 kPa at 80% strain) and a near-zero Poisson’s ratio. Importantly, the robust interlaminar network enhances resistance to delamination, allowing the aerogels to sustain tensile deformation up to approximately 40% strain before interlaminar failure. Meanwhile, interlaminar-guided heat-flow redistribution yields a low axial thermal conductivity of 0.035 W m−1 K−1 and pronounced anisotropic thermal insulation. This work provides an architectural strategy for designing folded-interlocked NFAs for thermal protection in aerospace and other harsh environments.

title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEPTA-Ce, with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEPTA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEPTA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

title: Passive anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation: From mechanisms to applications
abstract: Frost formation in low-temperature environments causes significant efficiency losses and safety hazards across aerospace, HVAC, and manufacturing industries. Conventional active anti-frosting methods suffer from poor energy efficiency due to periodic energy input requirements. This review summarizes recent advances in passive anti-frosting through interfacial humidity regulation—a strategy that inhibits ice crystal nucleation and growth by actively controlling local water vapor, offering substantial energy-saving potential. We firstly discuss theoretical models of ice nucleation in supersaturated vapor, examining how surface energy, microstructure, and chemistry govern interfacial humidity distribution and phase transitions. Secondly, three widely reported humidity regulating media, ice, hygroscopic gels, and hygroscopic liquids, are examined in terms of their vapor regulation mechanisms and frost suppression performance. Thirdly, we address advanced anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation via hygroscopic materials, biological protein and inspired microstructured surfaces. This review provides theoretical foundations and technical guidance for next-generation energy-efficient frost suppression technologies.

title: Spectral sensing at a glance
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Portable biosensors are revolutionizing the way we diagnose disease and ill-health. By varying a metasurface’s geometry continuously across a chip, a recent study by H. Kim et al. reports a new sensing strategy, which reads signals from individual camera images without the need for a spectrometer. This enables the label-free detection of biomarkers in a handheld format.

title: Strategic scenario planning for hydrogen supply chains via graph convolutional networks: overcoming mid-stream infrastructure bottlenecks in energy transitions
AC OPF learning via modular decomposition and adaptation to topology changes
abstract: We propose a novel framework for efficiently solving the AC optimal power flow (OPF) problem under varying grid topologies. Traditional learning-based approaches to OPF often retrain entire models when the network topology changes, leading to high computational cost and limited generalization. The proposed approach exploits the fact that different components of the OPF problem respond to topology changes to varying degrees: device-level operating limits remain largely unaffected, the network equations are modified locally around a tripped line, whereas the resulting optimal operating point may change throughout the network. It consists of two complementary training phases. In Phase I (modular pretraining), the OPF learning task under the intact grid topology is decomposed into three sequential subtasks (voltage setpoint prediction, power generation estimation, and generation cost computation) representing distinct functional mappings. In Phase II (adaptive learning), these pretrained modules are jointly fine-tuned for new topologies using a composite loss that combines supervised objectives with physics-informed regularization for branch-flow accuracy, nodal power balance, and operational constraint satisfaction. Extensive evaluations on benchmark grids demonstrate accurate predictions for the intact grid as well as for grids with seen and unseen contingencies. In our numerical experiments, at most 60 N − 1 contingency topologies are used for adaptation, and the largest mean prediction error among the reported variables under unseen topologies is approximately 3.1%.

title: Author Correction: A microbial platform for selective biosynthesis of monoterpene esters
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds

title: Using cross-regional grid interconnection to relieve growing energy storage demand in renewable energy integration: A case study from China
abstract: With the rapid growth of wind and solar generation, power systems face increasing balancing and energy storage needs. Cross-regional interconnection provides spatial flexibility through tie-line power exchange, yet the implications of tie-line scheduling flexibility for capacity planning remain insufficiently understood. This paper uses the Gansu–Shandong–Zhejiang interconnected system in China to quantify how tie-line scheduling timescales affect storage requirements for bulk energy shifting and system balancing. Within a common capacity planning and dispatch optimization framework, three stylized tie-line scheduling strategies are compared: Daily Fixed, Monthly Fixed, and Annual Fixed, representing decreasing levels of scheduling flexibility. Results show that greater tie-line scheduling flexibility changes the optimal capacity configuration, particularly the required battery energy storage (BES) capacity. Compared with Annual Fixed, Daily Fixed reduces BES capacity additions by 59.2% and total system cost by 22.8%. Sensitivity analyses further show that this advantage remains robust to variations in storage parameters and tie-line capacity. These findings indicate that the planning value of cross-regional interconnection depends substantially on its operational flexibility.

title: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anti-tuberculosis (TB) drugs must reach the disease site to be effective, but complex TB pathology limits drug distribution and efficacy, as bacteria in the necrotic center of lung cavities are difficult to access and kill. Our study generates the most comprehensive database of site-of-disease distribution for 24 drugs and drug candidates in a rabbit model of cavitary TB. We validate a lung lesion penetration model with clinical data and develop an integrated approach that combines microenvironment-specific pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Next, we simulate site-of-disease coverage of shortened regimens tested in major Phase 3 trials over the past decade, allowing direct comparisons with trial outcomes. We propose that regimens including at least two drugs achieving bactericidal concentrations in pulmonary cavities are more likely to meet primary clinical endpoints in patients with cavitary disease. Our translational platform constitutes a validated tool to support drug evaluation, smart regimen design, and de-risking of late-stage trials.

title: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. Such small viral genomes are searched in environmental metagenomes across public databases, including IMG/M and MGnify. Using hidden Markov models and protein language models, we identify and characterize small viral genomes encoding HK97-fold proteins that exhibit molecular similarities to encapsulins yet lack portal and tail genes. The phylogenetic analyses of HK97-fold proteins reveal independent mixed groups of viruses and encapsulins, and structural analyses identify similarities between encapsulins and procapsids, the immature state of viral capsids. The observations support a bidirectional evolution between encapsulins and HK97-fold viruses enabled by the viral procapsid state. Using biophysical and genomic arguments, we introduce an evolutionary model of HK97-fold protein shells, predicting that they emerged as lower-symmetry biochemical compartments and that HK97-fold viral capsids may retain biochemical functions.

title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

title: The claustrum contributes to working memory maintenance in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Working memory (WM) enables the temporary maintenance and manipulation of sensory information to guide behavior, yet the neural circuits supporting this process remain incompletely defined. The claustrum is a highly interconnected brain structure positioned to integrate distributed cortical activity, but its contribution to WM has remained unclear. Here, we combined microendoscopic calcium imaging, chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations in mice performing sensory-guided WM tasks to examine the role of the claustrum in WM. Claustrum neurons exhibited cue-evoked activity that persisted across delay periods and evolved dynamically over time, with population states retaining information about cue identity on single trials. Reducing claustrum excitability during encoding, delay maintenance, or target comparison similarly impaired WM performance across sensory modalities, without affecting sensory processing, motor output, arousal or inhibitory control. Together, these findings reveal an important causal contribution of the claustrum to WM maintenance.

title: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The autonomic sympathetic nervous system innervates peripheral resistance arteries, thereby controlling arterial diameter and modulating blood supply to organs and arterial tone. Despite its fundamental role in blood flow regulation and cardiovascular adaptation to challenging situations, how sympathetic arterial innervation develops remains poorly understood.We here show that sympathetic arterial innervation is regulated by the axonal guidance molecule EphrinA4 in arterial Smooth Muscle Cells (SMCs), which repels sympathetic axons via the EphA4 receptor. Using the EphA4flox-THCRE mouse, we specifically inactivated EphA4 in sympathetic axons, inducing a loss of repulsion and increased sympathetic innervation of peripheral arteries throughout life. Functional consequences included a significant increase in arterial tone, including resistivity and vasoconstriction, associated with elevated systemic arterial blood pressure at rest and a marked increase during acute stress. These findings identify a pathway that negatively regulates sympathetic arterial innervation and could contribute to elevated systemic blood pressure in male mice.

title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Although cerebellum is neuropathologically affected in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementia (ADRD), the cell type-specific genomic and epigenomic changes remain poorly understood. Here, we present single-nucleus multiome (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) analysis of 103,861 nuclei isolated from both the cerebellum and frontal cortex of diseased individuals and cognitively healthy controls. We identify 431,834 significant peak-to-gene linkages across cell subtypes, revealing cis-regulatory elements linked to cell type-specific and disease-associated transcriptomic and regulatory network changes. Differential trajectory analysis pinpoints disease-associated genes in cerebellar granule cells, such as STMN1 and CLU. Integrating epigenomic, genetic, and three-dimensional genome data, we pinpoint two likely causal variants linked to SEZ6L2 in Purkinje cells and KANSL1 in granule cells. Through CRISPR interference in patient-derived cerebellar organoids, we show that silencing the variant-containing regulatory elements suppresses SEZ6L2 and KANSL1 expression, which perturbs neurodegeneration-associated gene programs. This cell type-specific regulatory landscape provides genomic and epigenomic insights into the pathological role of the cerebellum in AD/ADRD.

title: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H2O2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Mutations preventing DLAT oxidation render PDH resistant to oxidative inhibition, impair NADPH generation, reduce peroxide detoxification, and sensitize cells to oxidative damage and death. DLAT oxidation also drives a Warburg-like metabolic phenotype of increased glucose uptake, elevated lactate secretion, and reduced TCA cycle activity. Thus DLAT oxidation is a redox-sensing mechanism that regulates PDH activity and central carbon metabolism.

title: Shifting balance between habitat and climate in boreal biodiversity patterns across space, time and taxa
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Climate and habitat are key drivers of biodiversity patterns. However, how they independently and jointly affect species distribution across space, time, and taxa remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluate the relative importance of habitat and climate variables underpinning occurrence and abundance patterns of 503 terrestrial animal species over 20 years and a ~ 1100 km latitudinal gradient in Finland. Habitat composition is the main explanatory variable of biodiversity patterns, with varying importance and uncertainty across taxa, regions, and years, and with effects being partially correlated for many species. Specifically, habitat dominate in importance for butterflies, birds, and small mammals, while both habitat and climate explain the patterns of large mammals and moths. Additionally, patterns between biogeographical regions and years are mainly explained by climate, while habitat explains most variation within regions and years. Further differences emerge among functional groups, as body size, pace of life and specialization modulate the relative importance of habitat and climate. Our findings emphasize that land use is a major force in shaping terrestrial biodiversity, while highlighting its tight connection with climate. Considering functional, spatial, and temporal contexts is thus essential for building effective conservation strategies for biodiversity under global change.

title: Effects of time-restricted eating and supervised exercise on intrahepatic fat and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity: the TEMPUS randomized controlled trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lifestyle interventions targeting intrahepatic fat remain limited. We investigated whether 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE), supervised exercise, or their combination reduced intrahepatic fat fraction (IHFF) more than usual care (UC; Mediterranean diet and physical activity education) and each other. This investigator-initiated, parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted in Granada, Spain. Participants were recruited from May 2023 to April 2024, and the trial was completed on 5 September 2025. Primary outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to group allocation, whereas intervention personnel were not. All 187 randomized adults with obesity (50% women) were included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis: UC (n = 48), TRE (n = 46), Exercise (n = 47), and TRE+Exercise (n = 46). The primary outcome was change in IHFF measured by magnetic resonance imaging after 12 weeks. IHFF change did not differ with TRE (−0.4%; 95% CI, −2.0 to 1.2; P = 0.93), Exercise (−0.8%; −2.4 to 0.8; P = 0.54), or TRE+Exercise (−1.1%; −2.7 to 0.5; P = 0.28) compared with UC, nor among intervention groups. These findings do not support greater short-term IHFF reductions with TRE, exercise, or their combination than with UC or between intervention groups. Trial registration: NCT05897073.

title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals inter-household networks of gut-colonising ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in two rural Malawian districts
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Infection with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-Ec) is a global health concern that disproportionately affects sub-Saharan Africa. Gut mucosal colonisation is thought to precede invasive infection. Understanding ESBL-Ec colonisation and transmission across communities is therefore essential. Here, we investigate the genomic epidemiology and spatial structure of 159 gut-colonising ESBL-Ec isolates from the faeces of 211 people in two rural Malawian villages using longitudinal sampling (2023–24), whole-genome sequencing and household mapping. Colonisation prevalence rose from 34.1% (95% CI: 27.8–41.0) to 54.2% (95% CI: 46.0–62.3) over one year. Isolates belonged to 33 sequence types (STs), most commonly ST38 and ST131, harbouring 46 distinct antimicrobial resistance gene types. Fifteen strains were identified in ≥3 households that were typically separated by short geographic distances (

title: Replacing anaerobic fermentation with reverse β-oxidation enables growth-coupled evolution for enhanced fatty-alcohol production
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Engineering robust fermentation hosts remains a barrier to scalable biomanufacturing. In this work we replace canonical mixed-acid fermentation in Escherichia coli with a redox‑balanced reverse β‑oxidation (rBOX) pathway that produces medium‑chain fatty alcohols and is bioenergetically equivalent to ethanol fermentation. This synthetic fermentation restores anaerobic growth, tightly coupling fitness to product formation and enabling adaptive laboratory evolution that selects for mutations increasing rBOX flux. Evolved strains increase maximum productivity fourfold (110 ± 0.15 mg/L/hr) and titer more than threefold up to 4.0 ± 0.28 g/L compared to the unevolved strain. Proteomic analyses of evolved strains indicate differential expression of enzymes at key metabolic nodes and activation of latent genes with functions overlapping those of rBOX enzymes. These results establish redox-balanced growth coupling as a powerful tool for strain improvement and demonstrate rBOX as a practical synthetic fermentation pathway.

title: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The emergence of evolutionary novelties remains a central challenge in biology, particularly for complex organs such as the vertebrate eye. Here, we use the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps to investigate adaptation to simultaneous aerial and aquatic vision. Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics reveal that the ventral retina, which processes aerial light, is developmentally expanded and exhibits region-specific opsin expression. Ventral PR1 cones express opn1mw2 rather than the longer-wavelength-sensitive opn1lw paralogs expressed dorsally. Machine-learning predictions indicate that Opn1mw2 is red-shifted relative to Opn1mw1 but remains blue-shifted relative to dorsal Opn1lw pigments. Dorsal-ventral patterning markers further reveal an overrepresentation of ventral retinal identities. Comparative spatial profiling of developing and adult Anableps and killifish indicates dorsal displacement of the retinal boundary, producing a proportionally larger ventral domain. Thus, Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of the ventral retina and regional reconfiguration of opsin expression within conserved cone subtypes.

title: Luminal geometry and coiled coil length determine submembrane localization of type II transmembrane Golgi proteins
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We previously showed that transmembrane proteins laterally partition within Golgi cisternae: trafficking components (e.g., GPP130, a type II transmembrane protein) are enriched at the cisternal rim, whereas Golgi enzymes localize to the cisternal interior. However, the underlying mechanism was unclear. We found that the luminal juxtamembrane coiled coil of GPP130 is necessary and sufficient for rim localization, with coiled coil length, rather than sequence identity, determining partitioning. When retargeted to the ER, GPP130 preferentially localized to ER sheet rims and was partially excluded from the nuclear envelope, an exclusion reduced upon nuclear envelope expansion. Cryo-electron tomography revealed that the intraluminal widths of Golgi cisternal interiors, some ER sheets, and the nuclear envelope are smaller than the predicted coiled coil length. Two additional type II Golgi transmembrane proteins with long luminal juxtamembrane coiled coils similarly localized to cisternal rims. These findings identify intraluminal width as a mechanism governing the lateral partitioning of type II transmembrane proteins with long luminal coiled coils.

title: Fatty acid metabolism controls plasma membrane cholesterol accessibility via ATGL-dependent phospholipid remodeling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Accessible cholesterol, the pool of membrane cholesterol with high chemical activity, regulates vital processes including vertebrate development and pathogen evasion. The mechanisms that govern plasma membrane (PM) cholesterol accessibility are incompletely understood. Using a genome-wide screen we find that acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha (ACC1) loss causes a ~10-fold increase in PM accessible cholesterol in cells and a male mouse model. We demonstrate that reduced fatty acyl-CoA levels, achieved by targeting metabolic enzymes including ACC1, fatty acid synthase (FASN) or acyl-CoA synthetases long chain (ACSL1, 3 and 4), results in the activation of adipose triacylglycerol lipase (ATGL). ATGL activation elevates polyunsaturated diacylglycerols even in triacylglycerol-deficient backgrounds, suggesting that ATGL acts independently of triacylglycerol hydrolysis. These diacylglycerol species are utilized to generate polyunsaturated phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine, which raises PM fluidity and cholesterol accessibility. Conversely, ATGL inhibition rigidifies the PM, reducing PM accessible cholesterol. Increased PM fluidity impairs cholesterol transport, triggering SREBP2 activation. This study reveals a surprising link between fatty acid metabolism and cholesterol homeostasis, demonstrating how ATGL-dependent lipid remodeling tunes membrane fluidity to regulate intracellular cholesterol signaling.

title: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Infection triggers the fever response, but the response’s effect on antimicrobial peptide (AMP) function remains unknown. We discovered that human AMP LL-37 antibacterial activity is temperature-dependent and were curious as to why. Its temperature dependence is not an accident, as AMPs from other animals with different body temperatures have distinct temperature sensitivities. We find that AMP temperature sensitivities are tuned to animals’ body temperatures, and that for animals able to raise their body temperature, this is used to increase the AMP’s antibacterial efficacy. This effect reflects a balance between optimizing antibacterial killing while minimizing mitochondrial damage. In contrast, cold-blooded animals that are unable to raise their body temperature use a different strategy to avoid mitochondrial damage. Together, this study suggests that fever is beneficial for antimicrobial defense by raising AMP activity towards bacteria while reducing mitochondrial damage when pathogens are absent.

title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis. (R)-3-([1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)-2-aminopropan-1-ol (ABP), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor. Here, we engineer an ω-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding. Dynamic cross-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with >99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP. This integrated computational-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel-pocket binding trade-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis.

title: Genome-reduced Aridivitia evolved predation to thrive in Earth’s oligotrophic depths
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deep soils represent one of Earth’s largest yet most enigmatic microbial habitats, where survival strategies under extreme oligotrophy remain poorly understood. Here, we report the Aridivitia group, a globally distributed bacterial lineage enriched in oligotrophic soils and thriving down to 22 m depth across sites in the United States and China. Despite its genome reduction (average size ~2.9 Mb), Aridivitia exhibits high metabolic flexibility in utilizing diverse carbon and energy sources. Cellular, genomic, and metatranscriptomic evidence, including small cell and genome sizes, host-associated metabolism, and the active expression of attachment- and attack-associated surface structures such as Tad pili and pore-forming toxins, indicate a predatory lifestyle in Aridivitia. Ancestral genome reconstruction reveals that Aridivitia originated as free-living mixotrophs, but subsequently lost the ability to fix carbon as they evolved a predatory lifestyle. Collectively, Aridivitia exemplifies a unique evolutionary strategy that reconciles genome reduction with functional versatility, expanding our understanding of microbial adaptation and evolution at the energetic limits of life.

title: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

title: Multiplexed live imaging deciphers nuclear force-driven chromatin dynamics and embryo development
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mechanical forces transmitted to the nucleus regulate chromatin organization and gene expression to guide cell fate transitions. However, how the forces dynamically reshape the genome in living systems remains unclear. Here, inspired by the visualization of perinuclear chromatin detachment under low tension, we develop a genetically encoded fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based nuclear tension sensor (NuTS) that directly quantifies forces transmitted into the nucleus through LINC complex proteins SUN1/2 and their effect on chromatin reorganization. NuTS enables high spatiotemporal mapping of forces across the nuclear envelope. Combined imaging of NuTS and lamina-associated domains (LADs) reveals that force fluctuations are coupled to LADs repositioning, and that a force of approximately 6 pN on SUN2 is required to maintain perinuclear chromatin anchoring. A drop below this threshold triggers lamin A phosphorylation at Ser22, which precedes and drives perinuclear chromatin dissociation and LAD reorganization by about 10 min. LINC-complex force transmission critically regulates cell migration and is essential for embryonic notochord development in vitro and in vivo. Our study establishes a mechanochemical framework linking nuclear forces to chromatin organization and function.

title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The 2025 M7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

title: Hemispheric asymmetry in predicted range shifts of anti-tropical fish under future climate change
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anti-tropically distributed species have long intrigued biogeographers. However, how they will respond to future climate change remains a key unresolved question, particularly for marine species given an expected hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. Here, using species distribution models for 172 anti-tropical marine fishes, we predict that northern hemispheric lineages will experience significantly higher range contractions, in agreement with the hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. Our predictions show that suitable habitat will be reduced at a similar rate both within and outside marine protected areas, leading protection efficacy (the proportion of the total suitable habitat protected) to remain at current levels, irrespective of the scenario and period considered, and the level of protection efficacy to remain significantly higher in the Southern Hemisphere. These results highlight the need for accounting for hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming when designing future conservation strategies.

title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Wildfires in the Amazon have far-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited. Here we identify a large-scale atmospheric precursor of August–September Amazon wildfires: a June–July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers (ARs), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south. This dipole is strongly linked to interannual variability in Amazon wildfire activity through land–atmosphere feedbacks associated with reduced precipitation and humidity, enhanced surface warming and solar radiation, and increased vegetation stress. We estimate that wildfire-related forest loss associated with this AR dipole mode accounts for approximately 26% of the observed interannual variability in total forest loss. Adding the South Atlantic AR dipole to predictors based on May–June sea surface temperature anomalies and June–July wildfire activity yields substantial predictive skill for August–September burned area (R² = 0.67). Climate model projections further indicate a future intensification of the South Atlantic AR dipole mode, implying increased wildfire-driven ecological degradation in the Amazon under continued warming.

title: Risk-aware and network-compatible bidding of aggregated DER under energy-as-a-service model
Frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid renewable P2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers
abstract: Renewable power-to-hydrogen (ReP2H) enables large-scale renewable energy utilization and supports the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors, such as chemicals and maritime transport, via hydrogen-based renewable ammonia and methanol fuels. As a result, utility-scale ReP2H projects are expanding worldwide. However, off-grid ReP2H systems exhibit low inertia due to their converter-dominated nature, making frequency security a critical concern. Although recent studies show that electrolyzers can contribute to frequency regulation (FR), their support capability depends on operating states and loading levels, creating a trade-off between hydrogen output and frequency security. To address this challenge, this work develops a unified co-optimization framework for frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid ReP2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers. A system-level frequency response model is established to capture multi-stage FR from alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs), proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEMELs), and other resources, including ammonia-fueled generators retrofitted in co-located chemical plants, battery energy storage, and wind turbines (WTs). Stage-wise transient frequency security constraints are derived, reformulated into tractable forms, and embedded into production scheduling, enabling coordinated on/off switching and load allocation across electrolyzers to maximize hydrogen output under uncertain renewable power input while enforcing frequency security constraints. Case studies based on real-world systems demonstrate that the proposed approach allows hydrogen plants to replace 55.52% and 96.85% of FR reserves from WTs and AFGs, respectively, while improving the system-level net hydrogen yield by substantially reducing ammonia-fuel consumption. Year-long simulations show an average 28.96% increase in annual net profit resulting from reduced reliance on conventional reserves.

title: Dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles
abstract: Unlike passenger electric vehicles, heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles operate for long periods under high-load conditions. The continuous heat rejection of the engine-generator set through the engine high-temperature coolant loop makes fan/pump power directly interact with the direct-current (DC) bus power balance and generator–battery power split. Therefore, cooling power scheduling is part of energy management, rather than only a thermal-protection task. This paper proposes a dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination strategy, termed DTP-HETC, for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles. A shared-encoder dual-head bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) predictor is used to capture short-horizon traction fluctuations and long-horizon engine-loop thermal evolution. The predicted thermal risk is quantified as thermal debt and converted into thermal buffer intensity B T k , which further adapts the thermal-load-shaping weights and the control-grid resolution of dynamic programming-based model predictive control (DP-MPC). By using this information, DTP-HETC advances part of the cooling effort from boundary-triggered response to thermal-risk formation intervals, smoothing cooling-induced DC-bus disturbances and coordinating fan/pump power with generator–battery power allocation. Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 220-ton series hybrid mining truck show that, under sustained heavy-load uphill operation, DTP-HETC reduces equivalent fuel consumption by 12.16% and lowers peak engine-loop coolant temperature by 2.53 °C compared with a rule-based baseline. The mean execution time is 33.7 ms, confirming controller-level real-time feasibility. These results indicate that DTP-HETC provides an effective thermal-load reshaping approach for improving energy efficiency and thermal reliability in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles.

title: Bridging deterministic and stochastic scheduling: Learning risk-aware forecast adjustments for PV-BESS operation
abstract: The participation of hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) installations in electricity markets requires modeling multi-temporal forecast uncertainty via temporal trajectories and integrating this information into bidding optimization frameworks. Most state-of-the-art approaches rely on stochastic or robust optimization methods, which are computationally intensive and offer limited interpretability to decision-makers. Consequently, deterministic optimization approaches remain the industry standard in practical market applications. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a novel learning-to-optimize framework that combines a deterministic mixed-integer linear programming formulation with a context-aware artificial neural network policy trained through reinforcement learning. The policy operates as a learned cost function approximation , translating probabilistic forecast metrics into time-dependent multiplicative forecast adjustment parameters. This approach preserves the simplicity and industry acceptance of deterministic optimization while effectively embedding information related to forecast uncertainty and risk-awareness into the day-ahead bidding and scheduling process for hybrid PV-BESS systems. For a real-world electric vehicle charging station case study in Portugal, equipped with 375 kWp of PV generation and a 1.258 MWh BESS, the proposed learning-to-optimize framework substantially outperforms the deterministic baseline. Specifically, it captures 39.27% and 27.26% of the maximum theoretical cost-saving potential achievable under perfect forecasts during autumn and summer peak periods, respectively. At the intraday level, the learned policy effectively mitigates systematic forecast errors, reducing the cumulative daily negative imbalance volume by 48.22% under standard operating conditions. Moreover, the framework maintains a robust operational safety margin, reducing imbalance exposure by 10.02% during large unforeseen PV generation drops caused by clouds.

title: Theory-guided lightweight decomposition for efficient and robust day-ahead electrical load forecasting
abstract: Accurate electrical load forecasting is important for operational planning and dispatch in modern power systems, yet existing models often face a trade-off among predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to imperfect exogenous inputs. To address this challenge, we propose a Theory-guided Lightweight Efficient Decomposition (TgLED) framework with a Structured Temporal–Exogenous Mixer (STEM) for day-ahead electrical load forecasting. TgLED transforms raw load data into a normalized load-ratio series and decomposes it into a transferable dimensionless trend and a local fluctuation component. The trend captures stable structural patterns through domain knowledge, whereas the fluctuation is learned by STEM, a lightweight dual-path architecture that separately models temporal inertia and exogenous drivers using efficient feedforward operations. Four-fold cross-validation on hourly load and weather data from 12 districts in Beijing shows that TgLED achieves an average MSE of 0.056, reducing the error by 9.8% compared with the previous theory-guided baseline TgDLF. Compared with recently proposed lightweight time-series forecasting baselines, TgLED achieves evident superiority in forecasting performance. On the same RTX 4090 platform, TgLED reduces the training time from 768.66 s to 6.85 s and the inference time from 19.25 s to 1.91 s, indicating its practical value for frequent retraining and multi-district day-ahead forecasting. Additional noise-injection experiments on weather inputs show slower performance degradation, indicating stronger robustness to exogenous-input uncertainty and weather forecast errors. These results demonstrate that TgLED provides an efficient and interpretable approach to electrical load forecasting under limited computational budgets and imperfect exogenous information.

title: Transport characteristics and formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in 200-cell PEMFC stack: Numerical reconstruction and experimental investigation
abstract: Due to the difficulty in directly observing and resolving internal mass transport in multi-cell proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks, current studies on stack voltage inconsistency remain largely confined to macroscopic performance analysis. Consequently, the mechanisms responsible for voltage inconsistency remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, this study develops a framework integrating offline pressure testing, pressure boundary extraction, and grouped numerical reconstruction to investigate internal transport processes and clarify the formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in large-scale multi-cell stacks. In this framework, pressure data measured at different stack positions are used as boundary conditions to reconstruct the transport behavior of representative cells and analyze stack mass transport characteristics. The reconstructed results are then combined with sensitivity analysis of the experimental data to identify the dominant factors governing stack voltage nonuniformity. Finally, numerical simulations are performed to reproduce the development of low-voltage cells and further verify the proposed mechanism. The results show that the maximum oxygen concentration difference among cells at different stack positions is only 0.4 mol/m 3 , indicating that oxygen distribution differences alone are insufficient to cause significant performance variations. Correlation analysis further indicates that liquid water accumulation at the bottom of the stack is the dominant factor responsible for voltage reduction in the bottom cells. Water-rich simulations demonstrate that increased liquid-water loading in the bottom cells can obstruct oxygen transport and cause voltage decay. This study provides an effective numerical reconstruction method for resolving internal transport processes in multi-cell PEMFC stacks and offers guidance for improving stack cell-voltage consistency.

title: Downside-risk pre-positioning for resilient scheduling of an off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system under extreme weather
abstract: An off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system (DOEH-IES) provides a practical carrier for onsite offshore wind utilization and multi-energy coordination. However, under typhoon conditions, coupled wind-wave effects and platform motion reduce the available power of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), introducing a time-varying downside risk that conventional scheduling methods often fail to mitigate proactively. To address this issue, a downside-risk pre-positioning framework is developed for the DOEH-IES that converts physical FOWT power reductions into actionable scheduling decisions. First, a wind power correction model for FOWTs is established by considering wave, floating-platform motion, and air density variation. A dynamically asymmetric envelope is then constructed to extract the time-varying downside exposure during a typhoon and further develop a downside risk indicator. Subsequently, driven by the risk indicator, BESS capacity is reserved in advance of the onset of high-risk periods. Case studies based on typhoon reanalysis data from the South China Sea show that the proposed dynamic asymmetric envelope achieves risk-oriented boundary characterization without increasing weekly average envelope conservatism, with a pre-typhoon average envelope width of 2.69 MW and a maximum downside deviation of 150 MW during peak disturbance. Relative to the comparison case without risk-informed pre-positioning, the proposed framework eliminates electrical load shedding and reserve insufficiency, increases pre-disturbance available stored energy by 72.5%, and reduces natural gas consumption by 15.0% with only a 2.09% cost increase. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively translate the risk into pre-positioning actions, safeguarding supply and equipment continuity.

title: A methodology for long-term hourly electricity demand forecasting driven by GDP and invariant load profiles
abstract: Long-term electricity demand forecasting is necessary for grid and operations planning, as well as for the analysis and planning of energy transition strategies. However, accurate long-term load forecasting with high temporal resolution remains a challenge as most existing approaches focus on aggregated forecasts, which require accurate prediction of many other variables. This study proposes a parsimonious methodology that uses t-tests to verify the temporal invariance of historical load profiles and the correlation of load with gross domestic product (GDP) to arrive at a long-term hourly load forecast. Applying this methodology first to a controlled benchmark analysing Singapore’s isolated grid, and of multi-year historical data (2004–2022) reveals that its relative hourly load has remained statistically invariant, with an overall percentage deviation of 4.24% across seasonality indices. Utilizing these invariant historical load profiles, five-year-ahead total yearly forecasts were generated using GDP as a predictor, and the hourly loads were then forecasted using hourly seasonality index fractions. The maximum Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) across multiple experiments of six years ahead forecasts was only 6.87%. To systematically evaluate the generalizability and macroeconomic limitations of this top-down methodology beyond Singapore, the methodology was subsequently tested across six European countries. Results show that the methodology achieves high accuracy (MAPE < 8%) for economies with strong GDP-load correlations (Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Spain) but exhibits some performance degradation in decoupled economies where macroeconomic growth no longer drives electricity demand expansion linearly (Germany, UK). Additionally, invariant seasonality metrics were incorporated into a short-term forecasting model based on exponential smoothing (ES), demonstrating comparable or improved accuracy relative to existing machine learning-based methods. The findings show that parsimonious approaches can be effective in arriving at long-term, high resolution forecasts.

title: Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
Who leads the global gas market? Geopolitics and price transmission between the U.S. and Europe
Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Energy policy and energy poverty under geopolitical fragmentation: Evidence on structural constraints
Energy transition under fragmentation: A threshold analysis of inclusive governance in developing economies
abstract: Although institutional quality is widely recognised as important for environmental performance, less is known about whether the governance–energy relationship varies across levels of institutional capacity. This study examines the relationship between inclusive governance, energy intensity, and CO 2 emissions volatility across 71 developing economies in the context of an increasingly fragmented global energy system. We focus on whether the governance–energy relationship varies across levels of institutional capacity. Inclusive governance is measured using a composite index incorporating political institutional quality, gender representation, and income equality. The empirical analysis uses a piecewise panel specification based on the sample median of inclusive governance, with system-GMM and local-projection estimates providing supplementary sensitivity evidence. Inclusive governance is negatively and significantly associated with energy intensity in both governance regimes in the baseline specification, with a somewhat stronger association in the higher-governance regime. However, this nonlinear pattern is sensitive to alternative estimators and breakpoints and is therefore interpreted as suggestive rather than definitive. In contrast, inclusive governance is not significantly associated with CO 2 emissions volatility across most specifications. These findings indicate that the relationship between governance and environmental performance may be outcome-specific: institutional capacity is more clearly associated with energy efficiency than with emissions volatility. The results are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects and suggest that the environmental relevance of governance may vary with both institutional capacity and the outcome being examined.

title: Global expansion of compound drought–heatwave risk
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The increasing frequency of compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events poses a growing threat to water security, agriculture, and ecosystems. However, the evolution, expansion, and spatial reorganization of CDHW hotspots across global land regions remain largely unexplored. Here we track more than 2500 CDHW events using a three-dimensional connected-component (CC3D) labeling approach and show that CDHWs, often treated as spatially stationary extremes, exhibit systematic displacement over time. Larger and longer-lasting events tend to travel farther and faster, expanding the spatial footprint of compound heat and moisture stress. Most contiguous events persist for 6–12 days, displace by up to ~500 km, and reach peak daily spatial extents of 2–5 × 10⁵ km². Migration is strongest in the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and is predominantly eastward. We identify emerging hotspots of increasing CDHW migration potential across the European Plains, western North America, the Amazon, the West African Sahel, Central Asia, and northern Australia. These shifts are linked to evolving large-scale atmospheric circulation and are reinforced by downstream drying through reduced moisture transport and strengthened land–atmosphere coupling. Increasing CDHW migration potential over agricultural landscapes may expand exposure to compound heat and moisture stress, particularly in grazing-dependent regions vulnerable to pastureland-to-scrubland transitions.

title: Redox Properties of the Copper Centers in Particulate Methane Monooxygenase
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Particulate methane monooxygenase (pMMO) and its homolog ammonia monooxygenase (AMO), central enzymes in the global carbon and nitrogen cycles, contain three highly conserved mononuclear copper centers, denoted CuB, CuC, and CuD. While these sites have been well characterized structurally and spectroscopically, with recent studies identifying CuD as the active site, their reduction potentials have not been measured. This knowledge gap has hindered efforts to determine how the two electrons and two protons required for substrate oxidation are sourced and delivered. Here, we have elucidated the redox properties of each copper center in pMMO/AMO by protein film voltammetry using samples with copper occupancies known from cryoelectron microscopy (cryoEM) structures. The reduction potential of the CuB site, −72 to −139 mV, is significantly lower than the ∼400 mV measured for the CuD site, with consistent values determined for pMMOs and AMO from different species. Mutation of a residue in the second sphere of CuB, Glu35, alters the redox potential and impairs cell growth and pMMO activity, indicating that redox chemistry at CuB might be functionally relevant. Finally, a Pourbaix diagram constructed for the CuBII/I and CuDII/I half-reactions suggests that a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process occurs at the CuD site but not at the CuB site. Thermochemical analysis of this proposed PCET process is compatible with electron delivery by a quinol reductant. These results provide new context for future investigations of the pMMO and AMO reaction mechanisms.

title: Life cycle and techno-economic analysis of hydrogen-based ship propulsion concepts in light of future regulatory environments
abstract: The shipping sector faces ongoing challenges in developing pathways to net-zero emission concepts. Hydrogen as an energy carrier offers the opportunity to provide a low- to zero-emission solution, depending on the fuel production pathway. However, high production costs as well as logistical challenges in transporting the fuel globally hinder the economic competitiveness compared to current fossil fuel alternatives. To enable a faster adoption of zero-emission concepts, regulators such as the European Union and the International Maritime Organization have developed mechanisms that provide financial incentives and regulatory specifications. This paper investigates hydrogen-based propulsion concepts for the use case of a short-sea RoPax ferry and a deep-sea liquid hydrogen carrier. System models of different propulsion concepts are used to model their techno-economic performance under different well-to-tank hydrogen production and supply pathways. The proposed IMO GHG Fuel Intensity standards and corresponding penalties/incentives are included in the techno-economic comparison. Results are compared to a fossil-fueled baseline case and a battery-electric benchmark.

title: Tailoring Superhydrophobic Ultramicropores in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Humidity-Resistant Methane Purification
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Efficient purification of methane from raw natural gas under humid conditions remains challenging because water adsorption often degrades the separation performance and structural stability of porous adsorbents. Here we report a topology- and stacking-guided molecular design strategy that integrates ultramicropore engineering with pore-surface fluorination to construct superhydrophobic covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for humidity-resistant methane purification. Two isoreticular fluorinated COFs, TF-COF and NF-COF, were constructed by rationally controlling framework topology and interlayer stacking, generating well-defined ultramicropores for size-selective discrimination of C1–C3 hydrocarbons. Fluorination simultaneously enhances pore-wall hydrophobicity and strengthens host–guest interactions, creating a confined adsorption environment that promotes hydrocarbon recognition while effectively suppressing competitive water adsorption. As a result, NF-COF exhibits a propane uptake of 99.4 cm3 g–1 and an exceptional C3H8/CH4 IAST selectivity of 251.7 at 298 K. Dynamic breakthrough experiments further demonstrate efficient methane purification under both dry and highly humid conditions, with the separation performance fully retained at 97% relative humidity owing to its superhydrophobic surface. Theoretical calculations reveal that densely distributed fluorine atoms generate synergistic pore confinement and multiple C–H···F van der Waals interactions, simultaneously maximizing adsorption capacity and molecular discrimination. These findings establish fluorinated superhydrophobic COFs as a robust platform for energy-efficient natural gas upgrading under industrially relevant humid conditions.

title: Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Tetrapods arose from lobe-finned fishes with a notochord-dominated axial column
                    1–3
                    . During this transition, the skull became separated from the shoulder girdle
                    4–6
                    , giving rise to a neck region. This head–shoulder separation has generated hypotheses suggesting that neck mobility increased during the origin of tetrapods, facilitating the ecological transition towards more terrestrial habitats
                    4,5,7–9
                    . However, incompletely co-ossified vertebral components
                    10
                    have posed a challenge to modelling the mobility of these early tetrapod necks. Here we used material tests on the similarly configured axial columns of sturgeon to predict the capacities of the tetrapod neck region for lateral flexion, extension and rotation across the tetrapod stem. Our model indicates that the soft tissue-dominated axial column was surprisingly rigid, despite lacking co-ossified vertebral components. We estimate that most stem tetrapods could move their heads less than 6° laterally and less than 3° dorsally but could not rotate them. Notably, mobility did not shift in conjunction with the head–shoulder separation that occurred between the origin of tristichopterids (represented by
                    Eusthenopteron
                    ) and that of more crownward stem tetrapods. Therefore, mobility in the tetrapod neck did not serve as a functional driver of head–shoulder separation. Instead, forelimb-driven locomotion, implicated in early tetrapods
                    11–14
                    , provides a better functional explanation for the head–shoulder separation.

title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition
                    1
                    . Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV–V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.

title: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a central anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses immune responses in myeloid cells but can also activate T cells, limiting its therapeutic use in chronic inflammatory diseases owing to narrow efficacy windows and dose-limiting toxicities
                    1–5
                    . Here we show that myeloid and T cells differ in their dependence on JAK-family kinase pairing for IL-10 signalling and function. We took advantage of this differential kinase dependence to engineer a tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist (msIL-10R agonist) that fully recapitulates IL-10’s potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells. Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis reveals a distinct receptor cross-linking geometry of the msIL-10R agonist compared with native IL-10 family cytokines. This tetravalent architecture renders signalling strictly TYK2-dependent and highly sensitive to IL-10Rα and IL-10Rβ receptor abundance, thereby conferring selective activity in myeloid cells. This msIL-10R agonist reduces inflammation in humanized mouse models of lipopolysaccharide challenge, delayed-type hypersensitivity and colitis. A humanized version exhibits IgG-like pharmacokinetics, sustained receptor occupancy and durable myeloid suppression up to 30 days without T cell activation or haematological toxicities in non-human primates. These findings establish a geometry-based strategy for achieving cell-type-selective cytokine signalling and identify the msIL-10R agonist as a therapeutic candidate for myeloid-driven inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel diseases.

title: Structural basis of ligand recognition and gating in mosquito IRs
abstract: Ionotropic receptors (IRs) are essential for insect olfaction, enabling the detection of carboxylic acids, amines, moisture, and temperature cues that mediate critical behaviors, including mosquito host-seeking 1,2. However, the structural mechanisms underlying ligand specificity and channel activation in these receptors remain unclear. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures and functional validation of the IR8a-IR75k complex from the malaria mosquito Anopheles stephensi, a carboxylic acid detector, captured in four states: the ligand-free full-length closed form (apo state), the ligand induced full-length open state, and the nonanoic acid (NA)- and octanoic acid (OA)-bound extracellular domains. These structures reveal a dynamic ligand-binding pocket in IR75k, in which specificity is determined by alkyl chain length and carboxylate geometry. Ligand binding triggers closure of IR75k’s bilobed ligand binding domain (LBD), and this conformational change propagates through conserved mechanical linkers to the transmembrane domain (TMD), functioning as a molecular lever that dilates the pore via outward displacement of transmembrane helices. This gating mechanism was further corroborated by molecular dynamics simulations and electrophysiology. These insights provide an atomic resolution view of IR mediated host detection in mosquitoes and establish a foundation for the rational design of next generation mosquito control strategies targeting host-seeking behavior.

title: Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis
                    1–5
                    . Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential
                    6–10
                    . Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell–transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

title: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion–Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate‐phase film with a Ruddlesden‐Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two‐step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums‐based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm 2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1‐sun illumination (ISOS‐L‐2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.

title: Voltage Hysteresis Induced by Fragile Quasi‐Flat Bands in Oxygen‐Redox Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Cathodes exploiting oxygen redox chemistry underpin the realization of lithium battery systems with specific energies beyond 600 Wh kg −1 . However, voltage hysteresis exceeding 1 V, especially during the first cycle, remains a long‐standing and unresolved challenge, severely limiting energy efficiency and practical deployment. Here, we propose a quasi‐flat‐band framework in which oxygen 2p states near the Fermi level are intrinsically sensitive to perturbations. Even weak perturbations, such as minor lattice distortions during delithiation or thermal vibrations at room temperature, can disproportionately amplify band dispersion and induce hysteresis. This insight reframes the long‐standing design strategy by extending it beyond suppressing structural reconstructions to include control of perturbation‐driven electronic instability. Future materials design should pursue two principles: stabilizing symmetry to sustain quasi‐flat‐band characteristics and engineering orbital hybridization to enhance their robustness against perturbations. This work rethinks the origin and mitigation of voltage hysteresis, bringing oxygen‐redox cathodes closer to reliable operation at high voltages.

Conventional systems, however, rely on physically stacked discrete sensors and von Neumann architectures, causing data redundancy and impaired wearability. title: The Molecular Logic of Platelet-Activating Factor (PAF)
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Platelet-activating factor (PAF) is a well-known if enigmatic lipid signal with important roles in inflammatory responses, allergic reactions, autoimmune diseases, and thrombotic cascades. Several lines of evidence suggest that our current model of PAF’s molecular mechanism is inadequate. This report describes a recontextualized model for PAF. The revised model embeds PAF in a plasmalogen-based molecular mechanism in which activation is a spontaneous chemical reaction triggered by environmental conditions that liberates a PAF receptor (PAF-R) agonist from a membrane-bound phospholipid. The active ligand subsequently undergoes a thermodynamically driven spontaneous rearrangement into an inactive isomer, a feature that controls response lifetime. The revised model is a molecule-autonomous set of transformations that create a response with spatial and temporal control. More generally the revised model’s congruence with a similar model for RORγt supports a picture in which plasmalogens form a part of the immune system that is separate from the cell-based innate and adaptive immune systems.

title: Axial Benzotriazole‐Coordinated Ni Single Atoms Enable Rapid Interfacial Electron Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic Acetylene Semi‐Hydrogenation
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic semi‐hydrogenation of acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) often suffers from inefficient interfacial electron transfer from the photocatalysts to adsorbed C 2 H 2 . Here, we demonstrate that axial coordination of benzotriazole (BTA) to Ni single atoms in C 3 N 4 (BTA‐Ni SAs‐C 3 N 4 ) facilitates interfacial electron‐transfer processes. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, in situ transient surface photovoltage spectroscopy, in situ photochemical infrared spectroscopy, and theoretical simulations reveal that BTA‐coordinated Ni SAs serve as the centers for rapid electron transfer by upshifting the Ni d‐band center and strengthening the orbital overlap between Ni SA and adsorbed C 2 H 2 . Consequently, BTA‐Ni SAs‐C 3 N 4 achieves a very high C 2 H 4 production rate of 32.29 mmol g cat −1 h −1 with a C 2 H 4 selectivity of 97.6% under simulated solar irradiation, which is ∼4‐times higher than that for Ni SAs‐C 3 N 4 . The apparent quantum yield at 365 nm is up to 4.65%, superior to reported photocatalytic acetylene semi‐hydrogenation. This work highlights the importance of interfacial charge transfer in photocatalytic acetylene hydrogenation and provides a rational strategy for designing high‐performance photocatalysts.
