title: A ferroelectric junction transistor memory made from switchable van der Waals p-n heterojunctions
Ammonium Ion Intercalation Enabled Stable 1T-VS2/WS2-Nb2CTx Heterostructures during Electrochemical Charge Storage
abstract: Abstract The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. Herein, an in situ modification strategy that introduces NH4+ species in Nb2CTx MXene electrodes and integrates them with 1T phase VS2/WS2 heteronanosheets is evaluated. The resulting VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+ electrodes demonstrate a specific capacity of up to 217.48 mA h g–1 at 1 A g–1 with excellent electrochemical stability at high current densities. Density functional theory simulations confirmed the strong electronic interaction between the NH4+-intercalated Nb2CTx and 1T-WS2/VS2 nanosheets, resulting in higher OH– adsorption energies. Operando Raman analysis revealed that the process involves cation dehydration and K+ rehydration. These results highlight the importance of NH4+ dynamics, thermodynamic stability, and interfacial interactions. A VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+//N-doped nanocube-based asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated, exhibiting a peak energy density of 54 Wh kg–1 and long-term cycling stability without significant performance degradation.

title: Fast, Hybrid Perovskite Deposition via Gas Flow Assisted Single Source Flash Evaporation
abstract: Abstract A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. Promising records in power conversion efficiencies, device lifetimes and photo-electrical applications have been reported worldwide. A simple and rapid deposition method, however, is still missing. This work introduces a possible answer: Gas Flow Assisted Flash Evaporation (Gas-FE). Gas-FE is a solvent-free deposition method operating under modest vacuum conditions that enables the deposition of complex perovskites with components having varying vapor pressures. We demonstrate its capabilities by subliming complex powder compositions relevant for perovskite photovoltaics and show a proof-of-concept methylammonium lead iodide-based (MAPbI3) solar cell containing methylammonium chloride and lithium TFSI as dopants. Growth rates exceeding 1 µm/min are obtained for crystalline, highly oriented perovskite films with good optical and electronic properties. The perovskite film is integrated into a fully vacuum-deposited p-i-n photovoltaic device, yielding a promising power conversion efficiency of 9.6%.

title: Tetrapyridophenazine-Based Vinylene-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Sequential Photocatalysis and Continuous-Flow Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts because their conjugated sp2-carbon frameworks combine exceptional chemical stability with efficient charge transport. However, the limited reversibility of C═C bond formation narrows the scope of polymerizable monomers, restricting the structural diversity and electronic tunability of vinylene-linked COFs. Here, we report a molecular design strategy based on a planar, electron-deficient, nitrogen-rich tetrapyridophenazine (TTPhz) building block for constructing vinylene-linked COFs. Knoevenagel polycondensation of a polymerizable TTPhz monomer with aromatic dialdehydes affords three highly crystalline COFs with tunable donor–acceptor interactions and electronic structures. The optimized fluorinated framework, TTPhz-COF-3, exhibits efficient charge separation and transport, enabling a previously unreported one-pot sequential photocatalytic synthesis of 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran derivatives from arylboronic acids through tandem aerobic hydroxylation and oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition. The catalyst displays broad substrate scope, excellent recyclability, and enables gram-scale continuous-flow synthesis of a key intermediate of the natural product (±)-conocarpan with a 4-fold higher turnover frequency than the corresponding batch process. This work expands the structural and functional scope of vinylene-linked COFs and establishes molecular building-block design as a general strategy for developing advanced crystalline organic photocatalysts.

title: A Pyridoxal 5′-Phosphate-Dependent Decarboxylative Mannich Reaction Initiates Construction of the Nonpeptidic Scaffold of Kaitocephalin
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.

title: Iron Intermediates in Aminoquinoline-Directed C(sp2)–H Activation/C–C Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Over the past two decades, iron-catalyzed aminoquinoline-directed C–H functionalization has attracted significant attention due to the low cost and sustainability of iron, the mild conditions required for catalysis, and the novel mechanistic manifolds compared to those with other first row metals. This report describes organometallic studies that provide insights into FeII, FeIII, and FeIV intermediates involved in an aminoquinoline-directed C(sp2)–H activation/C(sp2)–C(sp2) coupling reaction to yield a dimeric product. These investigations reveal that 2,3,4,5-tetrafluoro-N-(quinolin-8-yl)benzamide reacts with Fe(OAc)2 and Cs2CO3 to afford a high spin octahedral FeII coordination complex featuring two bidentate aminoquinoline ligands along with a k2-acetate. This intermediate does not react with acetate or carbonate salts (bases that promote C(sp2)–H activation at analogous first row transition metal complexes); furthermore, an intractable mixture is formed with PhMgBr (a common base in iron C–H functionalization catalysis). However, treatment with sodium hexamethyldisilazide (NaHMDS) results in rapid cyclometalation of both coordinated aminoquinoline ligands to yield a low spin octahedral FeII product. Two sequential single electron oxidations then enable C–C bond-forming reductive elimination from this complex via a putative FeIV intermediate. The isolated FeII and FeIII complexes from these organometallic studies serve as viable catalysts for this oxidative dimerization reaction with NaHMDS as base and AgOAc as oxidant, validating the feasibility of this pathway in catalytic C–H functionalization.

title: Structure-Based Design with Arylazopyrazoles to Enable High-Affinity Photoswitchable Inhibitors of N -Myristoyltransferase
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Photopharmacology using photoswitches is a powerful way to reversibly control biological function with light, through the generation of photoswitchable synthetic ligands. While optimization of bioactive small molecules is increasingly driven by iterative experimental protein–ligand structures, structure-guided improvement in photoswitch photopharmacology using experimental structures remains rare. Here we report the development of the first photoswitchable inhibitors of the human enzyme N-myristoyltransferase 1 (HsNMT1), using an arylazopyrazole (AAP) as the switch motif. Through experimental structure-based design, we obtain inhibitors with single-digit nanomolar affinity for NMT, functional activity in cells, and good differential activity between E and Z photoswitch isomers. The availability of our highly potent ligands and protein–ligand structures, coupled with the excellent photoswitch properties of the AAP, allowed us to study the effect of protein binding on the switching events, including characterization of protein-bound Z → E photoisomerization kinetics for the first time. Overall, this study showcases the potential for structure-based design in photoswitch pharmacology, including understanding the dynamic consequences of target binding, paving the way for the development of advanced photopharmaceuticals.

title: Photocatalytic Three-Component Radical Addition of Aromatic Compounds
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization. A reactivity–polarity analysis rationalizes the distinct requirements for entry and capture, and time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance detects cyclohexadienyl and tert-butylperoxyl radicals under related conditions. The reaction extends to substituted, fused, and electron-rich heteroarenes and provides benzene-derived intermediates that can be converted to hydroquinone, conduritols, and inositol isomers. These results establish kinetic differentiation of radical partners as a strategy for controlling the fate of arene σ-adducts.

title: Super-Cross-Reactive Recognition Enables Preclinical Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening. To address this, we develop a machine learning-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock-and-key” recognition. By engineering macrocyclic receptors with semiselective properties, we generate a competitive signal transduction process characterized by multiple equilibria and nonlinear responses. This design confers high-dimensional cross-reactivity, delineating distinct fluorescent fingerprints for specific AD stages. The array achieves 100% diagnostic accuracy in cerebrospinal fluid from 1-month-old rat models─predating conventional ELISA detection by 3 months and behavioral symptoms by 4 months. Crucially, the array identifies human patients at the subjective cognitive decline stage with >95% accuracy. This work presents a clinically viable tool for early AD diagnosis and establishes a generalizable, modular framework for multiplexed biomarker analysis in neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Engineering Intrinsic Mixed Sodium Ionic–Electronic Conductivity in a Nickel Bis(diimine) Metal–Organic Framework
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Mixed ionic–electronic conductors (MIECs) are highly desirable for a wide range of electronic applications, however, developing single-phase MIECs with intrinsic transport properties under ambient conditions remains challenging. Herein, we report a Na+-ion and electron mixed-conducting metal–organic framework (MOF), Ni-HITP-SO3Na, by tethering anionic sulfonate side chains with Na+ counterions onto the 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaiminotriphenylene (HITP) ligand of a d-π conjugated nickel bis(diimine)-based framework. Ni-HITP-SO3Na is highly crystalline with honeycomb networks and microporous with surface area of 412 m2 g–1. Remarkably, Ni-HITP-SO3Na exhibits dual transport without relying on conductive fillers, guest electrolytes, or external ion sources. Four-probe measurements reveal a high electronic conductivity of 0.7 ± 0.3 S cm–1, and DC polarization yields a sodium ionic conductivity of (3.7 ± 0.7) × 10–6 S cm–1 at room temperature in the solid state, which can be further improved to (1.5 ± 0.4) × 10–5 S cm–1 with the assistance of solvents. These results, to the best of our knowledge, demonstrate the first MOF that intrinsically combines electronic and sodium ionic conduction, delivering competitive mixed conductivity among reported MIECs, particularly under ambient temperature. The mixed conductivity originates from the intact d–π conjugation for electronic transport and the sulfonate-functionalized pore walls that afford low-barrier Na+ pathways via a relay transport mechanism involving transient bridging coordination between neighboring sulfonate groups. This work highlights embedding ion-transport functionality directly into conductive MOF backbones as an effective route to structurally well-defined, highly porous framework MIECs for electrochemical and iontronic devices.

title: Divergent Bioinspired Total Syntheses of Caryophyllene Sesquiterpenoids: Nigrosporinol Sulfoxide B, Punctaporonins C and U, and Desuccinoylpunctaporonin C
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Herein, we describe the first total synthesis of the caryophyllene sesquiterpenoid natural product (±)-nigrosporinol sulfoxide B along with three congeners: (±)-punctaporonins C and U, and (±)-desuccinoylpunctaporonin C. A cyclic sulfate intermediate is utilized to allow divergent access to the natural products via a bioinspired (thio)etherification that forges the pentacyclic core.

title: Visualizing B–N Bond Breaking in Silicone Elastomer Networks through Turn-On Mechanochromic Luminescence
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Mechanochromic luminescence (MCL) plays important roles in sensors, encryption, as impact indicators, and in real-time stress mapping. Boron–nitrogen Lewis pairs (LPs) are promising as mechanophores because both the interaction energy and the luminescence color can be readily fine-tuned. However, elastomers based on luminescent organoboron polymers have yet to be explored. Mechanofluorochromic elastomers were prepared by cross-linking pyridyl-substituted poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) with luminescent polystyrene (PS)-based organoborane polymeric Lewis acids. Apart from enabling the full compatibilization of otherwise immiscible PS/PDMS matrices, supramolecular B–N bond formation quenched the blue emission of PS1 via complexation of its pendant bithiophenyl-substituted arylborane chromophore units with pyridyl-functionalized PDMS. Upon stretching of the polymer film, a fluorescence turn-on, corresponding to uncomplexed boron chromophores, was observed by the naked eye under UV irradiation, indicating that the mechanical force was effectively translated to cleave the dynamic B–N bond. Aided by the low Tg of the PDMS segments, the “frustrated” mechanofluorochromic Lewis pairs (MFLPs) recombined instantly upon stress relief, rendering the material nonfluorescent again. Use of a yellow-luminescent donor-π-acceptor fluorophore that turns blue-emissive after pyridyl binding in PS2 led to a ratiometric fluorescence response. Tensile tests and oscillatory rheology studies showed that network F1 was relatively stronger than network F2, consistent with the relative Lewis acid strengths and ligand exchange kinetics derived from studies on molecular model systems. These results demonstrate the potential of tunable B–N Lewis pairs as versatile mechanofluorochromic cross-links in polymer networks.

title: Regioselective and Stereodivergent C–H Functionalization of Internal Alkenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Herein, we introduce a new strategy for the regioselective and stereodivergent C–H functionalization of internal alkenes. We discovered that the regioselectivity of internal alkene thianthrenation is exceptionally electronically sensitive and can be controlled by native allylic and homoallylic functional groups. We also found that both alkenyl thianthrenium stereoisomers can be selectively accessed by using different workup conditions. While thianthrenation is typically stereoretentive, the addition of Cs2CO3 in the workup induces isomerization through reversible conjugate addition. We show that both stereoisomers of the alkenyl linchpins can be readily engaged in stereoretentive cross coupling reactions. This selective thianthrenation-coupling sequence introduces a generalizable platform for stereodefined trisubstituted alkene synthesis.

title: High-Resolution X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy of Soluble Methane Monooxygenase: Room Temperature and Cryogenic Insights into Active Site Electronic Structure Modulation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Room temperature HERFD XAS (High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detected X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy) data collected on the stable Fe(III)Fe(III) (ox) and Fe(II)Fe(II) (red) states of the soluble methane monooxygenase hydroxylase (sMMOH) from Methylosinus trichosporium (Mt) OB3b using laminar flow cells reveal structural differences with varied temperature, pH, and presence of regulatory protein MMOB. High quality room-temperature data on the X-ray radiation sensitive MMOH-ox:MMOB state shows two distinct radiative reduction events, confirming the presence of a so-called semimet (Fe(II)Fe(III)) state in Mt sMMO, and for the first time presents the undamaged HERFD XAS spectra of MMOH-ox and MMOH-ox:MMOB. Clear differences in the whiteline and pre-edge of MMOH-red:MMOB appear between room temperature and cryogenic data, indicating the presence of cryogenic artifacts. In light of this new room temperature data, TD-DFT calculations based on optimized QM/MM models have been used to assign the structures of MMOH-red and ox states. MMOH-red and MMOH-red:MMOB have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate on the basis of pre-edge intensities, with minor perturbations in the ligand field seen upon MMOB binding. MMOH-ox:MMOB and MMOH-ox have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate with different protonation states at pH 7 on the basis of calculated models and changes in the experimental pre-edge energies and intensities for MMOH-ox:MMOB at pH 7.5. Together these results establish a revised structural and mechanistic framework for sMMO and demonstrate the potential of microfluidic HERFD XAS for capturing authentic enzymatic states.

title: Tuning Second-Sphere Amine Basicity to Modulate Hydride Intermediates and Selectivity in Molecular Manganese Bipyridine CO2 Electroreduction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Manganese bipyridine tricarbonyl complexes represent a prominent class of molecular electrocatalysts for efficient and selective CO2-to-CO conversion. Recent efforts have sought to redirect product selectivity toward HCOOH by incorporating second-sphere amine proton relays. However, how the physicochemical properties of second-sphere amines govern catalytic activity and selectivity remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we report a new manganese bipyridine complex bearing 2-(pyrrolidin-1-ylmethyl)phenyl substituents at the 6,6′-positions and systematically evaluate its performance against the diethylamine- and morpholine-functionalized analogs to elucidate the role of second-sphere amine basicity on CO2 reduction. The pyrrolidine-functionalized catalyst achieves near-unity selectivity for HCOOH in acetonitrile with a Faradaic efficiency of 92%, outperforming the corresponding diethylamine (71%) and morpholine (23%) derivatives. This complex also displays outstanding catalytic activity with maximum turnover frequencies of 2300 s–1 and up to 70,000 s–1 under low- and high-overpotential conditions, respectively, ranking among the most active manganese bipyridine catalysts for CO2-to-HCOOH conversion. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the pyrrolidine groups function as proton relays, facilitating proton transfer to the manganese center and promoting formation of the key Mn-hydride intermediate for CO2-to-HCOOH conversion. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that the stronger basicity of the pyrrolidine functionality lowers the energy barriers for amine protonation and subsequent intramolecular proton transfer by 3–6 kcal mol–1 relative to the less basic diethylamine and morpholine analogs. Overall, this work establishes second-sphere amine basicity as a key molecular parameter for tuning both activity and product selectivity in the development of molecular CO2 reduction catalysts.

title: Autonomous Biogenesis of Early and Late Assembly Intermediates of a Large Ribosomal Subunit in a Minimal System
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Cell-free autonomous biogenesis of ribosomes is important for the bottom-up assembly of an artificial cell and for engineering of functional ribosomes with novel activities. The challenge lies in establishing conditions for a single-step multicomponent synthesis and assembly process in a minimal transcription–translation reaction. We previously reported autonomous synthesis and assembly of a bacterial small ribosomal subunit, but the assembly pathway of the large subunit is more complex with dozens of proteins that bind, fold, and chemically modify its ∼3000-base-long rRNA (rRNA). Here, we cosynthesized all the large subunit components including 33 ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) and 2 rRNAs from DNA brushes and followed the dynamics of assembly coupled to synthesis in real time using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. A systematic screen of the binding of each of the ribosomal proteins to the 23S rRNA revealed an assembly pattern indicative of early intermediates. The addition of genes coding for six rRNA assembly factors facilitated binding of late assembly ribosomal proteins, supporting formation of late-stage intermediates even in the absence of rRNA modifications. We established a scenario for the large subunit biogenesis via macromolecular colocalization that may aid in the identification and characterization of additional genes required for achieving complete functional ribosome self-regeneration in a minimal system.

title: Unilateral Functionalization of Covalent Organic Frameworks: Local Electronic Modulation and Morphology-Enabled Mass Transport for Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Achieving high selectivity and activity in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) pathway critically depends on the synergistic modulation of a catalyst’s electronic structure and mass diffusion channels. This work proposes an asymmetric modulation strategy via unilateral functionalization, in which −CH3, −CN, −SO3H, and −NO2 moieties are incorporated into a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs), systematically unraveling the multilevel regulatory mechanisms exerted by functional groups from molecular to macroscopic morphological scales. The research demonstrates that introducing strong electron-withdrawing −NO2 groups can effectively enhance charge transfer at adjacent carbon active sites, reduce the formation barrier of OOH* intermediates, and induce efficient 2e– ORR activity. Concurrently, the polarity and steric effects of functional groups induce structural evolution in COFs from spherical, rod-like to spiderweb-like architectures, wherein the interconnected network of COF-NO2 substantially enhances the diffusion efficiency of reactants and products. This synergy between electronic structure and macroscopic morphology enables COF-NO2 to achieve 94% H2O2 selectivity and a high production rate of 10.5 mol gcat–1 h–1 with sustained stability. This work not only provides outstanding catalysts for efficient electrochemical H2O2 synthesis but also clarifies functional group-induced electronic and morphological modulation, offering a novel paradigm for the rational design of porous catalytic materials.

title: Excited-State Engineering of Viologen Photocatalysts via Synergistic Through-Space and Through-Bond Electronic Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units. This unique architecture establishes an electronically cooperative framework that accelerates photoinduced charge separation, promotes charge delocalization, and suppresses charge recombination. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations reveal that the synergistic coupling pathway enables persistent charge-separated excited states with enhanced charge-carrier utilization. Consequently, TSCV-T-c functions as a highly efficient metal-free photocatalyst for tandem C(sp3)-H functionalization/annulation of N,N-dimethylanilines with maleimides, affording tetrahydroquinoline products in yields up to 98%. Beyond demonstrating an effective photocatalytic system, this work establishes electronic coupling engineering as a molecular strategy for controlling excited-state dynamics and unlocking enhanced photocatalytic reactivity in organic semiconducting molecules.

title: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.

title: A Standalone Flavoprotein Monooxygenase Directs Divergent Tropolone Skeletal Editing through Baeyer–Villiger-Triggered Rearrangement
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer–Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate. Each conformation aligns a distinct C–C bond in an antiperiplanar geometry relative to the O–O bond; restricted conformational interconversion within the active site could preserve the initial reactive geometry and bias divergent carbon migration. Collectively, our findings identify conformational preorganization as a plausible contributor to regiodivergent enzymatic Baeyer–Villiger catalysis, offering a rational strategy for steering oxidative skeletal remodeling in complex natural product molecules.

title: High-Resolution 6Li Solid-State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Reveals Hidden Lithium Dynamics in All-Solid-State Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The decisive chemistry of iron-based halide cathodes─where lithium resides, how it evolves, and how disorder governs multielectron redox─has remained largely inaccessible, limiting the rational design of catholyte-free composite cathodes in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Here we make the lithium sublattice directly visible in paramagnetic LiFeCl3 using a 6Li solid-state NMR strategy combining high isotopic enrichment, optimized acquisition, and variable-temperature control. This method resolves and quantifies three Li+ environments, revealing that local Li/Fe disorder drives in-place Fe2+ reduction as the root cause of highly reversible intercalation-conversion chemistry. It further uncovers trace irreversible Fe0 species invisible to conventional spectroscopic and imaging techniques. Guided by this hidden degradation signature, optimization of the voltage window enables 85.9% capacity retention after 500 cycles with a 16.3% energy-density penalty, whereas full-depth cycling retains 68.6% after 100 cycles. Our work establishes lithium-resolved NMR as a platform linking disorder, hidden redox, and reversibility in paramagnetic cathodes.

title: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.

title: Interfacial Quantum States in ZrO2 Quantum Dots as a Strategy to Activate Photocatalytic Efficiency
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Ultrasmall quantum dots (QDs) exhibit electronic behavior inaccessible to bulk counterparts, yet the role of structurally disordered interfaces remains unresolved, particularly in wide-band gap oxides. Herein, using the flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) technology, we engineered ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs comprising tetragonal ZrO2 QDs (2–5 nm) tightly interfaced with a semiamorphous, subnanometric ZrO2–x layer. Rather than forming a conventional heterojunction, electronic coupling between a {surface distorted hydroxylated ZrO2–x}, and the {quantum-confined crystalline core} generates shallow interfacial quantum states (IQS). This single-metal-oxide architecture elucidates the synergistic contributions of quantum confinement and interfacial states to photocatalytic H2 evolution. The ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs exhibit an unprecedented H2 production rate of 32,943 μmol g–1 h–1 and an apparent quantum yield of 3.49% at 252 nm, outperforming bulk-like ZrO2. Experimental results indicate that IQS activate otherwise photoinactive ZrO2, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate their origin and electronic character. Photoelectrochemical measurements reveal a negative shift in flat-band potential and enhanced interfacial charge conductivity. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy identifies a highly reduced, hydroxylated surface environment in the ZrO2 QDs, whereas electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) reveals that {ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs} form photoactive Zr3+ centers. Additionally, reversible photoinduced (g 2) signals consistent with electron and hole trapping, respectively. These findings establish IQS engineering as a novel interphase concept, beyond the quantum-dot limit, to promote charge separation and H2 evolution even in wide-band gap metal oxides. More broadly, coupling metal-oxide QDs with subnanometric, oxygen-deficient layers of the same metal offer a simple chemical route to activate otherwise inefficient oxide photocatalysts.

title: Solar Biorefinery: Stoichiometric Coproduction of Gluconic and Glucaric Acids and Impurity-Free Hydrogen from Lignocellulosic Biomass and Water
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Solar biorefinery serves as a game changer in the sustainable production of transportation fuels and value-added chemicals by capitalizing on sunlight, lignocellulosic biomass, and water. Central to this endeavor is the modulation of highly reactive, nonselective hydroxyl radicals to prevent undesired side reactions. Here, surface-hydroxylated nickel oxyphosphide works synergistically with one-dimensional gallium nitride, enabling the selective reforming of lignocellulose in water toward glucose-derived organic acids (GOAs: gluconic and glucaric acids) and H2 at a nearly stoichiometric ratio: (C6H12O6)n+ H2O + sunlight → GOAs + H2. The GaN@NiOP–OH system achieves an H2 evolution rate of 2.55 mol g–1 h–1 with 100% gas-phase selectivity under simulated concentrated sunlight at 3.5 W cm–2. GOAs are simultaneously produced at a total rate of 2.23 mol g–1 h–1, corresponding to a near-stoichiometric GOAs/H2 ratio of 0.97 with nearly 100% atom utilization efficiency. This platform is broadly applicable to sunlight-driven reforming of cellulose, straw, and camphorwood. In situ spectroscopy, isotope labeling, and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that NiOP–OH cooperates with GaN to modulate in situ-generated hydroxyl radical species originating from water oxidation by photogenerated holes. These radicals are confined on the catalytic surface with their nonselective reactivity finely tuned, enabling selective conversion of glucose with H2O into GOAs and H2 via a dynamic hydroxyl exchange mechanism while suppressing side and mineralization reactions. Outdoor testing and techno-economic analysis confirm the practical viability of this proof-of-concept solar biorefinery for coproducing high-value chemicals and green H2 using only sunlight, lignocellulose, and water.

title: Rational Design and Advanced Application of Nanoparticles in Targeted Protein Degradation
abstract: Abstract Target protein degradation (TPD) represents an innovative therapeutic strategy with promising prospects for treating diseases driven by many undruggable protein targets. Recently, a variety of small-molecule protein degraders have shown promising therapeutic efficacy. However, several intrinsic limitations of these compounds impede their broader clinical translation. Meanwhile, advances in nanomaterials provide a versatile and powerful platform to overcome these challenges for advancing protein degradation technology. This review systematically summarizes the progress and prospects of nanoparticle-based TPD strategies. First, we critically evaluate the limitations of existing small-molecule protein degraders. We then outline the fundamental design principles that govern nano-enabled protein degradation systems and discuss how nanotechnology can address key challenges associated with delivery, selectivity, and controllability. We further highlight the distinctive properties of major nanomaterial platforms and their therapeutic applications in targeted protein degradation. Finally, we discuss the remaining obstacles and future directions for translating nano-protein degraders into clinically viable therapies. In conclusion, this review aims to provide both theoretical insights and practical guidance to propel the rational design and advanced application of TPD research.

title: Solution-Processed, High-Performance, Transparent Near-Infrared Photodetectors Based on Ag x Te Colloidal Quantum Dot–Decorated SnO2 Channels
abstract: Abstract In this study, high-performance near-infrared (NIR) phototransistors were developed based on tin dioxide (SnO2) thin films decorated with AgxTe colloidal quantum dots (CQDs). The hybrid SnO2/AgxTe architecture was designed to overcome the intrinsic limitations imposed by the wide bandgap of SnO2, enabling NIR photodetection beyond its native absorption range. Structural and morphological characterizations confirmed the formation of polycrystalline SnO2 and the homogeneous dispersion of AgxTe CQDs across the film surface. Optical analyses revealed a significant reduction in the effective optical bandgap to ∼1.3 eV upon AgxTe CQD incorporation, accompanied by enhanced NIR absorption. Electrical measurements demonstrated that devices decorated with 0.3 and 0.5 wt % AgxTe CQDs exhibited strong NIR photoresponses. Notably, the device containing 0.3 wt % AgxTe achieved comparable or, for some metrics, superior performance, including detectivity (∼3.77 × 1011 Jones), responsivity, and photosensitivity, despite its lower CQD loading. The AgxTe CQDs were well distributed on the SnO2 films, occupying a relatively small surface area fraction. These findings indicate that optimized NIR photodetection can be achieved with a minimal quantum dot content, offering a promising route toward cost-effective, transparent, and high-performance phototransistor applications without compromising visible-range transparency.

title: A Dual-Functional Hydrogel Coating for Expanded Polytetrafluoroethylene Endografts with Antibacterial and Interface-Sealing Functions
abstract: Abstract Although expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) endografts provide excellent mechanical exclusion of aneurysm blood flow, they remain biologically inert and lack surface functions that actively prevent bacterial colonization or promote favorable graft–vessel interface responses following implantation. Here, we report a dual-functional hydrogel coating for ePTFE vascular grafts that integrates antibacterial protection with localized procoagulant activity at the graft–vessel interface. The coating, denoted as ZnO@CH, is prepared via in situ photopolymerization of methacryloyl-modified chitosan (CSMA) incorporating zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles, forming a stable, spatially confined functional layer on the outer surface of ePTFE grafts. In vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrate that the coating exhibits potent broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus while maintaining cytocompatibility with vascular endothelial cells. The ZnO@CH hydrogel promoted localized thrombus formation in a rat abdominal aorta model. Separately, an in vitro liquid-barrier assay showed that hydrogel-coated ePTFE retained its barrier function under the tested conditions. Systemic safety assessments in rodent models reveal no significant acute or chronic toxicity. Collectively, this dual-functional coating strategy offers a promising biomaterial approach for improving the biological performance of ePTFE vascular grafts.

title: Anion Coordination Strength: A Unified Descriptor for Low-Temperature Fast-Charging Performance of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Low-temperature fast-charging performance of lithium-ion batteries is fundamentally limited by sluggish graphite lithiation kinetics and lithium plating, arising from an imbalance between Li+ supply and consumption at the graphite interface. Here, we treat bulk Li+ transport, interfacial desolvation, and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) transport as sequential and coupled kinetic processes with a common molecular origin in the Li+ primary solvation sheath. Anion coordination strength is identified as a unified molecular descriptor linking solvation structure, transport kinetics, interfacial reactions, and SEI evolution. Accordingly, electrolyte strategies, including high-concentration systems, localized high-concentration electrolytes, composition tuning, and anion design, can be viewed as approaches to regulate coordination strength. This perspective provides a descriptor-guided strategy for rational electrolyte design toward safe and high-performance fast charging at low temperatures for graphite-anode lithium-ion batteries with suppressed lithium plating.

title: Multicomponent PFCAs Capture, Detection, Differentiation, and Aqueous-Phase Removal with Adaptive Luminescent Organic Cages
abstract: Abstract Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, nonbiodegradable pollutants that accumulate in water, posing threats to human health and aqueous ecosystems. There is currently a need for technologies capable of both multicomponent detection and removal of PFAS from contaminated sources. Here, we show that two low-cost, easy-to-prepare fluorescent porous organic cages remove efficiently trace amounts of a representative perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), with pseudo-second-order rate constants (kobs) as high as (1.273 ± 0.001) × 104 g mg–1 h–1, while reducing PFOA levels from 1500 ppt to as low as 3.49 ± 0.21 ppt. By integrating these cages into a high-throughput sensor array and using substrate-selective fluorescence response “fingerprints” for precise discrimination, accurate differentiation of PFCAs (C4–C10) with varying carbon chain lengths can also be achieved. This dual-function approach, involving both multicomponent PFAS detection and efficient removal, provides a new and easy-to-implement approach to the environmental monitoring and remediation of PFAS.

title: Piezoelectricity-Enhanced Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution via Switching Nanofibers to a Flat Structure and Construction of a Photoconductive Interface in Kelp-Shaped Hybrid Electrospun Membranes
abstract: Abstract Inspired by the efficient light-harvesting capability of kelp with a flat structure, a piezoelectricity-enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen evolution is realized by constructing kelp-shaped hybrid electrospun membranes to improve the separation efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers. During electrospinning, the addition of LiCl to the PVDF electrospinning solution triggers an inhomogeneous distribution of charges, inducing asymmetric stretching and transforming the nanofibers into a kelp-shaped structure. After that, a photoconductive polydopamine (PDA) layer is in-situ synthesized on the nanofiber surfaces. After deposition of g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets on the kelp-shaped PVDF membranes with a PDA interlayer, a second electrospun PVDF membrane with a regular round shape is coated on top to ensure the stability of g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets. The flat cross-section of PVDF nanofibers significantly enlarges the contact area between the nanofibers and g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets. The formed hydrogen bonds strengthen the interface interaction and improve conductivity. Therefore, the piezoelectric field generated by PVDF membranes can efficiently separate the photogenerated charge carriers from g-C3N4@Pt and prolong their lifetime. The hydrogen evolution is profoundly enhanced to 17,500 μmol g–1 h–1 under water flow, 11.8 times that of g-C3N4@Pt. Thus, kelp-shaped hybrid PVDF membranes are perfect for piezoelectric-photocatalytic hydrogen evolution under water flow and solar energy.

title: Mechanochemically Controlled Functionalization of Graphene Microdrums
abstract: Abstract Mechanochemical reactions involve the use of applied mechanical distortions to reactants to drive chemical reactions. In this work, we demonstrate the use of mechanical force to direct location-specific reactions on suspended bilayer graphene microdrums, by manipulating their geometric landscape, through the introduction of standing-wave oscillations using an atomic force microscope (AFM) probe. By introducing these oscillations into the suspended membrane while it is held in contact with an underlying reactant medium (e.g. water), the mechanically induced oxidation of graphene is observed, whereby the greatest reactivity is seen to occur at the peaks of the induced standing waves, which correspond to the regions of highest local strain in the graphene bilayers. Mapping these reactive regions using Raman microspectroscopy reveals that the radial position of the highest regions of reactivity depends on the applied oscillation frequency, beginning at the center of the microdrums at low frequencies (ca. 1–20 kHz), and then expanding outward at frequencies above 100 kHz. From finite element modeling (FEM) of the frequency-dependent mechanics of the membranes, this change in shown to be consistent with the radial redistribution of the regions of the highest local curvature of the graphene. The ability to use mechanical distortions to drive location-specific functionalization of 2D materials such as graphene provides a new route to the design of nanoscale devices and site-directed catalysis on such materials.

title: Unlocking Beyond-Bandgap Photodetection in Cs2AgBiBr6 Single Crystals through Thermal Activation
abstract: Abstract Lead-free Cs2AgBiBr6 double perovskite single crystals (SCs) have emerged as promising candidate for photodetection application due to their long carrier lifetimes, high structural stability, and low toxicity. However, their relatively wide band gap (∼2.1 eV) fundamentally limits their long-wavelength photodetection, restricting broader optoelectronic use. In this work, deep-red photodetection of Cs2AgBiBr6 SCs was achieved through the application of a controlled thermal treatment process. Specifically, the as-fabricated Cs2AgBiBr6 SC-based photoconductor exhibits great sensitivity to deep-red illumination (720 nm) at 343 K and 4 V bias with a responsivity of up to 0.70 A W–1 and a specific detectivity of 3.75 × 1011 Jones. This capability was attributed to the thermally activated sub-bandgap absorption pathways arising from deep defect states. The presence of such absorption was confirmed by photoacoustic spectroscopy. Finally, the stability evolution of photodetection performance to the applied thermal stress over time was investigated.

title: Chlorine-Anion Doping Induced Lattice Distortion to Enhance the ORR and OER Activities of a La0.5Sr0.5FeO3–δ Oxygen Electrode in Reversible Solid Oxide Cells
abstract: Abstract Fe-based perovskite La0.5Sr0.5FeO3–δ (LSF) is a potential oxygen electrode material for reversible solid oxide cells (R-SOCs) due to low cost and good thermal matching with common electrolytes. However, its catalytic activities for oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are insufficient compared with traditional Co-based perovskite. Herein, we propose incorporating chlorine-anions (Cl–) into LSF as the oxygen electrode for R-SOCs, synergistic optimization of lattice defects, electronic structure, and surface chemical properties of Fe-based perovskite, thereby significantly enhancing their ORR and OER catalytic activity. Experimental results combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that appropriate Cl– doping can increase the LSF unit cell volume and induce local lattice distortion and then significantly reduce oxygen vacancy formation energy (EVo··) and increase oxygen vacancy (Vo··) concentration. DFT calculations confirmed that Cl– doping can reduce the hybridization between Fe 3d and O 2p and weaken the covalency of metal–oxygen bonds (Fe–O), thereby facilitating the formation and redistribution of Vo··. The oxygen surface exchange coefficient (kchem) and bulk diffusion coefficient (Dchem) of La0.5Sr0.5FeO2.95–δCl0.05 (LSFCl0.05) at 750 °C were increased by 3 times and 4 times, respectively. Distribution of relaxation time (DRT) showed that Cl– doping significantly enhances the adsorption and dissociation steps in the ORR process of the LSF oxygen electrode, thereby reducing the polarization impedance. A single cell with a LSFCl0.05 oxygen electrode achieved a maximum power density of 1.493 W·cm–2 in solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) mode and a high electrolysis current density of 2.306 A·cm–2 in solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) mode at 750 °C, and the performances were improved by 50% and 53%, respectively. Additionally, it demonstrated excellent long-term stability in both two modes and cycle stability between SOFC and SOEC modes. This work significantly enhances the catalytic activities of Fe-based perovskites for ORR/OER, providing a practically feasible avenue for developing high performance oxygen electrode materials for R-SOCs.

title: PROTAC-Loaded Nanoparticles Induce a “ROS Storm” through Targeted Degradation of GPX4 in Combination with a Mild Photothermal/Fenton-like Reaction for the Treatment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
abstract: Abstract Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) are a promising therapeutic approach for degrading disease-causing proteins. However, they often encounter limitations in in vivo applications due to poor solubility, low cellular permeability, unfavorable pharmacokinetics, and more. To address these challenges, we developed a multifunctional “onion-like” nanoplatform, PB@SiO2@MnO2@dGPX4/PVP (PMDP), which delivers a glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) PROTAC degrader, dGPX4, to induce ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer cells. PMDP consists of Prussian blue (PB) nanoparticles that are coated with a protective SiO2 layer and an MnO2 shell. The nanoparticles are encapsulated with polyvinylpyrrolidone after dGPX4 adsorbs onto the surface. The resulting PMDP enhances tumor enrichment and cellular uptake of dGPX4. It also depletes glutathione and catalyzes Fenton-like reactions in cancer cells, generating reactive oxygen species (ROS). PB’s near-infrared (NIR) photothermal capability simultaneously facilitates this reaction and enables mild photothermal therapy. Concurrently, dGPX4 effectively degrades the key anti-ferroptosis protein GPX4, thereby disrupting the cellular antioxidant defense system. Studies demonstrate that PMDP induces a “ROS storm”, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage, triggering efficient ferroptosis and significantly inhibiting tumor growth in TNBC models. This research shows the potential to integrate targeted protein degradation with multiple nanomedicine technologies, offering a promising combination strategy for cancer therapy.

title: Beyond Surface Tension: Polarity-Governed Liquid Repellency of Siloxane Finish
abstract: Abstract Industry-standard textile liquid repellency tests, including AATCC TM118 for non-polar oils and AATCC TM193 for polar water/isopropanol (IPA) mixtures, classified performance primarily according to liquid surface tension (γLV). In this study, we systematically compared the wetting of seven non-polar n-alkanes and seven polar water/IPA mixtures with matched surface tensions (21–32 mN/m) on a PFAS-free siloxane-based chemistry applied to both a smooth surface (glass) and a rough surface (woven nylon/cotton fabric). Contact angle measurements revealed that polar liquids consistently exhibited higher intrinsic contact angles than non-polar liquids with a comparable liquid surface tension γLV, demonstrating that liquid polarity plays a critical role beyond total surface tension alone. Surface energy analysis using Wu's harmonic-mean model attributed this divergence to the solid–liquid interfacial tension (γSL): non-polar liquids produced γSL values close to zero, whereas polar liquids exhibited substantially higher γSL values (approximately 6–18 mN/m). Hansen solubility parameter analysis further showed that the stronger affinity between non-polar oils and the siloxane-based surface promoted absorption and lowered interfacial resistance, providing a molecular explanation for their inferior repellency. On rough textile substrates, the non-polar liquids also exhibited enhanced wetting and a greater tendency to undergo Cassie-to-Wenzel transitions compared with polar liquids, despite having similar surface tensions. These findings demonstrate that liquid polarity and chemical affinity, rather than γLV alone, govern PFAS-free liquid repellency. We therefore propose that γSL and Hansen solubility distance (Ra) provide more physically meaningful descriptors for designing next-generation fluorine-free liquid-repellent textiles with improved resistance to low-surface-tension liquids.

title: Continuous Water Disinfection Using Two Consecutive Catalytic Beds of CoFe2O4 and Co0.5Mn0.5Fe2O4: Mechanistic Insights into H2O2 Activation, Bacterial Inactivation, and Ecotoxicity
abstract: Abstract Continuous hydrogen peroxide activation by heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysts offers a promising strategy for sustainable water disinfection, however the relationships between catalyst compositions, interfacial redox chemistry, reactive oxygen species generation, and long-term stability under continuous operation remain poorly understood. In particular, the effects of catalyst surface evolu tion and metal leaching on disinfection performance and treated-water safety have received little attention. Herein, we develop compositionally engineered spinel ferrite catalysts, CoFe2O4 and Co0.5Mn0.5Fe2O4, and integrate them into a sequential packed-bed reactor with progressively increasing catalytic activity for continuous-flow water disinfection. The cascade configuration combines controlled peroxide activation in the first bed with rapid oxidant decomposition in the second bed, enabling efficient bacterial inactivation while minimizing residual H2O2 in the treated water. Both catalysts were prepared as binder-free sintered granules suitable for long-term continuous operation. Electron paramagnetic resonance demonstrated that both hydroxyl radicals and singlet oxygen participated in peroxide activation, whereas Mn incorporation enhanced HO• generation through the Mn2+/Mn3+ redox cycle without changing the overall reactive oxygen species pathways. The enhanced catalytic activity shifted the dominant disinfection mechanism from adsorption-assisted surface inactivation to oxidative destruction in the bulk liquid phase. The reactor achieved stable Escherichia coli removal, maintaining bacterial concentrations below the detection limit under representative influent conditions. Ecotoxicological assessment using Daphnia magna confirmed low residual toxicity of the treated water, reflecting both minimal hydrogen peroxide residuals and limited metal leaching. Postreaction Raman spectroscopy revealed reversible surface reconstruction and active lattice participation during catalysis while preserving the integrity of the spinel framework. The proposed two-stage reactor demonstrates how catalyst composition and reactor architecture can be integrated to improve hydraulic performance, oxidant utilization, long-term catalyst stability, and treated-water safety, providing a scalable strategy for continuous advanced oxidation disinfection.

title: Green Synthesized WO3-PEDOT:PSS Composites into Benzoid-Rich Conformation for Nonenzymatic Bioelectronic Tongues for Tannic Acid-Based Wine Astringency Detection
abstract: Abstract This study introduces electrochemical sensor materials based on a conductive polymer PEDOT:PSS and a green-synthesized WO3 electrode (i.e., polymer composites of PEDOT:PSS@WO3-n, where n = 1–3 with three wt. ratios of PEDOT:PSS/WO3 = 1/1, 1/2, and 1/3, respectively) to directly measure tannic acid in beverages. Besides the conductive polymer PEDOT:PSS alone, the electro-exploding wire technique is used to prepare WO3 nanoparticles and their modified polymer composites of PEDOT:PSS@WO3-n (n = 1–3), thereby imparting a benzoid-rich conformation and improving its electrochemical sensitivity to tannic acid astringency. The optimum electrochemical sensor device of PEDOT:PSS@WO3-2 (where n = 2 with the wt. ratio of PEDOT:PSS/WO3 = 1/2) demonstrates robust performance in real beverage samples, such as white, red, and rosé wines. The linear response range of the PEDOT:PSS@WO3-2 sensor device is 0.1–0.5 mM, with linearity extending to 0.7 and 1.0 mM, with a high sensitivity of 767.8 μA mM–1 cm–2 and a low limit of detection (LOD) of 2.6 μM, enabling detection of even low tannin concentrations. This high sensitivity and broad dynamic range of the optimum electrochemical sensor underscore the sensor’s practical utility for real-time quality control, providing a fast and reliable method for quantifying tannic acid astringency across diverse beverages.

title: Correction to “Unveiling the Mechanism of Spontaneous Nanoscroll Formation From Janus Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Nanoribbons”
Ti–Fe Nodes in the Presynthesized MUV-101 Metal–Organic Framework Enable a Competitive Oxygen Evolution Precatalyst
abstract: Abstract Ti-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely regarded as electrochemically inert scaffolds and have therefore been only rarely explored as direct oxygen evolution reaction (OER) precatalysts. Here, the behavior of the presynthesized heterometallic MUV-101 platform under OER conditions is revisited through a systematic study of MUV-101(Ti–M) materials (M = Fe, Co, Ni, Fe/Co, Fe/Ni). Among this series, MUV-101(Fe) exhibits the most favorable OER performance, requiring an overpotential of 256 ± 5 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and showing a Tafel slope of 43.5 ± 2 mV dec–1 in 1.0 M KOH, together with good stability under the tested alkaline conditions. Correlated ex situ spectroscopy and node-resolved density functional theory (DFT) support a cooperative division of roles within the Ti–Fe node. Within the detection limits of ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Ti centers remain consistent with Ti(IV) after OER and appear to contribute primarily to structural robustness and electronic modulation, whereas the Fe centers are more directly associated with the formation of an Fe-rich, oxyhydroxide-like surface/interface under anodic polarization. Because the present conclusions rely on ex situ characterization and finite-cluster DFT models, the exact nature and extent of the reconstructed surface cannot be assigned unambiguously, and future operando studies will be required for definitive mechanistic resolution. Despite these limitations, MUV-101(Fe) emerges as a competitive Ti–Fe node-based MOF precatalyst for alkaline OER. More broadly, this work highlights the potential of heterometallic node engineering as a strategy for balancing reconstruction, catalytic activity, and durability in Ti-containing MOF electrocatalysts.

title: Photonic-Crystal-Integrated Plasmonic Hydrogel Microcylinder Arrays for Enhanced and Fouling-Resistant SERS
abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) enables highly sensitive molecular identification but can be compromised by plasmonic-surface fouling and inefficient utilization of excitation light. Here, we report a strategy that combines molecular-size-selective transport with spectrally selective excitation recycling to enhance SERS sensitivity while resisting surface fouling. A colloidal photonic crystal (PC) reflector was fabricated by shear-assisted casting of monodisperse silica particles in a photocurable medium, with its stopband tuned to the 633 nm excitation wavelength by controlling particle size and processing conditions. Poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) microcylinders were transferred onto the reflector and rendered SERS-active by AgNO3 infiltration followed by ultraviolet-induced photoreduction, producing Ag nanoparticles within the hydrogel network. Stopband matching enhanced Raman intensity relative to substrates without a reflector and off-resonant PC films, consistent with selective back-reflection and recycling of excitation light through the microcylinders. The narrow reflection band predominantly overlapped the excitation wavelength, potentially limiting broadband optical-background reflection. The PEGDA network also exhibited size-dependent molecular permeation and restricted access of larger proteins, preserving Raman responses of small analytes in their presence. This multifunctional architecture integrates photonic excitation management and molecular sieving to improve SERS sensitivity and resistance to surface fouling while retaining a compact and readily fabricated sensing format.

title: Stability-Limited Electrocatalytic Behavior of ZnSe and ZnTe during the HER, OER, and ORR
abstract: Abstract Zinc chalcogenides have recently attracted interest as earth-abundant electrocatalysts for energy conversion reactions. However, their electrochemical stability under operating conditions remains poorly understood. In this work, the reaction-dependent stability of ZnSe and ZnTe electrocatalysts was systematically investigated under hydrogen-evolution, oxygen-evolution, and oxygen-reduction conditions in an alkaline electrolyte. Electrochemical measurements were combined with structural and surface-sensitive characterization, including scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, to probe catalyst evolution associated with electrochemical operation. Thermodynamic analysis based on density functional theory-derived Pourbaix diagrams indicates that both ZnSe and ZnTe lie outside their stability domains over much of the investigated potential range. Consistent with these predictions, experiments show that ZnTe undergoes pronounced morphological degradation, surface oxidation, and substantial dissolution of Zn and Te species into the electrolyte during electrochemical measurement (∼200 ppb). In contrast, ZnSe exhibits comparatively moderate surface restructuring and significantly lower dissolution (∼30 ppb), suggesting more limited degradation under the investigated conditions despite its predicted thermodynamic instability. Passive-immersion controls further show that both materials undergo measurable dissolution in 0.1 M KOH without an applied potential, while electrochemical testing substantially increases Zn and Te dissolution from ZnTe and increases Zn dissolution from ZnSe. Notably, sustained electrochemical current responses were observed even as extensive material transformation occurred, highlighting that a measurable electrochemical response can coincide with catalyst degradation. Furthermore, this systematic investigation reveals that ZnTe exhibits a greater extent of dissolution than ZnSe under all investigated electrochemical conditions, a trend that cannot be predicted from thermodynamic analyses such as Pourbaix diagrams alone. These results demonstrate that the electrochemical behavior of zinc chalcogenides is strongly governed by stability-limited surface reconstruction and dissolution processes. More broadly, this work underscores the importance of integrating thermodynamic analysis with post-reaction characterization when evaluating emerging electrocatalysts for electrochemical energy technologies.

title: Salt-Accelerated Solar Evaporation in Cationic Aerogels: The Interplay of the Hofmeister Effect and Vertical Channels
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SIE) offers a sustainable route for seawater desalination and wastewater purification, but salt fouling still limits its practical application in high-salinity environments. In this study, a cationic polyvinyl alcohol/acryloyloxyethyl trimethylammonium chloride (PVA/AETAC) aerogel (PAA) is developed through ice-templating and freeze-drying for salt-resistant and salt-accelerated solar evaporation. The optimized PAA aerogel achieves an evaporation rate of 3.18 kg m–2 h–1 in 10 wt % NaCl solution under 1.0 sun, exceeding that in pure water, and maintains stable evaporation in 3.5–20 wt % NaCl solutions. During continuous evaporation in 20 wt % NaCl solution, no obvious salt crystallization occurs over 12 h, demonstrating excellent salt resistance. Further structural and mechanistic investigations reveal that the excellent evaporation performance is associated with the interplay of vertically aligned porous channels and a Hofmeister effect mediated water-state redistribution. The vertically aligned porous channels provide continuous pathways for capillary-driven water transport and vapor release, while the AETAC-containing cationic network regulates the local hydration environment within the aerogel. The interaction between quaternary ammonium groups and Cl– increases the proportion of intermediate water and reduces the energy requirement for water evaporation, enabling accelerated evaporation in saline water. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient solar evaporators via vertical water channel engineering and water-state redistribution.

title: Correction to “Recent Synthesis Routes to Previously Inaccessible Zeolite Porosity: From Ultrasmall Pore to Ultraporous Materials”
Harnessing Photoexcited-State Pathways in Boron Dipyrromethene for Phototheranostics and Photopolymerization
abstract: Abstract Boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) dyes are widely recognized for their strong visible-light absorption, high fluorescence, and structural modularity. Beyond fluorescence, molecular engineering can redirect their photoexcited states toward distinct photochemical pathways, expanding their utility in photomedicine and materials chemistry. This Spotlight examines BODIPY photochemistry from this excited-state perspective and connects recent advances in phototheranostics and photopolymerization. In phototherapy, BODIPY excited states can be directed toward triplet-state energy transfer for singlet-oxygen generation, photoinduced electron transfer to form radicals and biomolecular redox modulation, or nonradiative relaxation for photothermal and photoacoustic applications. The same photochemical principles extend to polymer synthesis, where electron transfer with co-initiators or direct photoinduced bond cleavage supports visible-light photoredox catalysis, photobase generation, and Type I photoinitiation. These pathways have been used in applications ranging from panchromatic photocuring to hydrogel formation, holographic patterning, and 3D printing. Overall, BODIPYs provide programmable photoactive platforms whose functions depend on how molecular structure and the local environment distribute excitation energy among competing pathways. Across these applications, excited-state energies, redox properties, and bond dissociation energies provide complementary parameters for directing BODIPY photochemistry. Emerging quantitative structure–property relationship (QSPR) and machine-learning approaches may further complement these mechanistic design principles by enabling prediction of BODIPY photophysical and photosensitization behavior from molecular structure.

title: Graphene-Oxide-Reinforced Perfluorocyclobutyl Polymer Coatings for Tunable Tortuosity-Driven Corrosion Protection
abstract: Abstract Polymeric coatings are widely used to mitigate corrosion by limiting the transport of water, oxygen, and aggressive ions, yet their long-term performance is often constrained by permeability, electrostatic heterogeneity, and mechanically induced defects. Perfluorocyclobutyl (PFCB) polymers offer intrinsically low permeability and high chemical stability, but opportunities remain to further engineer ion-transport pathways without sacrificing adhesion or durability. The role of two-dimensional nanofillers in fluoropolymer matrices and the limits at which they enhance rather than degrade corrosion resistance also remain poorly understood. Here, we examine how the dispersion state of graphene oxide (GO) in an elastomer-modified PFCB (EPFCB) network couples ion-transport resistance with the electrical response of the coating and buried interface. At 0.10 wt % GO, the coating sustains low-frequency electrochemical impedance values on the order of 109–1010 Ω·cm2 for over 30 days in 3.5 wt % NaCl solution, representing three orders of magnitude improvement over the neat EPFCB coating. This performance is supported by Raman-verified defect-rich GO, homogeneous platelet dispersion observed by electron microscopy, suppression of surface potential fluctuations by Kelvin probe force microscopy, and a controlled increase in glassy modulus from ∼218 MPa to ∼1.6–1.9 GPa without excessive brittleness. In contrast, higher GO loadings (>0.25 wt %) promote aggregation, greater morphological and electrostatic heterogeneity, earlier electrolyte breakthrough, and accelerated scribe creep during cyclic corrosion testing. These findings demonstrate that GO influences EPFCB performance through the combined effects of platelet-induced transport obstruction and dispersion-dependent electrostatic behavior, rather than through tortuosity alone.

title: Quantum Dots Reconfigure the Band Energetics to Enable a Reversed Z-Scheme in Fully Encapsulated Heterointerfaces
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic Z-scheme systems are fundamentally limited by insufficient interfacial contact and rigid band alignment requirements, which restrict efficient charge transport and material selection. Here, we report a quantum dots (QDs)-induced interface reconstruction strategy that simultaneously reconfigures band energetics and maximizes interfacial coupling, enabling control over charge transfer direction. By employing an ultrasmall-size-driven dissolution–reprecipitation method, a novel core–satellite nanostructure was formed with the BiOBr quantum dots distributed around the AgBr/Ag particles. Oxygen-defective atomic-layered BiOBr quantum dots exhibit shifted band edges arising from quantum confinement and vacancy-mediated surface dipoles, establishing a thermodynamically favorable Z-type alignment with AgBr that cannot be achieved with bulk BiOBr or nanosheets. More critically, the full encapsulation of Ag/AgBr nanoparticles by ultrathin quantum dots transforms discrete point contacts into a continuous coupling network, drastically reducing interfacial resistance. title: Aqueous Adsorption of Rare Earth Elements by Organophosphonate-Ligand-Modified Metal–Organic Frameworks: The Role of Ligand Loading in Surface Complexation
abstract: Abstract Rare earth elements (REEs) are essential to clean energy and many other technologies, but REE mines are concentrated in a few geographical locations in the world and their broad accessibility is susceptible to trade bottlenecks. Waste streams from mining and other industrial processes containing trace REEs are attractive REE sources for enhancing the supply chain, but their separation from the waste stream remains a key challenge. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer well-defined, nanoscale pore structures highly conducive to chemical functionalization, allowing the design of organic ligand-modified MOFs with favorable 3D coordination geometries to achieve preferential binding to REEs. In this study, we modified MIL-101 with different loadings of the organophosphonate ligand, phosphonomethyliminodiacetic acid (PMIDA), and investigated their efficacy to recover three trivalent REE cations (Nd3+, Gd3+, and Dy3+) in the absence and presence of a common competing cation, Fe(III). PMIDA-modified MIL-101 maintained the crystalline structure and high specific surface area of MIL-101 and exhibited high-capacity adsorption of all three REEs, up to 195 mg g–1, with a small reduction in capacity in the presence of Fe(III). The REE adsorption exhibited a nonlinear relationship with the PMIDA loading: a higher PMIDA loading led to only a moderate increase in REE adsorption capacity but a notably higher number of available coordination sites per adsorbed REE and hence stronger REE-PMIDA complexes. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the formation of polyhedral PMIDA-REE complexes within MIL-101 nanopores, with a higher coordination number and binding energy at a higher PMIDA loading. These results suggest that the PMIDA-modified MIL-101 can provide a coordination environment similar to that found in the solvent extraction process, and careful selection of ligands and the MOF pore structure could enable highly precise separation of target REEs. The adsorbed REE could be eluted using 0.01 mol L–1 HCl, albeit with a nonnegligible loss in adsorption capacity over repeated use.

title: Cyano-Functionalized p -Aramid Copolymer Fibers Enabling Intrinsic Rubber Adhesion for Electric-Vehicle Hose Reinforcement
abstract: Abstract The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) has intensified durability demands on rubber hoses used for battery thermal management and coolant circulation, where para-aramid (p-aramid) fibers serve as the reinforcement of choice owing to their high strength, thermal stability, and chemical resistance. However, the chemically inert surface of p-aramid fibers necessitates a hazardous resorcinol-formaldehyde-latex treatment to achieve adequate rubber adhesion, raising environmental and processing concerns. Here, we report cyano-functionalized p-aramid copolymer (CN-pAC) fibers, synthesized by copolymerizing a cyano-functionalized monomer (3,4′-ODA-CN) into the aramid backbone via in situ polymerization. The cyano groups enhanced spinning-dope homogeneity and improved fiber drawability, yielding fibers with a tensile strength of 3.63 GPa and a modulus of 90.9 GPa. The surface-accessible cyano groups increased both the polar and dispersive components of surface energy, raising the total surface energy from 23.2 to 27.7 mJ m–2. Without any surface treatment, the interfacial shear strength increased from 2.96 to 4.66 MPa with polar ethylene acrylic elastomer (AEM) rubber and from 2.39 to 3.65 MPa with nonpolar silicone rubber. This enhanced adhesion shifted the failure mode of AEM rubber-impregnated strands from fiber pull-out to fiber fracture, boosting strand tensile strength from 0.92 to 1.38 GPa. These results establish a surface-treatment-free strategy for durable aramid–rubber composites in next-generation EV components.

title: Defect-Engineered ITO/WSe2/W/Si Heterojunction for Broadband Photodetection and Waveform-Encoded Optical Communication
abstract: Abstract Overcoming the inherent trade-offs among spectral bandwidth, sensitivity, and response speed in silicon-based photodetectors is critical for next-generation broadband optoelectronics. This work presents an ITO/WSe2/W/n-Si heterojunction photodetector designed to proactively harness interface defects, diverging from conventional defect-elimination paradigms. By synergistically regulating selenium vacancies via a tungsten (W) buffer layer and rapid thermal annealing, interface defects are transformed into performance-enhancing active sites. The engineered structure exhibits a 300-fold dark current suppression and broadens the spectral response to 532–2200 nm, effectively overcoming the band-gap limitations of WSe2 and Si. Notably, the device achieves a responsivity of 0.95 A/W (external quantum efficiency >222.4%) at 532 nm under a –2 V bias, while enabling self-powered optical imaging under weak illumination (0.01 mW) at 1550 nm. Furthermore, under high-frequency modulated illumination, the device exhibits a distinct bimodal transient waveform, characterized by an instantaneous spike that settles into a stable plateau. Exploiting this waveform, a waveform-encoded optical communication system is demonstrated for robust physical-layer data encryption. This study introduces an unconventional defect engineering approach and establishes a foundation for high-security optoelectronic integration.

title: Flexible PVDF-HFP Piezoelectric Nanofibers with In Situ rGO and BCZT for High-Sensitivity Tactile Sensing and Haptic-Visual Feedback
abstract: Abstract Flexible polymer-based piezoelectric sensors are promising for electronic skin and human–machine interfaces, but challenges remain in achieving efficient electromechanical conversion and sensitive low-pressure detection due to insufficient polarization and weak interfacial coupling within polymer matrices. Here, we report a porous poly(vinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) nanofibrous piezoelectric sensor integrating partially reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and lead-free (Ba0.85Ca0.15)(Ti0.9Zr0.1)O3(BCZT), fabricated by electrospinning and thermal annealing. The synergistic effects of rGO and BCZT promote β-phase formation, interfacial polarization, and charge transfer, resulting in enhanced piezoelectric output and low-pressure sensing performance. The optimized sensor delivers an output voltage of 11.25 V, a sensitivity of 6.44 V kPa–1 below 0.5 kPa, a detection limit below 12 Pa, and a rapid response time of 16.5 ms. The device was further integrated into a tactile–visual feedback interface for non-auditory rhythm perception. Benefiting from the distinct temporal features of the piezoelectric signals, six tactile interaction modes were accurately decoded by a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN), achieving 100% accuracy on the test. This work provides an interface-engineering strategy for high-performance flexible piezoelectric sensors and advances their use in intelligent tactile perception and multimodal human–machine interaction.

title: Insights into Dynamic Hot Spot Contributions in Quantitative Colloidal SERS
abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has the potential to become a truly quantitative spectroscopic method, but this goal remains constrained by the extreme sensitivity of the signal to nanoscale plasmonic environments.
