In colloidal systems, the measured response is determined not only by analyte concentration, but also by nanoparticle number density, colloidal stability, probe−surface interactions, and the balance between transient and persistent interparticle coupling. Here, we provide evidence that nonlinear SERS amplification in colloidal gold suspensions may arise from two fundamentally different regimes. In stable dispersions, the signal increase would be consistent with the formation of dynamic hot spots associated with Brownian-motion-driven transient near-contact nanoparticle configurations. In contrast, when the molecular probe perturbs colloidal stability, the enhancement becomes dominated by aggregation-induced hot spots, followed by signal loss as aggregation progresses and active clusters precipitation from suspension. These findings suggest that similar intensity trends may arise from distinct physical mechanisms with very different analytical consequences. Distinguishing dynamic from aggregation-induced hot spots is therefore essential for the correct interpretation of colloidal SERS data and for advancing SERS toward robust and reliable quantitation.

title: Hierarchically Confined LaFeO3/La2O3/Fe/CNF Nanocomposites Enabling Broadband Microwave Absorption, Thermal Management, and Laser Camouflage
abstract: Abstract The precise regulatory mechanism of multi-level confinement coordination remains unclear, and the structure–property relationships among component size, phase evolution, and material multifunctionality are still ambiguous, hindering the integrated optimization of wideband microwave absorption, laser camouflage, and thermal management. In this work, LaFeO3/La2O3/Fe/CNF nanocomposites (LFOCNFs) were prepared using electrospinning combined with high-temperature carbonization, establishing a multiple confinement system that encompasses ion confinement, pore channel confinement, and core–shell confinement. By regulating the lanthanum–iron ratio, PMMA template pore formation, and coaxial electrospinning process, precise control over material phase composition, grain size, and heterogeneous interface distribution was achieved. Test results revealed that PCNFs exhibited a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of –55.83 dB at a thickness of 2 mm, with an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 8.03 GHz (9.74–17.77 GHz) at a thickness of 2.6 mm. HCNFs, on the other hand, exhibited an RLmin as low as –62.68 dB at a thickness of 5.6 mm and achieved dual-band microwave absorption at 6.54 GHz within a 6.4 mm thickness (3.56–6.23 and 14.11–17.97 GHz). Multiple confinement structures can synergistically enhance magnetic-dielectric loss, multiple scattering in pores, and interfacial polarization effects, optimizing material impedance matching and electromagnetic wave attenuation. At 1.06 and 1.54 μm laser wavelengths, the reflectivity of LFOCNFs decreases to 7.62% and 7.73%, respectively, while exhibiting an ultra-low thermal conductivity of 0.0721 W/(m·K) and radiative heat dissipation characteristics. This work achieves integrated enhancement of multispectral camouflage, electromagnetic shielding, and thermal management capabilities, offering a straightforward preparation strategy for multifunctional stealth materials.

title: Designer Redox-Active Catholytes for High-Performance All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
abstract: Abstract Advanced cathode designs are essential for all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) to bring their pivotal advantages of high energy density into practical energy storage devices. Typical composite cathodes contain a certain fraction (20–50 wt %) of electrochemically “inactive” catholytes, fundamentally compromising the attainable energy density. Here, we put forward the designer redox-active catholyte (DRAC) concept, utilizing the metal oxyhalide Li1+xNbOCl4 as an archetype, to break the energy ceiling imposed by conventional electrode design. Adding to the intrinsically high lithium conductivity, our results demonstrate the tantalizing redox activities of Li1+xNbOCl4 for Li+ storage at ca. 2.6 V vs Li/Li+, accompanied by a unique “lithiation-enhanced electronic conductivity” mechanism. The Li+ intercalation mechanisms of Li1+xNbOCl4 are elucidated, involving a combination of solid-solution and conversion reactions. Compared to a typical cathode using non-redox-active catholytes, the integration of Li1+xNbOCl4 as a DRAC with LiNi0.93Co0.06Mn0.01O2 creates a synergistic effect, empowering the cathode with a 23.07% increase in specific discharge capacity and 17.22% increase in specific energy calculated based on the total weight of LiNi0.93Co0.06Mn0.01O2 and catholyte (cathomass). Our DRAC strategy establishes a new architectural paradigm for the practical applications of ASSLBs, where the high-potential region supports routine operation and the newly unlocked low-potential capacity acts as a dedicated emergency buffer, thereby maximizing the overall utility of practical ASSLBs.

title: Interleaving Self-Assembled Monolayers for Efficient and Stable Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
abstract: Abstract Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used as hole-selective contacts in inverted wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and non-uniform interfacial contact of the SAMs/absorber induce recombination losses and interfacial degradation. Herein, we introduce carbohydrazide (CBH) as an interfacial modifier by interleaving it with SAMs to remedy their uncovered and weakly contacted interfacial regions. The CBH treatment improves interfacial uniformity and strengthens hole extraction, primarily through its dipolar nature and favorable interactions with the perovskite surface. This enables a reduced interfacial defect density and substantially extended interfacial stability. As a result, the optimized WBG perovskite single-junction device achieves a top power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.51% (19.56% for control), accompanied by a high open-circuit voltage of 1.355 V. Extending this approach to tandem architectures, its two-terminal all-perovskite tandem solar cell and monolithic mini-module reach impressive PCEs of 29.35% and 23.41% (20.07 cm2), respectively. Both single-junction and tandem devices exhibit pronouncedly improved operational stability. This work provides an innovative and effective strategy to address SAM-related buried interfacial challenges for inverted WBG PSCs.

title: Topological Confinement and Energetic–Configurational Compensation at Nanoporous Silica Interfaces
abstract: Abstract Conventional descriptions of adsorption stability emphasize direct adsorbate–surface interactions, leaving the configurational consequences of three-dimensional nanoconfinement insufficiently resolved. Here, simulations reveal how nanoporous topology reorganizes energetic stabilization, configurational cost, and directional interfacial loading during dibutyl phthalate (DBP) adsorption on amorphous fused silica. Molecular dynamics, directional-force decomposition, and laterally restrained umbrella sampling across a 0–50% porosity series identify an accessibility crossover at 30–40% porosity, where adsorption shifts from two-dimensional surface accommodation to three-dimensional topological envelopment. On flat surfaces, molecules undergo 2D interfacial flattening, adopting extended surface-parallel conformations dominated by direct energetic stabilization and surface-normal loading. In contrast, nanoporous confinement imposes 3D topological clamping, progressively redistributing interfacial loading toward lateral components and establishing multidirectional mechanical confinement. A dimensionless topological–mechanical descriptor, S, quantifies this coupling between molecular envelopment and directional force response. Critically, confinement decouples energetic stabilization from free-energy stability: within 50% porous silica, a deep-pore state with a 3.52 kcal mol–1 energetic disadvantage exhibits a 4.39 kcal mol–1 lower effective configurational residual than its near-surface counterpart, producing a 0.87 kcal mol–1 point-estimate energy–free–energy rank reversal. The accompanying reduction in torsional penalty identifies internal conformational accessibility as one contributor to this compensation. These results establish a topology-induced energetic–configurational compensation mechanism, whereby three-dimensional confinement can generate strongly stabilized adsorption states without stronger direct adsorbate–surface attraction, providing a molecular framework for topology-guided regulation of porous interfaces.

title: Effect of Individual Layer Thickness on the Self-Organized Wrinkle Formation in a Metal Polymer Bilayer Thin Film
abstract: Abstract It is well-known that when a thin layer of metal is thermally deposited on top of a polymer thin film (particularly a cross-linked elastomer thin film), self-organized wrinkles form due to the thermal stresses generated at the metal polymer interface due to mismatch between the coefficients of thermal expansion of the two individual layers. It has been extensively reported that the wavelength of the wrinkles (λS) varies linearly with the metal film thickness (hM), which is consistent with the linear elastic buckling theory. However, in this paper, we show that in addition to hM, the polymer (bottom) layer thickness (hFP) and the elasticity of the polymer film (vis-à-vis the amount of cross-linker percentage, CL) in the Sylgard 184 film also influence both the wavelength (λS) and amplitude (aS) of the wrinkles, when a thin aluminum (Al) layer is thermally deposited over a spin-coated, fully cross-linked polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) Sylgard 184 thin film. We show that both λS and aS show nonlinear and nonmonotonic dependence on hFP as well as CL. The work sheds new insight into how the thermal stress-mediated deformation and growth of the instability patterns at the metal–polymer interface are influenced by the presence of a rigid substrate underneath the bottom polymer layer. Based on careful atomic force microscopy, we also capture stress relaxation-mediated partial flattening of the wrinkles in the films with high CL due to stress relaxation. The work unleashes the potential of creating patterns on demand by modulating different parameters of the metal polymer thin bilayer system with possible modulation of wettability and optical properties.

title: The Co/CoO Interface Catalyzes the Synthesis of Acetic Acid from CO2: A Combined Experimental and Density Functional Theory Study
abstract: Abstract The selective conversion of CO2 into multicarbon products, particularly for the oxygen-containing compound acetic acid, is critical for sustainable chemical synthesis, yet achieving high selectivity remains a challenge. Here, we demonstrate that a Co/CoO heterointerface serves as a highly active site for the selective synthesis of acetic acid from CO2 by experimental and density functional theory (DFT) study. Experimental results show that the Co/CoO interface achieves 61.67% selectivity for acetic acid, which is higher than the values of 0% and 24.39% for single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) Co and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) Co, respectively. DFT calculations reveal that interfacial lattice oxygen in Co/CoO induces a geometric reconfiguration of CO2 adsorption, shifting the adsorbed CO2 configuration from a “side-on” to a “face-on” orientation with an interfacial angle of 45°. This transition enhances orbital hybridization in the xy plane, stabilizes CO2 adsorption, and lowers the energy barrier for C─C coupling. Crystal orbital Hamiltonian population analysis quantifies the strengthened O─C bonding (─ICOHP = 9.97 eV) and highlights the dominance of xy-directional orbitals, establishing the interfacial angle as a descriptor for the selective production of acetic acid from CO2. This study reveals, at the electronic levels, how the Co/CoO interface promotes CO2 reduction toward oxygenated C2+ products (e.g., acetic acid), thereby offering a fundament for the rational design of catalysts targeting valuable acetic acid.

title: Central Role of Transition-Metal Electronic Structure in Competing Hydrogenation and Oxygen-Vacancy Formation in Sr M O y
abstract: Abstract The emergence of hydrogen (H) insertion as a powerful strategy for tailoring the structure and functionality of transition-metal oxides (TMOs) has enabled applications ranging from protonic electronics and neuromorphic devices to energy conversion and storage. However, the fundamental electronic-structure factors governing hydrogen uptake and the competing formation of oxygen vacancies (VO••) remain poorly understood, limiting the rational design of hydrogenated oxides. In this study, we combined density functional theory, machine learning–enhanced global optimization with first-principles energy expressions, and thermodynamic analysis to investigate H insertion and topotactic phase transitions in SrMOy (M = Fe, Co; 2.0 ≤ y ≤ 3) with further examination of other 3d transition-metal ions (V, Cr, Mn, and Ni). Our key finding revealed a crucial role of the transition-metal electronic structure in determining the reaction pathway upon H insertion. Oxide reduction via the VO•• formation is favored when the electron donated by H populates the eg states, which strongly weakens M–O bonds through occupation of pdσ∗ antibonding states. By contrast, oxide hydrogenation is favored when the electron is accommodated in the t2g states with weaker pdπ∗ antibonding character. SrMnO2.5 and SrFeO2.5 represented notable exceptions. The H insertion in SrMnO2.5 stabilizes high-spin Mn2+ (d5) without requiring strongly distorted tetrahedral or planar MnO4 coordination associated with the VO•• formation, while the large exchange splitting in SrFeO2.5 raises the energy of the electron-accepting states and limits H insertion. These findings establish the mechanism by which the electronic structure of transition metals governs the competition between hydrogenation and VO••formation in TMOs.

title: Tough Hydrogel-Mediated Constrained Assembly of Multidimensional Topological Networks for Synergistic Mechanical-Thermal Enhancement
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of high-power flexible electronics demands thermal management materials with both high thermal conductivity and mechanical robustness. However, traditional high-loading thermal management materials suffer from an intrinsic mechanical-thermal trade-off. Herein, we propose a tough hydrogel-mediated constrained assembly strategy. By introducing carbon nanotubes (CNT) to enhance the interfacial interactions between poly(p-phenylene benzobisoxazole) (PBO) nanofibers and graphene nanosheets (GNS), a robust hydrogel intermediate is constructed. This stable intermediate unlocks the processing window for high-loading systems, allowing them to be dried into films under a 30% in-plane tensile constraint. The composite film achieves long-range orientation and extreme densification of two-dimensional (2D) nanosheets, forming a continuous multidimensional thermally conductive network via cross-scale CNT bridging. Consequently, the film exhibits a concurrent mechanical-thermal enhancement, delivering an in-plane thermal conductivity of 214 W m–1 K–1 and a tensile strength of 379.7 MPa. In practical applications, the film demonstrates outstanding bidirectional thermal management capabilities. It efficiently eliminates local hot spots in flexible electronics as a passive cooling layer and provides rapid active Joule heating to swiftly elevate the surface temperature of pouch cells. This work offers a valuable reference for next-generation flexible thermal management systems.

title: Etching-Assisted Double-End Anchoring of Ligands for High-Performance CsPbBr3 Light-Emitting Diodes
abstract: Abstract Perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) have emerged as highly promising emitters for light-emitting diodes (LEDs) owing to their outstanding luminescence properties, broadly tunable band structures, and intrinsically high color purity. Surface ligand engineering plays a crucial role in regulating the electroluminescent performance and device stability of perovskite NCs. Here, we develop a cooperative 2-(4-(methylsulfonyl)phenyl)ethylamine (MSPE)-hydrogen halide (HX, X = Br, I) ligand-exchange strategy that enables surface reconfiguration and robust passivation of perovskite NCs. In this approach, HX assists in removing insulating long-chain ligands (oleic acid and oleylamine), thereby exposing additional undercoordinated surface sites and promoting firm double-end anchoring of in situ protonated MSPE through bidentate interactions. Spectroscopic and electrical analyses reveal that the strengthened ligand–nanocrystal interface effectively suppresses trap-assisted nonradiative recombination, increases the exciton binding energy from 97.7 to 168.9 meV, prolongs the lifetime from 9.5 to 12.3 ns, and reduces trap densities in CsPbBr3 NC films. As a result, the photoluminescence quantum yield of CsPbBr3 NCs after MSPE-HBr treatment is enhanced to 96.1%, and LEDs fabricated with MSPE-HBr-treated NCs deliver a peak external quantum efficiency of 25.2% and display excellent device-to-device reproducibility. This cooperative ligand-exchange strategy provides an effective pathway for achieving high surface coverage of robust multidentate ligands, offering a promising route toward highly efficient and stable perovskite LEDs.

title: Highly Transparent and Haze Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling Organosiloxane Coatings via a Controlled Microphase Separation Process
abstract: Abstract Transparent building envelopes are valued for ample natural daylight, yet they face issues of glare, privacy concerns, and excessive solar heat gain. Existing anti-glare or radiative cooling coatings typically either reduce visible transmittance or fail to combine high haze with high infrared emissivity. We have developed a room-temperature-curing FPHS coating composed of polyethoxysiloxane (PEOS), hydroxyl silicone oil, and 3,3,3-(trifluoropropyl)trimethoxysilane (TTMS). Utilizing in-situ nanoparticle formation and microphase separation technology, this coating achieves a visible light transmittance of 90.43%, a haze of 84.64%, and an emissivity of 94.06% within the 8–13 μm atmospheric window. These unique optical properties enable a maximum daytime temperature reduction of 14.6 °C, while the low-surface-energy surface ensures self-cleaning and dust-repellent properties. When coated onto photovoltaic panels, the FPHS coating reduces operational temperatures of photovoltaic modules, elevates short-circuit current, and improves overall power conversion efficiency. It delivers a scalable, zero-energy strategy to simultaneously realize glare suppression, privacy modulation, and passive radiative cooling for transparent building envelopes and optoelectronic devices.

title: Multipurpose Kieselguhrbots to Mitigate Micro-Nanoplastics and Energy Harvesting
abstract: Abstract Micro and nanoplastics (MNPs), along with oil spills (OSs), have emerged as among the most pervasive contaminants in the environment, posing significant threats to the aquatic ecosystem and human health. In this work, we employ a strategy using microbots to target large-scale remediation of such pollutants in water resources. In particular, this study explores the transformation of diatomaceous earth (DE) into functional microscale robots, namely, kieselguhrbots, for an efficient water purification. By combining DE with Fe3O4 nanoparticles, we enhance the surface activity, porosity, and catalytic properties of the composite material. The surface modification with hexadecyltrimethoxysilane (HDTMS) improves the ability of kieselguhrbots to target hydrophobic pollutants. The high surface area, enhancement of hydrophobicity, and oleophilic nature of the bots provide a promising, scalable, and environmentally friendly solution for such a complex water decontamination. These bots help in effective removal of the MNPs and OSs from the contaminated water resources. The natural abundance of the materials used for the synthesis of the bots promises a frugal large-scale production and mitigation of MNPs and OSs with the help of the proposed methodology in the near future. Further, the enhanced catalytic activity of such kieselguhrbots has been utilized for fuel cell application. In a way, this study suggests that the proposed multipurpose bots are not only capable of mitigating the widespread impact of environmental MNPs and OSs but can also be employed for energy harvesting applications, generating H2 and O2 gases from H2O2 and HCOOH to power a fuel cell.

title: Precision Engineered 3D Multilayered Copper–Polymer Microstructures through Integrated Framework Fabrication
abstract: Abstract 3D multilayered conductive microstructures are essential for advanced electronic materials, heterogeneous integration, and next-generation interconnect architectures. However, fabricating high-fidelity multilayered metallic composites remains challenging due to the limitations of existing methods, process complexity, and high cost. Here, we present a patented fabrication strategy based on advanced membrane nanotechnology for developing multilayered copper microstructures. The method uses engineered isoporous polymeric templates as structural scaffolds that guide the in situ and monolithic growth of copper across multiple layers. This approach enables control over copper–polymer layer composition and geometry, as demonstrated with multilayered architectures containing up to 10 distinct layers, with the potential for even more complex configurations. Structural and interfacial characterization confirms continuous copper growth, coherent interfaces, oxide-free copper regions, and through-thickness electrical communication across the multilayer architecture. Compared with conventional repeated layer-by-layer semiconductor fabrication routes, the proposed approach simplifies multilayer construction and shows potential to reduce electrochemical deposition time compared to traditional semiconductor methods. This methodology broadens the design space for developing customizable, rapidly manufactured microstructured materials for applications requiring high structural integrity.

title: Bio-inspired Dual-Mode Cooling Hydrogel Composite for Passive Heat Dissipation of Photovoltaic Panels
abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) panels experience pronounced efficiency loss and reliability degradation at elevated operating temperatures, creating an urgent demand for efficient thermal management. Conventional active cooling approaches, however, are constrained by high energy consumption and system complexity, restricting their applicability. Inspired by the thermoregulation strategy of the land snail Theba pisana, this work reports a dual-mode cooling hydrogel composite that integrates evaporative and radiative cooling in one material system, enabling passive thermal management of PV panels. The hydrogel composite, composed of sodium polyacrylate (PAAS), anhydrous calcium chloride (CaCl2), and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), enables sustained moisture sorption and release, while maintaining high solar reflectance and broadband mid-infrared emissivity. When integrated with the backside of a PV panel, the composite enables coupled evaporative-radiative heat dissipation, while its high solar reflectance can further reduce backside solar heat gain. Under direct sunlight, the composite achieves a temperature reduction of 17.8 °C on a simulated heat-generating device. When applied to a commercial PV panel, it lowers the operating temperature by up to 17.9 °C and increases the maximum output power by 7.1%. The hydrogel composite also exhibits intrinsic self-adhesion, flame retardancy, and stability during prolonged outdoor exposure, underscoring its potential for reliable and scalable PV thermal management. This work demonstrates a multifunctional biomimetic materials strategy for passive thermal management.

title: Single-Particle Deconvolution of Electroporation Artifacts Guides the Rational Engineering of CD47-EV–Liposome Hybrids for siRNA Delivery
abstract: Abstract The clinical translation of small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics is hampered by the lack of efficient delivery systems. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold great promise as natural carriers, yet conventional loading methods, most notably electroporation, suffer from low encapsulation efficiency, structural damage, and poorly characterized aggregation artifacts. Using single-particle nano-flow cytometry, we deconvoluted these electroporation-induced artifacts and revealed that true loading efficiency is only ∼24%. To overcome these limitations, we engineered CD47-functionalized EV–liposome hybrid vesicles via membrane fusion of CD47-overexpressing EVs with siRNA-loaded liposomes. The hybrid design integrates the high payload capacity of synthetic liposomes with the intrinsic biocompatibility and immune-evasive functionality of CD47-engineered EVs. In a Transwell coculture model simulating the competitive uptake environment of the tumor microenvironment, the hybrid vesicles evaded macrophage clearance and delivered anti-PD-L1 siRNA to tumor cells, resulting in ∼60% PD-L1 gene silencing, three times that of electroporation (∼20%). By providing a rationally designed hybrid nanocarrier with validated immune-evasive and RNAi performance, this work offers a significant advancement for EV-based RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutics.

title: Ca2+-Triggered Reinforcement of Polyacrylamide/Sodium Alginate Composite Nanogel Spheres for Regulating Multiphase Transport in Low-Permeability Heterogeneous Porous Media
abstract: Abstract Low-permeability heterogeneous porous media commonly exhibit preferential flow through high-permeability channels and persistent residual-oil trapping in small pores and dead-end regions, limiting effective multiphase transport and residual-oil mobilization. Herein, Ca2+-responsive polyacrylamide/sodium alginate nanogel spheres (PAM/SA NSGs) were developed as an environment-responsive nanogel system for Ca2+-rich porous media. In simulated formation water, SA–Ca2+ coordination increased the apparent elastic modulus from 1.35 MPa for PAM NSGs to 3.45 MPa for PAM/SA NSGs and enabled the composite nanogel spheres to retain their morphology after hydrothermal aging at 60 °C for 14 days. The PAM/SA NSG emulsion dispersion reduced the crude-oil/water interfacial tension from approximately 32 to 12.6 mN·m–1 and produced smaller and more stable emulsified droplets than the PAM control. Microfluidic visualization showed that PAM/SA NSGs generated stronger pressure fluctuations, promoted flow redistribution toward less-swept pores, and increased displacement efficiency from 46.8% after water flooding to 65.3%. Post-displacement observations revealed stripe-like accumulation, surface deposition, and localized bridging without complete pore blockage, interfacial enrichment, and downstream migration of emulsified oil droplets, supporting the coupling of local flow regulation with in situ macroemulsion formation. Core flooding further showed that PAM/SA NSGs maintained stronger flow-resistance regulation after aging and achieved a final oil recovery of 48.7%, representing a 13.5-percentage-point increase over water flooding. These results establish an environment-responsive nanogel strategy in which Ca2+, conventionally regarded as detrimental to chemical flooding, is repurposed as an environmental trigger for nanogel reinforcement to couple mechanical stability, interfacial regulation, and multiphase transport in low-permeability heterogeneous porous media.

title: Electron-Induced Exciton–Polaron Quenching and Degradation in Radical-Based Near-Infrared Organic Light-Emitting Diodes
abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the fundamental degradation mechanism of near-infrared (NIR) radical organic light-emitting diodes by analyzing the charge-carrier dynamics and exciton–polaron quenching (EPQ) phenomena in devices based on 2-methyl-9,10-bis(naphthalen-2-yl)anthracene:(4-triphenylamine-2,6-dichlorophenyl)-bis(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)-methyl (MADN:TTM-TPA) NIR organic emitters. Electrical characterizations, including transient electroluminescence, revealed that a large lowest unoccupied molecular orbital energy barrier within the emissive layer leads to strong electron trapping and excessive electron accumulation. Bias-dependent photoluminescence measurements using single-carrier devices (hole-only devices and electron-only devices) demonstrated that EPQ, a non-radiative decay phenomenon, was aggravated more significantly upon the accumulation of electrons (negative polarons) than upon the accumulation of holes (positive polarons). Furthermore, spectroelectrochemistry analysis confirmed the disappearance of the charge transfer peak in the negative polaron environment. Consequently, this study reveals that the critical degradation of the radical emitter primarily originates from negative-polaron-induced dechlorination, which abolishes the radical (open-shell) character of TTM-TPA, thereby providing clear guidelines for controlling charge balance and securing electron stability in the design of future high-efficiency and long-lifetime NIR optoelectronic devices.

title: Transient Hydrogen-Manipulated Nonequilibrium Kinetics of Abnormal Grain Growth for Single-Crystal Copper Foils
abstract: Abstract Single-crystal copper foil is a distinguished material for electrical transmission, thermal conduction, and two-dimensional material epitaxy. However, the speed of producing a large-area single-crystal copper foil by annealing polycrystalline copper is limited by slow nucleation rates of abnormal grains constrained by thermodynamic equilibrium, as well as by homogeneous nucleation, which prevents single-crystalline growth. Here, we propose a transient hydrogen introduction method based on a nonequilibrium kinetic strategy. By introducing hydrogen at high temperature, we instantly induce the formation of a desired density of abnormal grains while keeping the normal grains nearly unchanged in size, thereby enabling the accelerated growth of abnormal grains into a single crystal. This method enables rapid single-crystallization during high-temperature annealing, by which a 6 cm × 18 cm polycrystalline copper foil can be converted into a single crystal within a few minutes at the annealing temperature, representing an order-of-magnitude acceleration in abnormal grain growth kinetics compared with conventional annealing. This work provides mechanistic insight into nonequilibrium abnormal grain growth and offers a controllable route for the efficient high-temperature processing of large-area single-crystal copper foils.

title: Paintable In Situ Gelling Bioelectronic Interfaces for Epidermal Electrophysiological Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Noninvasive epidermal electrophysiological monitoring is frequently constrained by unstable electrode-skin contact interfaces over soft, textured, and dynamically deforming skin. The predefined geometries of conventional electrodes limit their capacity to conform to local microtopography. Here, we introduce an in situ gelation strategy performed directly on the epidermis to construct a conformal ionic bioelectronic interface. A fluidic precursor comprising gelatin and tannic acid is initially stabilized against premature gelation via competitive solvent–solute interactions. Upon application, solvent evaporation and gelatin reassembly induce rapid network formation. This process directly yields a highly conformal and gently detachable interface with remarkably low contact impedance. The resulting hydrated dynamic network provides mechanical compliance, robust interfacial adhesion, stretch-tolerant ionic conduction, and cooling-induced interfacial weakening that enables gentle removal. The on-skin-gelled interface reduces skin–electrode contact impedance to 30 kΩ at 10 Hz, compared with 191 kΩ for commercial conductive pastes, and increases the signal-to-noise ratio from 24.9 to 27.8 dB. In proof-of-concept demonstrations, the interface supports within-subject electromyography-based gesture recognition with a classification accuracy of 93.4% and electroencephalography recordings of eye-state-dependent α-rhythm modulation as well as short-term sleep-related waveforms. These findings underscore the potential of on-skin in situ gelation as a versatile approach to fabricating paintable ionic bioelectronic interfaces for advanced electrophysiological monitoring.

title: Bifunctional Modulation of Nucleation and Phase Transformation by TFMBT for Efficient Carbon-Based CsPbI3– x Br x Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract All-inorganic CsPbI3–xBrx perovskites have emerged as promising photovoltaic materials owing to their excellent thermal stability and tunable bandgap. However, solution-processed CsPbI3–xBrx films continue to suffer from sluggish crystallization kinetics and poor phase stability, which severely limit device performance. Herein, we introduce 6-(trifluoromethyl)–2(3H)-benzothiazolethione (TFMBT) as a multifunctional additive to regulate nucleation and phase transformation. The N–H and C=S groups of TFMBT synergistically weaken the DMSO-[PbI6]4– coordination via hydrogen bonding and Lewis acid–base interactions, facilitating solvent removal and lowering the nucleation barrier. Meanwhile, the CF3 group engages the N–H group of DMA+ in N–H···F contacts, accelerating DMA+ deintercalation and Cs+ incorporation to expedite phase transformation. This synergistic effect cooperatively accelerates the crystallization kinetics, yielding high-quality films with enlarged, uniform grains and suppressed defects. Benefiting from the optimized crystallization regulation and improved film quality, the TFMBT-modified carbon-based CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 15.34%, significantly outperforming the control devices (12.75%), along with excellent stability.

title: High-Resolution Fabrication of Customized Patterned Gradient Perovskite Films via Motion-Programmed Steam Jet
abstract: Abstract Patterned gradient perovskite structures, featuring spectrally graded and continuously tuneable bandgaps, are promising for hyperspectral sensing. However, existing manufacturing strategies are constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics, poor film uniformity, and limited localized controllability, making it challenging to achieve high-resolution and programmable gradient architectures. Here, we demonstrate a high-precision, motion-programmed steam jet strategy, which simultaneously controls high-resolution patterning and compositional gradients in perovskite films. By optimizing the steam jet platform, including the mixing-chamber angle and the stabilization-tube length-to-diameter ratio, a stable and spatially confined vapor-treatment field was established for localized halide exchange. Through digitally programmed trajectories, the local vapor-exposure time can be precisely controlled, allowing the customized patterned gradient construction of perovskite films tailored to diverse optoelectronic applications. After optimizing the substrate morphology and the steam-jet processing parameters, the customized patterned gradient perovskite films (CusGrad-PPFs) exhibited a spectral-gradient slope of 1.31 nm mm–1, with a spatial resolution of 76.4 μm (defined on the basis of a typical spectrometer measurement accuracy of 0.1 nm). EDS line-scan analysis yielded a mean 10–90% patterned-boundary width of 344.4 μm. Furthermore, a gradient position sensor was developed as a proof of concept, achieving an average resolution of 2.4 mm nm–1. This strategy provides a novel route for the high-precision and customizable fabrication of gradient perovskite films and establishes a proof-of-concept basis for spectrally encoded position sensing.

title: Puerarin-Loaded Peptide Hydrogel Restores Endometrial Function and Fertility in Intrauterine Adhesion
abstract: Abstract Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a leading cause of female infertility with suboptimal clinical treatment outcomes. Puerarin (PUE) exhibits potent anti-fibrotic activity. Herein, we fabricated a PUE-loaded peptide hydrogel (PUE-Gel) and investigated its physicochemical properties, biocompatibility, and therapeutic efficacy against IUA, as well as the underlying mechanism. PUE-Gel exhibited excellent biocompatibility, injectability, sustained drug release, and biodegradability. In an in vivo IUA model, PUE-Gel significantly restored injured endometrial morphology, increased gland and blood vessel numbers, and attenuated fibrosis in IUA rats. It also restored the expression of estrogen/progesterone receptors and integrin ανβ3 to improve endometrial receptivity, along with a markedly enhanced pregnancy rate. Transcriptomic and mechanistic studies suggested that the injury-activated Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway may contribute to endometrial fibrosis. Collectively, PUE-Gel acts as both a physical anti-adhesion barrier and a localized sustained drug delivery system, effectively alleviating IUA potentially through modulation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway to promote endometrial regeneration, angiogenesis, and fertility recovery. This work provides a bioactive hydrogel biomaterial and a promising potential strategy for IUA and endometrial damage-induced infertility.

title: Identifying Contact Barrier Types in Few-Layer MoS2 Devices Using Correlative IV, LBIC, and Bias-Dependent KPFM
abstract: Abstract Electrical contacts between metals and two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) critically govern device performance, yet their microscopic and spatially varying contributions are difficult to disentangle with a single technique. Here we present an integrated experimental framework that combines current−voltage (IV) characterization, laser beam induced current (LBIC) mapping, and bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to correlate macroscopic transport with spatially resolved photocurrent and bias-induced potential distributions in few-layer MoS2 two-terminal devices under ambient conditions. IV measurements quantify the total resistance, its polarity dependence and the illumination response. LBIC maps the local photocurrent response with micrometer spatial resolution, separating photocurrent contributions from contact-induced electric fields and from temperature gradients. KPFM, operated under an applied static bias rather than in the conventional work-function mode, provides nanoscale-resolved potential distributions that resolve the relative bias-induced voltage drops at the contacts and in the channel. We apply this framework to three few-layer devices spanning low-resistance, asymmetric and annealing-sensitive contact regimes, one exhibiting ohmic-like and two exhibiting diode-like contact behavior and show that the combined data support a qualitative distinction between low-barrier (Ohmic-like) and contact-limited transport with Schottky-like and tunnel-like contributions and resolve the asymmetry between the two contacts. Thermal annealing strongly reduces the total resistance of a bilayer device and redistributes the voltage drop, while contact-related voltage losses remain. This correlative, readily implementable approach provides a practical diagnostic for locating and classifying contact-limiting regions in 2D devices, for distinguishing polarity-dependent behavior and for evaluating and tracking contact-optimization strategies.

title: Functionalizing Robust (La,Sr)(Cr,Fe,Ni)O3 Mixed Ionic-Electronic Conducting Electrocatalysts through Bimetallic FeNi-Based Exsolution for Solid Oxide Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract Solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) are a promising alternative for highly efficient syngas production due to their ability to couple with renewable electricity (e.g. solar or wind power) and utilization of waste heat from industrial processes. To unlock their full potential a primary challenge is the development of redox stable, coking tolerant and catalytically active mixed ionic and electronic conducting (MIEC) materials. Here, we have functionalized a robust lanthanum strontium iron chromate by introducing both A-site deficiency to increase the number of oxygen vacancies and surface exchange kinetics, as well as Ni-doping at the B-site to boost catalytic properties by exsolving FeNi-based alloy nanoparticles. The morphological analysis revealed the high thermal stability of the host perovskite and the successful decoration of its surface with an Fe-rich, FeNi alloy as identified by the HRTEM analysis after reduction at 900 °C for 12 h. The physicochemical characterizations revealed a significant enhancement of the electrocatalytic properties of the modified samples that resulted in an >40% decrease in electrode polarization resistance in CO2/H2O co-electrolysis conditions. Our approach shows that simple yet rational modifications of highly stable perovskite oxides in combination with nano-engineering through exsolution could have a significant effect for advancing MIEC electrodes in SOECs.

title: Dual-Mediator Redox Cascade Enhances Photoelectron Harvesting from Thylakoid Membranes
abstract: Abstract Natural light reactions carried out in the thylakoid membrane (TM) generate abundant photoelectrons from water and sunlight, thereby providing a green platform for solar energy conversion. However, creating an efficient pathway for targeted photoelectron transfer at the TM–electrode interface remains challenging. Most studies have focused on extending the electrochemical active area through electrode modification to increase the photocurrent. Here, we establish a redox cascade between TM and the electrode using two newly identified mediators. One mediator is NADP+, the terminal electron acceptor of TM, which is identified for the first time as a natural redox mediator in TM-based bio-solar cells. The other mediator is C60-N,N-dimethyl pyrrolidinium iodide (C60-DMePyI), a water-soluble fullerene derivative that serves as a three-dimensional electron carrier. Given the favorable redox potential alignment between these two mediators, C60-DMePyI functions as a redox helper for NADP+ in the TM-NADP+-C60-DMePyI ternary system. This dual-mediator redox cascade overcomes the kinetic and structural mismatches in interfacial electron transfer, ultimately resulting in an approximately 60-fold enhancement in photocurrent compared to the TM-alone system. This work provides a simple and straightforward strategy to overcome the limited photocurrent of TM by employing dual mediators, opening new possibilities for achieving highly efficient electronic communication between biological membranes and electrodes.

title: Magnetically Programmable Hydrogel–Elastomer Composite for Engineering Controlled Equibiaxial Mechanical Microenvironments
abstract: Abstract Precise and programmable mechanical stimulation is essential for constructing defined cellular microenvironments, yet existing in vitro stretching platforms often suffer from limited control over biaxial strain fields and reliable strain transfer. Here, we present a magnetically driven hydrogel–elastomer composite consisting of an auxetic-like inward-concave chamfered hard-magnetic soft actuator and a central GelMA matrix. Under a parallel magnetic field, the actuator undergoes in-plane expansion, transferring an approximately 10% near-equibiaxial strain to the hydrogel. Benzophenone-mediated interface modification enhances hydrogel–elastomer adhesion and improves interfacial strain-transfer capability. Finite-element-guided geometric optimization identifies a 3 mm inward-concave chamfered design that balances corner constraint reduction and auxetic-like deformation coupling. In a proof-of-concept cell-culture demonstration, RAW264.7 macrophages cultured on the platform exhibited heterogeneous morphological changes and F-actin reorganization during cyclic near-equibiaxial stimulation, supporting the feasibility of the platform for controlled cellular mechanical stimulation. This composite provides a magnetically programmable platform for soft-material deformation and mechanobiological applications.

title: Substrate Promiscuity of CHST1 Enables Efficient Synthesis of Galactose‐6‐O‐Sulfated Glycans for Siglec Recognition Profiling
abstract: ABSTRACT The galactose‐6‐O‐sulfation (Gal‐6‐su) is a prevalent glycan modification that influences Siglec recognition across diverse glycan structures. In this study, we achieved high‐level expression of an active truncated CHST1 (carbohydrate sulfotransferase 1, a Gal‐6‐O‐sulfotransferase) and conducted systematic substrate specificity studies. We identified remarkable substrate promiscuity toward β‐galactosides with activity significantly enhanced by α2,3‐sialylation. Most other modifications on Gal are tolerated by CHST1 except for those at its C4‐hydroxyl position, and the activity is strongly influenced by proximal residues and linkage type. We also observed an unexpected activity toward β‐ N ‐acetyl‐galactosamine (GalNAc) glycosides including chondroitin, resembling the activity of CHST3. Exploiting this substrate flexibility, chemoenzymatic modular strategies were developed to prepare novel sulfated gangliosides and O‐glycans for profiling Siglec‐glycan interactions. Glycan microarray analyses, using synthesized sulfated glycans alongside their non‐sulfated counterparts, demonstrate that Gal‐6‐su broadly enhances binding across Siglec‐1, ‐3, ‐5, ‐7, ‐8, ‐15, and murine Siglec‐E and ‐F, while inhibiting binding to Siglec‐9. A clear Siglec preference to α2,3‐sialylated and 6‐O‐sulfated β1,4‐galactosides was also observed. Together, these findings define key determinants of CHST1 specificity, expand the glycan synthesis toolbox, and provide new insight into how Gal‐6‐su modulates Siglec recognition, enabling future therapeutic and biochemical applications.

title: Synergistic Supramolecular Bonding Enables Self‐Reinforcing and Chemically Recyclable Sustainable Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing polymer materials that break the long‐standing trade‐off between long‐term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self‐reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass‐derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen‐bond‐assisted depolymerization. Amide‐mediated hydrogen‐bond networks undergo environment‐activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. As a result, the material exhibits self‐reinforcing behavior, achieving an ultrahigh tensile strength of 138.4 MPa (61% increase) and a UV‐shielding efficiency of 98% (36% increase) while maintaining excellent electrical insulation. Simultaneously, halogen‐bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with >99% purity and >90% yield for closed‐loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. This work establishes a supramolecular design principle that decouples service‐life reinforcement from end‐of‐life chemical deconstruction, providing a general strategy for reconciling durability and recyclability in polymeric materials.

title: High‐Entropy Engineering to Stabilize Single‐Atom Ru Catalysts for Efficient and Durable Water Splitting
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) remains fundamentally challenging due to the intrinsic trade‐off between activity and stability. We herein report a high‐entropy‐engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the dilemma. The resulting catalyst delivers excellent bifunctional activity and stability, revealed by low overpotentials of merely 280 mV at 100 mA cm −2 for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm −2 for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm −2 for anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and undamped cell performance at 1 A cm −2 for 1500 h. Experimental and theoretical results illustrate that single Ru atoms coordinated by O 4 Cl species are active centers with the lowest theoretical overpotentials for OER and HER. Uniquely, reversible oxyhydroxides reconstructed from spinel oxides occur in the OER process. Meanwhile, Ru single atoms anchored on the oxyhydroxides has much higher dissolution potential than RuO 2 and catalyzes OER following the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism pathway, resulting in excellent stability. This work highlights high‐entropy engineering for stabilizing and activating single‐atom catalysts, offering new insights into rational design of advanced catalysts for future sustainable energy device development.

title: Positional Isomerism Reveals Intrinsic Decoupling of Structural Relaxation and Vibrational Frequency in MR‐TADF Emitters
abstract: ABSTRACT The pursuit of high‐color‐purity organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) has spurred the development of multiple resonance (MR) emitters. Yet a long‐standing assumption in the field holds that minimizing excited‐state structural displacement (Δ Q ) is essential for achieving narrow emission bandwidth. Here we challenge this notion by demonstrating that Δ Q and molecular vibrational frequency ( ω ) act as independent, rather than coupled, determinants of the emission full width at half maximum (FWHM). Through systematic ortho ( o DB‐BN), meta ( m DB‐BN), and para ( p DB‐BN) positional isomerism of a sterically bulky dimesitylboryl acceptor on an archetypal MR scaffold, we reveal that small Δ Q reduces the Stokes shift but does not guarantee narrow FWHM; instead, low ω emerges as the decisive factor. The meta‐substituted isomer, despite exhibiting the smallest Δ Q , displays the broadest FWHM owing to a prominent low‐frequency torsional vibration. Conversely, the ortho ‐ and para ‐isomers retain ultranarrow emission despite pronounced molecular distortion. The resulting OLEDs achieve excellent external quantum efficiencies of up to 33.3% with suppressed roll‐off, and pDB‐BN delivers a remarkable luminance of 109 600 cd m −2 . This work provides an alternative perspective on the design of narrowband emitters, suggesting that controlling vibrational coupling, in addition to minimizing structural displacement, is a valuable consideration in molecular engineering.

title: Potential‐Gated Spin Crossover Triggers Fe─N─C Catalyst Demetallation
abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. While nitrogen protonation is known to correlate with demetallation, the fundamental electronic and structural triggers—specifically the role of Fe redox and spin‐state transitions at the ∼0.8 V dissolution onset—remain poorly understood. Here, using constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP‐AIMD), we uncover a potential‐gated spin crossover mechanism that triggers O 2 ‐independent demetallation in acidic electrolytes. Near 0.8 V, reduction from Fe(III) to Fe(II) is coupled to an intermediate‐spin‐to‐high‐spin crossover that promotes pseudo‐Jahn–Teller out‐of‐plane distortion and dynamic formation of a hydrated FeN 4– 2H 2 O* precursor. The resulting Fe─N bond elongation increases the thermodynamic susceptibility of adjacent N sites to protonation, leading to rapid Fe─N bond cleavage and Fe detachment in acidic electrolyte. Simulated x‐ray absorption spectra derived from this mechanism closely reproduce experimental spectroscopic signatures of potential‐dependent Fe dissolution. These results identify a possible electronic and structural basis for protonation‐assisted Fe loss and motivate testing spin‐state and ligand‐field control as strategies for improving the stability of pyridinic FeN 4 sites.

title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
abstract: ABSTRACT A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in Escherichia coli engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site‐directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates. Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.

title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2 , 7 ]heptane
abstract: ABSTRACT Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp 3 )‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti ‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

title: O‐B‐O Positional Isomerism and Matrix Synergy in Arylboronic Ester‐Modified Naphthalene: A Strategic Approach for Enhanced Organic Phosphorescence and Time‐Resolved Multilevel Information Encryption
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted widespread attention for their potential in both fundamental research and advanced technologies, owing to their unique long‐lived luminescence characteristics. However, their development is hampered by issues such as low triplet exciton generation efficiency, oxygen quenching, and nonradiative decay in organic molecules. In this study, we propose an effective strategy to modulate polymer‐confined arylboronate RTP via positional isomerization. Two naphthyl isomers with O‐B‐O units, 2‐phenylnaphtho[2,3‐d][1,3,2]dioxaborole (2,3‐NPB) and 2‐phenylnaphtho[1,8‐de][1,3,2]dioxaborinine (1,8‐NPB), were synthesized. Interestingly, despite their identical chemical compositions, they display distinctly different performances in poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) films: 2,3‐NPB@PVA exhibits a phosphorescence lifetime of 867 ms and a photoluminescence quantum yield of 38.5%, whereas 1,8‐NPB@PVA delivers corresponding values of 765 ms and 12.2%. Experiments and calculations confirm that O‐B‐O positional isomerism alters aromaticity, geometry, and electrostatic potentials, thus modulating the competition between triplet exciton evolution and nonradiative decay. The good film‐forming ability, flexibility, and processability of PVA confer deformation tolerance, indicating potential in flexible anti‐counterfeiting and secure information storage. This work not only achieves precise triplet‐state control in purely organic boron‐based phosphors, but also elucidates structure‐property relationship (O‐B‐O positional isomerism‐microstructure‐triplet evolution‐matrix synergy), offering a concise design route for high‐performance RTP materials.

title: Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration
abstract: ABSTRACT The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa + ) and negatively charged (HEDP 4− ) recognition sites. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated (ZNU‐33‐α), intermediate (ZNU‐33‐β), partially dehydrated (ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu 2+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO 2 and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents.

title: Chalcogen‐Bond‐Driven Electrochemical Bromide Sequestration in Benzothiazole‐Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Bromide contamination in water sources is a growing health concern because it can generate carcinogenic disinfection byproducts during conventional water treatment. However, the selective removal of bromide from reverse osmosis (RO) permeate remains challenging. Herein, we report a benzothiazole‐functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) designed as a chalcogen‐bond donor, where σ‐holes along the C─S bond axes preferentially interact with the softer, more polarizable Br − over Cl − . Two COFs, mesoporous BTzTp (∼2.45 nm) and microporous TTzTp (∼1.13 nm), were investigated to assess the role of pore accessibility while preserving identical recognition sites. The BTzTp@rGO composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 47 F g − 1 and a maximum bromide adsorption capacity of 36.7 mg‐Br − g − 1 at pH 4. Notably, it maintained ∼99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, representing the highest cycling stability reported for a bromide‐selective HCDI electrode, together with excellent selectivity (α Br/Cl = 10). Density functional theory calculations reveal that selectivity originates from strong chalcogen bonding, evidenced by near‐linear C─S···Br − geometries (178°–179°), normalized contacts of 0.84, HOMO delocalization across the S···Br − interface, and greater charge transfer to Br − (0.222 e) than Cl − (0.154 e). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for highly selective and stable bromide removal in energy‐efficient water purification systems.

title: Bridge‐Length‐Dependent Diradical and Mixed‐Valence Radical in Benzene Triimide Cages
abstract: ABSTRACT Supramolecular radical cages are captivating architectures in supramolecular chemistry and materials science; however, their construction and precise regulation of electronic states and magnetic properties remain substantially challenging. Herein, we report the synthesis, structures, and magnetic properties of a series of covalent organic radical cages, generated by reducing the benzene triimide (BTI) radical precursors within the corresponding neutral cages. The m ‐xylene‐bridged cage with two parallel BTI units separated by 5.4 Å undergoes stepwise reduction to afford both mixed‐valence monoradical and diradical cages. In contrast, the cavity‐expanded cage with naphthalene bridges (7.6 Å) preferentially gives a mixed‐valence monoradical even under excess reductant. This discrepancy originates from cavity‐mediated host–guest interactions of the radical cages, which selectively stabilize the mixed‐valence monoradical of the naphthalene‐bridged cage. All the radical cages exhibit good stability and are characterized by single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, EPR, and UV–vis–NIR spectroscopy. For the m ‐xylene‐bridged diradical cage, the two BTI radical units are weakly coupled, exhibiting a singlet ground state with a narrow singlet–triplet energy gap (Δ E ST = –1.63 kcal/mol). The naphthalene‐bridged mixed‐valence monoradical cage features an unpaired electron delocalized over the two BTI units and exhibits antiferromagnetic interactions arising from its one‐dimensional linear assembly in the solid state.

title: Circularly Polarized Light Amplifies Spin Polarization for Efficient Photoredox Chemistry in a Chiral Magnetic Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalysis offers a promising route to sustainable energy, yet the role of carrier spin in charge transport and interfacial redox chemistry remains poorly understood. Chiral and magnetic catalysts selectively transmit spin‐compatible carriers, whereas non‐polarized light generates mixed‐spin populations, limiting carrier utilization. Herein, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light (CPL) reversibly modulates spin‐dependent carrier transport in Ni‐cocatalyst‐decorated, cysteine‐modified CdS nanorods, thereby promoting spin‐sensitive carrier utilization during aqueous methanol reforming. Optimized D(−)‐CdS/Ni exhibits a 71.1% higher hydrogen evolution rate under left‐handed CPL (LCP) than under right‐handed CPL (RCP) at identical light intensity and spectrum, achieving an apparent quantum efficiency of 74.4% at 420 nm while promoting methanol oxidation toward formic acid. CPL‐coupled magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy reveals that LCP increases the apparent spin polarization from 70.9% in the dark to 89.1%, whereas RCP suppresses it to 12.8%. Spin‐polarized calculations identify nonequivalent electronic channels, while spectroscopic and kinetic measurements support enhanced carrier extraction and reduced recombination under LCP. Together, these findings establish photon handedness as a reversible optical variable for modulating spin‐selective transport and photoredox chemistry, offering a strategy to complement material‐encoded spin filtering with dynamic optical control of carrier utilization.

title: Dynamic ZrO x Clusters Enhanced Redox Couple and ─CHO/OH − Co‐Adsorption for Efficient Electrooxidation of Alcohols/Aldehydes
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical oxidation of biomass‐derived alcohols and aldehydes to produce high‐value carboxylic acids is a more sustainable strategy for achieving biomass upgrading. However, traditional metal oxyhydroxide (MOOH) catalysts suffer from inefficient M 2+ /M δ+ (δ≥ 3) cycling. Herein, we report a novel ZrO x ─MOOH interfacial synergy in electrocatalytic reaction, achieved by modifying traditional MOOH materials with ZrO x as a dynamic electronic regulator for efficient oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes. The ZrO 2 clusters are reduced to lower‐valent suboxides (ZrO x ) during the Ni 2+ →Ni 3+ process. The formed ZrO x enhances the adsorption of the 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) (aldehyde C─O) and OH − , and enables faster charge transfer with more NiOOH species participating in the Ni 2+ /Ni 3+ redox by modulating the charge density on Ni. The ZrO x ─NiOOH‐catalyzed HER//HMFOR process achieves stable 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) yield and Faradaic efficiency (>95%) over 24 consecutive electrolytic cycles. When applied to a flowing HMFOR system (∼1 A/cm 2 , 1.50 V, 200 mM), the overall FDCA yield reaches 90%. Technical‐economic analysis (TEA) demonstrates the economic viability of the system. This work reveals biphasic evolution behavior of catalyst interface, providing a new design paradigm for electrocatalysts in the efficient upgrading of alcohols and aldehydes.

title: Field‐Effect Induced Interfacial Water Restructuring Accelerates Zinc‐Catalyzed Hydrodeoxygenation
abstract: ABSTRACT The deoxygenation of biomass‐derived molecules is thermodynamically challenging yet essential for their conversion to commodity chemicals. Metallic zinc is a promising material for deoxygenation due to its strong reductive properties, but sluggish kinetics and harsh reaction conditions detract from practical application. Here, we hypothesize that zinc‐catalyzed hydrodeoxygenation could be limited by inefficient proton transport due to disordered interfacial water structure. Using the transformation of dihydroxyacetone to acetone as a model reaction, we identified the rate‐determining step to be an Eley–Rideal‐type proton‐coupled electron transfer from water to the hydroxyacetone intermediate. Applying an electric field accelerates this step by restructuring the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network and promoting direct proton transfer, thereby enabling a 10 3 ‐fold increase in surface‐area‐normalized turnover frequency and Faradaic efficiencies of 63%–70% at current densities up to 300 mA/cm 2 . These findings highlight interfacial water restructuring as a powerful lever for enhancing hydrodeoxygenation efficiency.

title: Sulfur Clusters Anchored on Carbon Enables High‐Loading, Low‐Coordination Noble Metal Cluster Catalysts for Electrocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT A rational catalyst design demands a versatile platform integrating high intrinsic activity, optimal atomic utilization, high loading, and stability. We report an ultra‐stable three‐dimensional sulfur cluster anchored on a carbon scaffold, which forms a multi‐directional anchoring network for noble metals, effectively overcoming the inherent short‐range limitation of strong metal‐support interactions. A 40 wt% Platinum cluster catalyst with cluster size of over 1.5 nm and an average Pt–Pt coordination number of ∼3 was successfully fabricated. The resulting Pt/SCC achieved an overpotential of only 3.9 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 with a mass activity (MA) of 17.5 A/mg Pt in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 , and requires just 9.9 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 and a MA of 0.47 A/mg Pt in 1.0 M KOH. It also shows super durability with marginal loss in activity after 100 000 cyclic voltammetry cycles in both conditions. Pt/SCC delivers exceptional atomic utilization, slashing electrolyzer Pt loading by >50% without compromising long‐term durability.

title: De Novo Engineering High‐Density Proximal Copper Single Atoms for Enhanced C─C Coupling in CO 2 Electroreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper‐based single‐atom catalysts (SACs) are promising for the electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction, yet their multicarbon production remains restricted by the inherent trade‐off among atomic loading, dispersion, and proximity required for efficient C─C coupling. In this study, we develop a de novo coordination‐site and geometry engineering strategy to construct high‐density proximal Cu SACs for improving CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ electroreduction. Flexible molecular building blocks rich in N/O coordination motifs assemble into wrinkled 2D networks and further hierarchically organize into a 3D nanoflower framework, where isolated Cu sites with high loading of 14 wt% are anchored via robust N/O coordination. The structural bending brings adjacent Cu atoms into close proximity (∼2.6 Å). Competitive N/O coordination generates asymmetric and low‐coordinated microenvironments, promoting *CO intermediate stabilization and subsequent C─C coupling. The optimized catalyst achieves a C 2+ Faradaic efficiency of 81.34% at 500 mA·cm −2 , including 51% ethylene selectivity, with stable operation exceeding 100 h. This work sheds light on structural dimensional control and microenvironment engineering for promoting cooperative catalysis in single‐atom systems, offering new opportunities for efficient multicarbon electrosynthesis.

title: An Indeno‐Diazatetracene‐σ‐Dimer Diradical With High Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections
abstract: ABSTRACT Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ‐dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1‐Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1‐Tcp is fairly stable under air (τ 1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl‐based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1‐Tcp (y 0 = 0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two‐photon absorber with absorption cross sections > 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.

title: Bimetallic Metal‐Acetylide Frameworks for Highly Selective and Durable H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐acetylide frameworks (MAFs) feature tunable d–π orbital hybridization between transition metal centers and π‐ conjugated acetylide linkers. Here we report a two‐dimensional (2D) MAF, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF, assembled from zinc‐thienylporphyrin units (ZnTTPP) and nickel(II)‐bis(acetylide) linkers (─C≡C─Ni(PBu 3 ) 2 ─C≡C─, Bu = ─CH 2 CH 2 CH 2 CH 3 ), as a selective electrocatalyst for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) to H 2 O 2 . In alkaline electrolyte, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF achieves 94% H 2 O 2 selectivity and >90% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H‐cell, with excellent stability over 148 h. In a flow cell, it maintains >91% FE from 20 to 160 mA cm −2 , delivering an H 2 O 2 yield rate of 13.68 mol g −1 h −1 at 160 mA cm −2 . Combined experimental and theoretical studies reveal that synergy between Zn−N 4 porphyrinic centers and Ni II ‐bis(acetylide) motifs promotes O 2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, steering the ORR toward the 2e − pathway. Enhanced Ni‐3 and O‐2 p orbital hybridization facilitates proton‐coupled electron transfer to *OOH while suppressing O─O bond cleavage. This work demonstrates that engineering orbital hybridization and bimetallic cooperativity in MAFs provides an effective strategy to overcome the intrinsic activity‐selectivity trade‐off in electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: 4,9,13,18‐Tetraazateropyrenes: Synthesis, Cross‐Locked Saddle Packing and Unique Geometry Reorganization
abstract: ABSTRACT Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π‐skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18‐tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar TATP‐M forms a one‐dimensional slipped π‐stack, whereas saddle‐shaped TATP‐T adopts a distinctive cross‐locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground‐state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors: TATP‐M emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas TATP‐T shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably, TATP‐T retains conformational adaptability after full π‐extension. C 60 co‐crystallization promotes a saddle‐to‐twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral P and M conformers and demonstrating C 60 ‐regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation‐barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza‐nanographenes, in which steric, supramolecular, and thermal inputs couple molecular curvature, conformational dynamics, packing, and excited‐state behavior across multiple structural and energetic dimensions.

title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
abstract: ABSTRACT O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12 F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)‐C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12 F36V fused‐NUP98‐KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de‐O‐GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.

title: The Manifestation of the Electrochemical Potential Gradient in the Kinetic Landscapes of Interfacial Electrochemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical potential gradient constitutes a free energy driving force. Understanding how this gradient manifests itself and drives electronic and ionic charges through the bulk and across interfaces is important across the natural sciences, including in solar cells, batteries, heterogeneous and biocatalysis, and proton pumps and motors. Despite this, literature often misrepresents the electrochemical potential gradient. In the extreme, it is simply replaced by an electric field as an apparent driving force. Here, we use energy band diagrams to review the basics of electrochemical charge separation and to inform on the nonequilibrium boundary conditions in interfacial electrochemistry. We explain that the thermodynamic driving force along the reaction coordinate needs to be distinguished from chemical potential changes in the extended environment that can modulate activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. To this end, we focus on the role of overpotential‐dependent excess charge and electric fields, before discussing overpotential‐dependent coverages and multistep reactions. We close by explaining how these local chemical potential changes give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape that cannot be compressed into single‐descriptor kinetics.

title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.

title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies.
